## Introduction

Going forward, new issues in the new template at the bottom of this file, will go in the '## New format' section only. No more status emojis. Refer to '## Reference' for sort order. Issues in the old format (with status emojis) won't be refactored, but will continue to be worked until moved to closed, canceled, or deferred sections, and emojis updated. (Eventually this will all be moved to nano-git-db anyway. This new template is an intermediate effort to make issues going forward more structured and importable.)

This is the product backlog, until bugs, features, and enhancements move to GitHub Issues.

## Issues

- The warning for a submodule that is behind names no way to commit a move back made on purpose
	- ID: 2026112118464455
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261121-184644
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026112112175066, 2026112118463121
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: With a submodule level with origin, move it back on purpose with `git -C <submodule> checkout HEAD~1`, then run `gitsby pullcom`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The submodule is left out and the run says Nothing to commit. The warning names only `git submodule update`, which undoes the move. It also says the commit would have undone "that move", though no pull moved anything.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The submodule is still left out, since a checkout a pull left behind and a move back look the same. The warning also says how to record the older commit: `git add <folder>`, then the same command with `--staged`. Its wording fits both cases.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-21 on b23. `git add child`, then `gitsby -q pullcom --staged`, commits the move back.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The warning in cmdCommit (mutate.go) was written for the pull case only.
	- Decisions: Answered 2026-11-21: keep leaving it out, and name the way through. Committing a move back without a word is the High bug 2026112112175066 fixed, and the two cases can't be told apart once a run has ended. Goes with 2026112118463121, at the same site.
		- The add names the folder by its full path, quoted as other Fix lines are, so it works from any folder. The first sentence of the warning is kept, so [dfkzy] still holds.
	- Origin: 2cdbb74, the fix of 2026112112175066. Confirmed. Found while answering its Check: entry.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The warning was written for the pull case. It named only 'git submodule update', which undoes a move back made on purpose, and said the commit would have undone 'that move'.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The warning says a pull or switch leaves a submodule that way, and that committing it would take the branch back to the older commit. A Fix note names 'git submodule update', or 'git add' with the folder and then the same command with --staged. repo create and repo connect don't take --staged, so theirs names 'git commit' and a rerun. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfnay] and [dfnb0]. Go [dfnav] TestBehindFixNamesStaged.
	- Verified: [dfnay] and [dfnb0] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it. [dfnav] fails with --staged dropped from the rerun line, and with repo create and connect given it. The quick gate with every area passed: test.bash 2366/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec 37, as before.
	- Swept: behindGitlinks has one caller, cmdCommit, so the warning is the one site. [dfnav] covers every command stagesTree names, and checks that its rerun line parses with --staged.
	- Branch: nov22-2026112118464455
	- Commit: 61e6604
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the advice is the one the answer named.
	- Closed: 20261122-115204

- With submodule.recurse set, the pull no longer updates submodules
	- ID: 2026112118463121
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261121-184631
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026112112175066
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: In a clone with a submodule, run `git config submodule.recurse true`. Have origin's dev move the submodule to a newer commit, then run `gitsby -q pullcom` on dev.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The submodule's checkout stays on the old commit, and the run warns that it was left out of the commit. The warning comes back on every run until `git submodule update` is run by hand. Plain `git pull --ff-only` with that setting updates the checkout, and so did v2.1.0, which ran `git pull`. `br switch` still updates it, through `git checkout`.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: With `submodule.recurse` true, each merge that stands in for a pull is followed by `git submodule update --recursive --checkout`, as `git pull` does, and the plan lists it. A failed update warns and the run goes on, since the commit already leaves out a submodule that is behind. Without the setting nothing changes, and a repo with no `.gitmodules` costs no extra process.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-21 on b23, git 2.51, local bare repos. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: f61adb6 made the pull step a `git merge --ff-only`, and `git merge` never reads `submodule.recurse`. Only an upstream on another remote still runs `git pull`.
	- Decisions: Answered 2026-11-21: follow the setting, rather than always update or never update. The setting is the user's own request for it, so the detached checkout is what plain git already gives them, and gitsby then agrees with `git pull`, v2.1.0 and its own `br switch`. Without the setting the checkout is left alone, per 2026112112175066.
		- With the setting, the update also checks out the recorded commit for a submodule moved back on purpose and not staged, as git pull does. A staged move back is kept, since the update reads the index ([dfnb0]). A failed update exited 128 on git 2.51, so [dfnaz] checks the text rather than the code.
	- Origin: f61adb6, Go port. Confirmed. Found while answering the Check: entry of 2026112112175066.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: f61adb6 made the pull a 'git merge --ff-only', and git merge never reads submodule.recurse, so the update git pull runs after its merge with that setting never ran.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: pullStep in mutate.go, which cmdPull and pullIfOnline call, follows the merge with 'git submodule update --recursive --checkout' when submodule.recurse is true. The setting is read once a run, and only where the work tree has a .gitmodules. planPull in preview.go lists the update under each pull in the plan. A failed update warns with its exit code and the run goes on. An upstream on another remote still runs git pull, which updates by itself. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfnaw], [dfnax], [dfnaz] and [dfnb0].
	- Verified: all 4 fail on the build before the fix and pass with it. git pull --ff-only with the setting updates a submodule even when already up to date, so the update runs after every merge. The quick gate with every area passed: test.bash 2366/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec 37, as before.
	- Swept: pullArgs is called only from pullStep, which covers cmdPull and every pullIfOnline caller (br switch, br create, br hotfix, br merge, release, pr ok). Every pull line in the plan goes through planPull, 10 sites. The other merges, br merge's --no-ff, the hotfix back-merge and release's, aren't pulls, and plain git merge leaves submodules alone there too.
	- Branch: nov22-2026112118464455
	- Commit: 61e6604
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261122-115204

- pr ok takes the PR's target from its head's name, not the base the git host gives it
	- ID: 2026112113223086
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Queued
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261121-132230
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026112017135624
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Open a PR from hotfix/x against dev on the git host's web page, then run `gitsby -q pr ok <n>`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The git host merges it into dev. pr ok then reads the head as a hotfix, checks out and pulls main, and back-merges main into dev at exit 0, though the fix never reached main. A plain branch's PR opened against main merges there, and pr ok checks out dev and skips the back-merge.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: pr ok takes the target and the back-merge from the base the PR has, or refuses before the plan when the base isn't the one its head's name gives.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: readPr asks gh, tea and glab for the head and state only. prTarget in pr.go reads the target off the head's name.
	- Origin: 4918b5b, Go port. Plausible. Found while fixing 2026112017135624, whose pr create now opens every PR on the base pr ok expects, so only a PR opened elsewhere is left.

- Code Review 20261120 item 26: install.ps1 picks a different release than install.bash when a tag has a dot suffix or 4 numbers
	- ID: 2026112017135503
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Queued
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261120-171355
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Feed both installers the same release list, with v3.1.0.rc1 as a pre-release, v3.0.0 and v3.0.0-rc.1, and run `-Release dev`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: install.ps1 takes v3.0.0 and install.bash takes v3.1.0.rc1. Over v3.0.0 and v3.0.0.1, install.ps1 takes the candidate over its own release.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Both follow design.md:458. A full release ranks above pre-releases of its own version, and a dot suffix is a candidate.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on vm925w in 5.1 and 7, and in pwsh on b23 with stubs. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: install.ps1:247 strips only a `-` or `+` suffix, so `[version]` fails on 3.1.0.rc1 and reads 3.0.0.1 as newer than 3.0.0.
	- Origin: 4ccd133 (2026-10-03). `-Release dev` (7c6a66a, 2026112015351403) now reaches it. Missed twin of 2026111920273377, whose Swept row left the installers out.

- Code Review 20261120 item 32: install.ps1 may count an unexpanded %VAR% PATH entry as present
	- ID: 2026112017135414
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Queued
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261120-171354
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: On Windows, put `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\gitsby` in a user PATH stored as plain REG_SZ, then run install.ps1.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: Test-OnPath expands the entry, finds the folder and writes nothing. Windows doesn't expand %VAR% in a REG_SZ value, so the entry doesn't work.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: An entry counts as present only where Windows expands it.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: No. Read only. vm925w's user PATH was checked as REG_SZ on 2026-11-20. Plausible.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: install.ps1:298-306 expands every entry, the ones from `$env:PATH` included.
	- Against: Code Review 20261119 item 34's fix, which expands %VAR% entries.
	- Origin: 808235d, 2856951 and fb6ae4c (Code Review 20261119 item 34).

- Code Review 20261120 item 33: raw git acts as the wrong account when a drive-relative -C follows another -C
	- ID: 2026112017135400
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Queued
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261120-171354
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: On Windows in w\c\top, run `gitsby raw git -C .. -C C:foo config --get user.email`. Do the same with `-C .. -C \Users\<you>\w\c\top\foo`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: git runs in the folder the options name, but raw acts as the starting folder's account, and git gets that email. A single drive-relative -C matches git.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: raw acts as the account of the folder git runs in, per design.md:381.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on vm925w in Git Bash. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: joinDir at main.go:1108 uses filepath.IsAbs, so C:foo and \foo are joined onto the earlier folder, and the chdir fails.
	- Origin: 12f1bc2, nov18, Code Review 20261110b item 7. Missed twin for Windows.

- `raw gh` loops forever when `gh` on PATH leads back to gitsby
	- ID: 2026101916533300
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Needs local test suite run?: No. test.bash ran 1597/0.
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Critical
	- Opened: 20261019-165333
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Prereq IDs: 2026102306584122
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: b28l
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]:
		- On a box where the first `gh` on PATH is, or runs, gitsby, run `gitsby raw gh <anything>`.
		- Not confirmed which form b28l had: a symlink or copy of gitsby named `gh`, or a wrapper script that calls `gitsby raw gh "$@"`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]:
		- Endless loop that eats time and a lot of memory. The session that hit it got out by calling the real `gh` by full path.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]:
		- Stop at once with a plain error that names the PATH entry, and never start a second copy of itself.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-10-21 on b23, with stand-ins on PATH. A wrapper `gh` that runs `gitsby raw gh "$@"` started itself until its counter stopped it at 20. A link named `gh` to the build ran gitsby as gh, which answered "Unknown command 'auth'". The link alone doesn't loop, since gitsby doesn't read its own name, so b28l most likely had a wrapper.
	- Possible cause [Bug]:
		- `cmdPassthrough` in main.go checks `gh` only with `mustBeInPath`, then `handover` in exec.go runs it by bare name. Nothing checks that the file found isn't gitsby itself, or something that calls it. A wrapper makes each run start the next, with no limit.
	- Requirements [Bug fix]:
		- Find the tool by walking PATH ourselves. Skip any entry that resolves (symlinks followed, `os.SameFile`) to the running gitsby. If nothing else is left, refuse with the usual "Not found in path" error and say a PATH entry points back at gitsby.
		- Set an env var such as `GITSBY_RAW_ACTIVE` on the handover. If it's already set when `raw` starts, refuse with a message that names it. This catches wrappers the file check can't see. Read it at startup, before the run sets it.
		- Cover `tea`, `glab`, `lazygit`, and `tig` the same way, since they share the path.
		- Test case needs a stand-in `gh` that is a wrapper and one that is a symlink to the build. Watch both fail on the current build first, and put a spawn limit on the test so a regression can't eat the box.
	- Progress log:
		- 2026-10-19: Logged from a report by another project's session on b28l. Cause is from reading the code, not from a run there. Still need the output of `type -a gh` on b28l.
		- 2026-10-21: Fixed as the requirements ask. `raw` walks PATH itself, through `exec.LookPath` on each entry, and passes over an entry that is the running binary. It sets `GITSBY_RAW_ACTIVE` to the tool's path before anything runs the tool, the tea probes and the account's gh calls included, and a `raw` that finds it set at startup refuses and names it. The hermetic suites unset it.
		- 2026-10-22: The guard refused every nested `raw`, hooks and aliases included. `GITSBY_RAW_ACTIVE` is now the chain of `raw` runs above, one short entry each, and a `raw` refuses only to start one already on it. While `raw` runs tools only to check them, such as the tea and gh probes, the chain ends in a probe mark, and a `raw` started under that refuses. A loop with new arguments each time stops at 16 deep.
		- 2026-10-23: The b28l session was tukzedo's. Its memory.md says a `gh` wrapper running `exec gitsby raw gh "$@"` grew to about 15,000 processes and 56 GB in 28 minutes on 2026-10-19. Tried that wrapper on b23 against the gover build: no loop, 2 or 3 starts and a refusal. The old build loops in every case until the rig's cap. The wrapper still fails, and so do gitsby's own gh calls behind it, filed as 2026102306584122. A wrapper that clears the environment still loops, filed as 2026102306584127. Rig: `private/claude_simple/tools/rawloop-rig.bash`.
	- Actual cause [Bug]:
		- As the possible cause says. `raw` ran the tool by bare name and never asked what it found. Every run through a wrapper started the next.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: `lookTool` in exec.go, used by `cmdPassthrough` for all six tools, and `rawActive` read in `newApp`. The tool still sees its own name as argv[0]. design.md's `raw` bullets say so. Since 2026-10-22, `rawNest` in exec.go builds and checks the chain.
	- Decisions:
		- With no other copy left, the refusal is "Not found in path: gh. '<entry>' is gitsby itself.", with the entry as found.
		- A gitsby entry ahead of a real tool is passed over without a word.
		- A plain copy of gitsby named `gh` isn't the same file, so only the env check stops it, on its second start.
		- 2026-10-22, from the answer "What any sane human git user would expect": whatever nesting plain git allows works the same under gitsby, with no refusal and nothing added to the output. That covers hooks under `raw git commit` or `push`, git aliases, lazygit and tig custom commands, and scripts. A loop gitsby causes still stops at once and names what looped.
		- An entry is the tool's name and a 12-digit hash of its path, the folder and the arguments. The folder is in it so a hook that runs the same command in a submodule isn't taken for a loop. Refusing on the same tool file alone was rejected, since it refuses `raw git` under `raw git`.
		- A `raw` started by one of gitsby's own checks of a tool is refused, since nothing a check runs has a reason to call `raw`. Without that, the tea wrapper check `[de89c]` failed, since the `--version` and `logins list` probes each started a nested `raw`.
		- The depth limit is 16. Plain git would loop forever there.
	- Branch: round-20261021, then round-20261022
	- Test case: test.bash `[de897]`, `[de898]`, `[de899]` and `[de89a]` for gh, and `[de89b]` and `[de89c]` for tea, glab, lazygit and tig, as a link and as a wrapper each. Each wrapper quits after 5 starts. Go `[de89d]` for the PATH walk and `[de89e]` for the refusal, reworded 2026-10-22 to a repeat on the chain. Since then test.bash `[de8pg]` and `[de8ph]` for a pre-commit hook running `raw git` under `raw git commit`, `[de8pj]` for an alias doing the same, and Go `[de8pk]` for the chain and the probe mark and `[de8pm]` for the depth limit.
	- Verified: All 12 new test.bash checks fail on the build before the fix, with the other 1579 passing. The 5 with only the link on PATH were rerun outside the suite with the same command and pattern, and fail there too. After it, test.bash 1579 -> 1591, 0 failed. Both Go tests fail with the self check and the env check taken out. `GOOS=windows go vet` and darwin and freebsd builds pass. The wrapper stand-in started once, then refused.
	- Verified: 2026-10-21, stage 7 passed on every box. test.bash 1368/0 on b26 and 1271/0 on vmFreeBSD, each 15 more than on 10-19, all from this round, and 1579/0 on vmDebARM64, 23 more, with leakflags' 8. All 12 of this item's test.bash checks ran on each. The Go tests passed there and on vm925w, where `[de89d]` skips, since it needs symlinks and the exec bit, and `[de89e]` passed.
	- Verified: 2026-10-22, test.bash 1594 -> 1597, 0 failed, with the reworded `[de899]` and `[de89c]`. On the build before, the 3 new checks fail. The Go tests fail with each part of `rawNest` taken out in turn: the repeat check, the probe mark, the depth limit, the folder and the separator between arguments. Outside the suite, a wrapper `gh` started once and was refused, and one adding an argument each time stopped at 16. `GOOS=windows go vet` and the Windows test build, and darwin and freebsd builds, pass.
	- Verified: 2026-10-22, stage 7 passed on every box for the nesting change. test.bash 1371/0 on b26 and 1274/0 on vmFreeBSD, each 3 more than on 10-21, which are `[de8pg]`, `[de8ph]` and `[de8pj]`. 1583/0 on vmDebARM64, 4 more, those 3 plus `[de8q2]`, which sits in the Linux-only pre-push gate block. `[de8pk]` and `[de8pm]` passed in the Go tests on b26, vmFreeBSD, vmDebARM64 natively and under Wine, and vm925w, where the Go tests were 191 ok and 23 skipped, 2 more ok than on 10-21. `[de89e]` passed there too. Log: `/mnt/ext/wip2/wip/tmp/test_gitsby_20261021-19403500/run1.log`.
	- Verified: 2026-10-23 on b28l, the box that hit it, on the synced build `c917c95`, which has this fix and 2026102306584122's. In tukzedo-linux's repo there, with tukzedo's wrapper `exec gitsby raw gh "$@"` first on PATH and the real `gh` 2.46.0 behind it, each start counted and capped at 20: `gitsby raw gh auth status`, a bare `gh auth status`, `gh repo view`, a script calling `gh api user`, `gitsby whoami`, `gitsby --no-fetch pr` and `gitsby -q raw gh api rate_limit` all reached the real `gh` as t00mietum and exited 0. 2 to 9 wrapper starts each, with no gitsby left running. The control, the same wrapper with `9e82970` first on PATH as `gitsby`, ran into the cap on both forms tried.
	- Verified: 2026-10-24 on b23, gover `c87c131`, with the rig. The wrapper reached the stand-in `gh` with 2 starts for `raw gh`, 3 for a bare `gh` or a script, and 6 for `whoami` and `pr`. A link or copy named `gh` is refused by name since 2026102306584132. A wrapper adding an argument each time stopped at 17 deep after 32 starts. No gitsby was left running.
	- Swept: every `raw` tool shares `cmdPassthrough`, git included. 2026-10-22: `rawActive` has one reader, `cmdPassthrough`, and the variable is unset in all 4 hermetic suites. Other commands still run gh and tea by bare name, so a gh link to gitsby gives a confusing error there; logged as 2026102111572785. Not a loop, since only `raw` hands over.

	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261121-121750
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Clone a repo with a submodule. Have origin's dev move the submodule to a newer commit, then run `gitsby -q pullcom` on dev.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The pull moves the gitlink, but the submodule's own checkout stays where it was. `git add --all` then stages the old commit, and pullcom commits it, undoing origin's bump. The next sync pushes that.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A gitlink the pull just moved isn't committed back. The submodule is updated, or left for the user with a note.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-21 on b23, git 2.51, local bare repos. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: cmdPull merges with no submodule update, and cmdCommit stages a submodule moved off its gitlink as new work, per 2026111016332293.
	- Origin: Go port. Found while working 2026112017151559. No round saw it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: A pull or switch moves the gitlink but not the submodule's checkout. git add --all then staged the old commit as a submodule move, and the commit took it. The checks made before staging read the same entry from status as work, so br switch refused to leave dev and sync on dev called it a direct push.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: After git add --all, cmdCommit reads the staged changes with --raw, in the spawn the index check already cost, and unstages any submodule checked out on an ancestor of the commit HEAD records, or lacking that commit. It warns, names the folder on a File: line, and names 'git submodule update'. treeDirty reads status v2 and skips the same case. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfkzx] to [dfkzz], [dfm00], [dfm01], [dfm09] to [dfm0b].
	- Verified: [dfm00], [dfkzx], [dfkzy] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it. [dfkzz] passed there before its bump condition was added, which is unverified on that build. [dfm09] and [dfm0a] fail with only the commit fixed and pass with treeDirty fixed. [dfm01] and [dfm0b] pass on both, as guards. [dfh4h] fails on a git status call without --untracked-files after its pattern was widened to see '-c' options. The quick gate with every area passed: test.bash 2358/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0, spawn counts. gosec 37, as before.
	- Swept: git add runs only in cmdCommit. Every pre-staging check goes through treeDirty: commitPending (directPush, releasePreflight), br switch's dirty refusal and pr ok's refusal. pr ok's isn't run here, since it needs a git host. The plan's status block still lists the submodule, as it does a dirty one.
	- Decisions: Left out with a warning rather than updated, since the submodule's checkout is its own, an update detaches a branch checked out there, and it may need a fetch the run already saw fail. git merge ignores submodule.recurse, so that setting isn't honored either. A move forward or sideways is still committed, since it may be the user's. A submodule lacking the recorded commit counts as behind: work built on that commit would contain it. The unstage shows as a step though the plan can't list it. treeDirty passes -c status.relativePaths=false, since v2 paths follow it, and [dfh4h]'s pattern now sees calls with -c options. Check answered 2026-11-21: leaving it out stays the default, as plain git leaves a submodule alone after a pull. With submodule.recurse set, `git pull` and v2.1.0 update it, so the pull follows that setting in 2026112118463121. The warning names how to commit a move back made on purpose in 2026112118464455.

- Code Review 20261120 item 1: With diff.relative or a textconv driver, an autostash conflict is committed and pushed
	- ID: 2026112017135886
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261120-171358
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Set `diff.relative=true`. Edit a file that origin's branch also changed, and a file in `sub/`. From `sub/`, run `gitsby -q sync -m work`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The autostash restore conflicts, the conflict check sees nothing, and the conflict markers are committed and pushed at exit 0. From `sub/`, pullcom says "Nothing to commit." while an edit outside the folder stays staged, and br switch takes that edit to dev. A textconv driver whose output doesn't change hides an edit the same way.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The conflict check and the commit decision see the whole repo, whatever the diff settings.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, git 2.51, with controls that don't have the setting. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The decisions read plain `git diff`, which follows diff config: mutate.go:155, :33, :43 and :745, and release.go:154.
	- Sweep: staged.go:66 changedPaths, refuseSparseAdd, branchcmd.go:429 and show.go:111.
	- Origin: cfb6d90 (Go port) and 9f53a91 (--staged). No round saw it. Same class as Code Review 20261119 item 2, whose sweep covered git status only.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Every git diff gitsby read for a decision followed the user's diff config. diff.relative cut it to the folder gitsby ran from, and a textconv driver whose output didn't change made 'diff --cached --quiet' say the index matched HEAD.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: One helper, diffArgs in mutate.go, starts every git diff with --no-relative, --no-textconv, --no-ext-diff and --ignore-submodules=none. The conflict check, the commit decisions, the --staged checks, the hotfix note and the incoming list all go through it.
	- Test case: Go [dfjwf] TestDiffReadsIgnoreDiffConfig, [dfjwh] TestDiffReadsSeeSubmoduleMove and [dfjwg] TestDiffReadsUseDiffArgs; test.bash [dfjwj] to [dfjwn] and [dfjwp].
	- Verified: [dfjwj], [dfjwk], [dfjwm], [dfjwn] and [dfjwp] fail on the build before the fix (test.bash 2235/5) and pass with it. [dfjwf] fails with --no-relative dropped, or with both --no-textconv and --no-ext-diff dropped. [dfjwh] fails with --ignore-submodules=none dropped, or put after the caller's options. The quick gate with every area passed: test.bash 2240/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec 37, as before.
	- Swept: every git diff in src-go, by grep for '"git", "diff"' and '[]string{"diff"': cmdCommit (2), refuseConflicts and commitPending in mutate.go, releasePreflight, changedPaths (which refuseSparseAdd and stagedPreflight use), warnHotfixTouchedCode and showIncoming. [dfjwg] fails on any new one. Read only, left alone: the 3 git diff reads in cicd.bash and release.bash run from the repo root and list names, which a textconv driver doesn't change.
	- Decisions: Flags on one helper rather than plumbing. diff-index needs a HEAD, which a new repo doesn't have, and ls-files lists only the current folder unless given ':/', so each site would need its own guard. --no-relative needs git 2.28 by its release notes (not run on an older git), one release past the 2.27 that pull --autostash on a merge already needs. --ignore-submodules=none goes past the item's list, since diff.ignoreSubmodules=all hid a submodule move that add stages and git commit takes, and design.md counts a moved submodule as work. On git 2.51 either --no-textconv or --no-ext-diff alone clears the textconv case; both stay.

	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.

- Code Review 20261119 item 1: sync, br switch and br create push to origin's main when the branch tracks origin/main
	- ID: 2026111910223293
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261119-102232
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026111016332392
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: git switch -c feat origin/main, commit, then gitsby -q sync.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It pushes HEAD to origin's main and exits 0. The plan says it pushes feat, and --direct never asks. br switch and br create park the same way.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A push goes where a bare push would send it, which under push.default=simple is a refusal, per item 2026111016332392's decision. A push that would reach a protected branch asks for --direct.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23. d5e76f2 refused. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: pushDest falls back to the upstream's ref. directPush judges the current branch's name, not the push's target.
	- Origin: 6e3ab95, round-20261111 (Code Review 20261110b item 5), and bb905b6, nov18. Regression of item 5.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: pushDest sent a branch whose upstream has another name to the upstream's ref whatever push.default said, so it did what push.default=upstream does where git's default refuses. directPush judged the current branch's name, so a push from feat to main never asked for --direct.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: pushDest follows push.default where the upstream on the push's remote has another name: simple refuses, upstream and nothing go to the upstream, current and matching to the branch's own name. sync, br switch, br create, br hotfix, br merge and pr create refuse before the plan where git would refuse the push, naming 'git branch --unset-upstream'. directPush judges where the push lands, so sync and br switch ask for --direct for a push to main from feat. The other 4 refuse it, naming 'sync --direct'. The sync plan line names the target when it differs. Any other push of the current branch refuses at the step. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Branch: nov19b-2026111910223293
	- Commit: ca1f916
	- Test case: test.bash [dfh3s] to [dfh40]; Go TestPushArgs [df52f] with 8 new cases.
	- Verified: [dfh3s] to [dfh40] fail on the build before the fix, all but [dfh3z], which passes on both since --direct pushed to main before too. All 8 pass with the fix. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2096/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0, spawn counts [df37w] 38 and [df052] 43, as before. gosec reports the same 32 hits, none in the changed files.
	- Swept: every push of the current branch goes through pushArgs: the park push of sync, br switch, br create, br hotfix, br merge, pr create and release, br merge's push of the target, release's 2 pushes, repo connect's push. The park pushes refuse before the plan, the rest at the step. Every other isProtectedBranch("") caller is about committing on or deleting a protected branch, not where a push lands, and was left alone. publishBranch and every first publish push to the branch's own name. release stays out of --direct, per 2026111016332380.
	- Against: 2026111016332392's Decisions. Its Go case for an upstream of another name expected a push there under the default push.default, and now expects a refusal, as this item asks. Its call for push.default=nothing, the upstream, stands.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261119-115700
	- Decisions:
		- simple refuses before the plan, under -q or not, since git would refuse the push only after the commit. That covers push.default unset, and a value git doesn't know, which git refuses too. The way off is 'git branch --unset-upstream', as for a gone branch, so the next push publishes it under its own name.
		- A push remote other than the upstream's still gets the branch under its own name, as before.
		- br create, br hotfix, br merge and pr create refuse a park push that lands on a protected branch, naming 'sync --direct', rather than take --direct. That keeps 2026111016332380's line that they never push a protected branch, and leaves --direct's command list as it is. Check: entry filed. Answered 2026-11-19: the call stands.
		- The refusals are asked only when something would go, since a branch made from origin/main and never touched has nothing to push.
		- Spawn counts are unchanged: branchRefs's one for-each-ref also reads the push fields and the current branch, and pushDest reads it in place of its own call. push.default is read only for a branch whose upstream has another name.
		- 20261119: TestPushArgs [df52f]'s 'upstream by another name' case now expects a refusal, where it expected HEAD:refs/heads/up. The rest of the test is as it was.

- Code Review 20261119 item 3: A pending am, range pick or resolved merge is finished or left behind by gitsby
	- ID: 2026111910223262
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261119-102232
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Stop a range cherry-pick or a git am partway, then run gitsby -q br switch dev, sync or pullcom.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: gitsby commits the half-done work under its own message, switches, exits 0, and leaves the sequencer. A later --continue applies the rest onto dev. br merge finishes a resolved merge of the user's.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Refuse before the plan, naming the operation and its --continue or --abort.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23, 5 cases. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: Nothing checks MERGE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, REVERT_HEAD, sequencer or rebase-apply. git's own refusal runs only when a pull does.
	- Origin: 4918b5b, Go port. The bash build had no guard either. No round reached it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Nothing read the files git keeps while an operation is stopped: MERGE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, REVERT_HEAD, sequencer, rebase-apply, rebase-merge and BISECT_LOG. Only a stopped rebase, or a bisect with checkout, was refused, and as a detached HEAD.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The branch commands, pr create, pr ok and release refuse before the fetch and the plan while git has one stopped. The refusal names it and its --continue and --abort, or git bisect reset. The paths come from git rev-parse --git-path in the rev-parse call every run already makes, so no spawn was added. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Branch: nov19b-2026111910223262
	- Commit: d1f0d4e
	- Test case: test.bash [dfh54] to [dfh5d]. Go test [dfh53] TestPendingOpNamed.
	- Verified: [dfh54] to [dfh5c] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it, and [dfh5d] passes on both. [dfh53] fails with the guard turned off, and its hand-committed pick and revert cases fail without the sequencer check. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2111/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0, spawn counts unchanged.
	- Swept: every mutating command. pullcom, sync, br create, br hotfix, br switch, br merge, br prune, pr create, pr ok and release go through the one check in run. status, whoami, br list and pr view only read. git's own refusal on a pull and backOutMerge's MERGE_HEAD check after a merge step are unchanged.
	- Decisions: A bisect refuses too, with checkout or without, since git status calls it in progress and git bisect reset moves HEAD back. The repo and account commands don't check, since none commits onto existing history or switches. A rebase is named ahead of a merge or pick it stopped on, since the rebase is what has to be finished.
	- Note: gosec reports 2 new findings in pendingOp, for os.Lstat and os.ReadFile of paths git rev-parse gave. Both are in the user's own repo, the same kind as the earlier false positives. CodeQL wasn't run.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261119-123039

	- Origin: 08e7452, 2026-11-08. Round-20261111 (2026111016332429) kept the helper on purpose but didn't try differing hosts. Same class as Code Review 20261110b item 1.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Every matching fragment's helper stays in git's list, and each reads the token file key the innermost fragment sets, which said nothing about its host. The same key let gitsby's own runs hand a Gitea token to github.com through the gitsby.ghTokenFile fallback, when a run named a bare GitHub login in a Gitea account's folder.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: Each fragment writes gitsby.host, its account's host, and the helper answers only when git asks about that host. The gitsby.ghTokenFile fallback checks it too. Both go through one host check, sameService in githost.go, which every token hand-over now uses.
	- Decisions:
		- A host key beside the token file, rather than a token key per host, so gitsby.ghTokenFile keeps its name and meaning, and every account sets it, so the innermost one's wins with nothing put back.
		- The helper reads gitsby.host from the global scope with includes, where it reads the token file, so a repo's own config can't claim a host.
		- No gitsby.host means the helper answers nothing, since every apply writes it. The fallback reads an unset key as GitHub's, its meaning before fragments, so a hand-set gitsby.ghTokenFile keeps working.
		- A fragment from an older apply keeps the old helper until account apply runs again. The changelog says so.
		- The host is compared in lower case, with the port if git gives one. A remote spelled with another port gets nothing, never the wrong token.
	- Branch: nov19b-2026111910223247
	- Commit: 22554f6
	- Test case: test.bash [dfh5s] and [dfh5t], which walk every path that hands out a token, pointed at another host and then at its own. Go [dfh5x] for the helper's host check.
	- Verified: on the unfixed build, [dfh5s] fails for 9 of its 10 paths (test.bash 2120/9) and passes after (2129/0). Its glab path passes both ways, and [dfh5t] passes both ways. With the helper's host line taken out, [dfh5x] fails and plain git in the nested folder gives the inner token again. With the fallback's check taken out, raw git with GITSBY_ACCOUNT naming a login gives the Gitea token again. Quick gate passed, all areas: test.bash 2129/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. Not run on Windows, where the helper's tr and character class run under Git for Windows' sh.
	- Swept: every path that hands out a token. Plain git's fragment helper, gitsby's own helper (scoped by its key), raw git, tig and lazygit through it, raw gh and gitsby's own gh calls (item 5), raw glab and pr's glab through tokenElsewhere, raw tea (keeps its token on GITEA_INSTANCE_URL), and the gitsby.ghTokenFile fallback. accountServesHost uses sameService too.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after.

- Code Review 20261119 item 5: raw gh hands the Enterprise token to any other host
	- ID: 2026111910223233
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261119-102232
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026111016332206
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: With GH_HOST on an Enterprise host whose account has a token, run gitsby raw gh auth token --hostname evil.example.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: gh prints the account's token. gh applies GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN to every host but github.com.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: No token for a raw gh that names another host, as glabTokenEnv does for glab.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23, real gh 2.96 and a fake token. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: tokenEnvVar exports the variable without checking the host gh is pointed at.
	- Origin: d5d8cfa, nov19 (2026111016332206). Regression: it moved the leak from github.com to other hosts. Same class as Code Review 20261110b item 1.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: selectAccount put the token in gh's own variable on every run. gh sends GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN to every Enterprise host, and GH_TOKEN to github.com, github.localhost and every *.ghe.com host, whatever host a command names. So a github.com token went to a ghe.com tenant the same way.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: selectAccount puts the token in gh's variable only when tokenElsewhere finds no other host among raw gh's --hostname, -h, -R, URL and repo arguments (ghNamedHosts) and the caller's GH_HOST and GH_REPO. git's helper reads GITSBY_HOST_TOKEN on every host, so git still gets the token. raw gh says when it isn't acting as the account, as raw glab does.
	- Decisions:
		- Refuse, with no pin. gh takes remotes only from the host GH_HOST names (checked with gh 2.96), and an Enterprise account's host is always that one. Left alone: a github.com account in a repo with a second remote on a *.ghe.com host gh is logged in to, which gh might pick with no host named.
		- A caller's GH_HOST on another host counts as pointing gh there, for gitsby's own gh calls too. gh then finds no remote on the account's host anyway, so nothing that worked stops.
		- The first of 3 parts in a -R is a host, as gh reads it. A bare argument counts only with a dot in it, as for glab, since repo clone takes a folder there.
		- Too many hosts means no token, never a token sent astray: -h counts as a host everywhere, though only gh's auth commands take it as one.
	- Against: 2026111016332206's fix, where the helper read gh's variable so git and gh agree. They still get the same token whenever gh gets one. design.md says so.
	- Branch: nov19b-2026111910223247
	- Commit: 22554f6
	- Test case: test.bash [dfh5s] and [dfh5t] (shared with item 4), Go [dfh5v] for the hosts a gh command line names, [dfh5w] for which runs keep the token from gh.
	- Verified: real gh 2.96 through the built gitsby, with a fake token. With GH_HOST on the Enterprise host, raw gh auth token --hostname evil.example printed the token before, and after prints 'no oauth token found' under the 'not acting as the account' line, while the same with no --hostname still prints it. From a github.com account, --hostname acme.ghe.com and github.localhost printed the token before and don't after. [dfh5s]'s 6 gh paths fail on the unfixed build and pass after. Quick gate passed, all areas: test.bash 2129/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0.
	- Swept: gh's own variables, set only in selectAccount. raw gh, and gitsby's own gh calls (pr, repo create, repo view, the token check), all after it. glab through the same tokenElsewhere. tea and git are scoped to the host already, per item 4's Swept.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Closed: 20261119-125820
	- Progress log:
		- 2026-11-19: gosec on src-go went from 34 findings to 37, all false positives. G101 on the GITSBY_HOST_TOKEN name, and G703 in readTokenFile and worldReadable, whose taint now comes through the account struct holding raw gh's arguments.

- Code Review 20261119 item 6: On Windows, a folder rule through a junction never matches
	- ID: 2026111910223218
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261119-102232
	- Opened by:
	- Target OS: Windows
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Make a junction to a folder holding a repo, write a path rule that names the junction, and run gitsby account from the repo either way.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: No account matches. account apply writes the junction path, so plain git gets no identity either. A symlink works.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A junction resolves like a symlink, as the comment in canonPath says and v2.1.0 did.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on vm925w. GODEBUG=winsymlink=0 makes it match. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: Go 1.23 and later no longer resolve mount points in EvalSymlinks.
	- Origin: d476da9, 2026-08-17. No round reached it. No Go test makes a junction.
	- Closed reason [Closed]: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Go 1.23 made EvalSymlinks leave mount points as written, and a junction is one. resolveLinks leans on EvalSymlinks, so a rule through a junction kept the junction path while git answered with the real one.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: go.mod sets winsymlink=0 and winreadlinkvolume=0, the pre-1.23 reading. A junction resolves like a symlink again, in canonPath and in the gitdir rule account apply writes. A comment at resolveLinks names the dependency.
	- Decisions: The Go setting rather than our own junction walk, since it's the reading the code was written against and Go refuses the build once the setting is dropped. winreadlinkvolume=0 too, so a folder with a volume mounted in it reads by drive letter rather than as a volume GUID path, as before Go 1.23. That half wasn't run on a box.
	- Swept: every EvalSymlinks, Lstat, ReadDir and Readlink call under src-go. lockBeside now takes one lock for a config file reached through a junction. The others test existence or list names, and read the same either way.
	- Verified: on vm925w, the Go tests pass on the fixed build. On a build without the go.mod block both new tests fail, and on the fixed build run with GODEBUG=winsymlink=1 the junction test fails. The real gitsby.exe was run the same way: status, account list, and plain git after account apply named the account from both spellings, where the old build named it nowhere. Under Wine the junction test skips, since mklink there makes nothing. Quick gate passed with every area.
	- Test case: TestAccountForDirThroughJunction [dfh6e] in Go, Windows only, and TestJunctionGodebugBuiltIn [dfh6f] on every platform.
	- Branch: nov19b-2026111910223218
	- Commit: 20da070
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, test failed before and passes after on vm925w.
	- Closed: 20261119-131110

- Code Review 20261110b item 1: raw glab sends the folder account's token to any GitLab host glab is pointed at
	- ID: 2026111016332442
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261110-163324
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: In a folder whose account is on gitlab.gnome.org with a token file, run `gitsby raw glab api --hostname gitlab.com user`, or `gitsby raw glab mr list -R gitlab.com/someone/else`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: glab sends the gitlab.gnome.org token to gitlab.com as `PRIVATE-TOKEN`. Plain glab sends none.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The token goes only to the account's own host.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23, glab 1.53.0, with the gitlab.com API pointed at a local logger.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: hostTokenEnv in githost.go puts the token in `GITLAB_TOKEN`, and glab applies that to every host. The code comment says the host beside it keeps the token where it came from, which holds for tea but not for glab.
	- Origin: 483ebc5 and d8d3c69, 2026-10. Same class as Bug 2026102209210000, whose fix pinned only `raw glab auth status`. Confirmed.
	- Sweep: Every glab subcommand that takes a host: `api --hostname`, `-R host/...`, `repo clone <url>`. Also tea's `--login` and any other variable a host CLI applies to every host.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: glab reads `GITLAB_TOKEN` before it looks at the host, so the token goes to any host a command names. `GITLAB_API_HOST`, from the caller's own environment, also sent it elsewhere.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: `glabTokenEnv` in githost.go. `raw glab` and `pr` hand the token only with `GITLAB_API_HOST` pinned to the account's host, since glab sends every API call there whatever host it's told. A run that names another host gets no token and no changed variables, and says so on stderr.
	- Decisions:
		- Pin and refuse both. The pin alone sends `api --hostname gitlab.com` to the account's host, a wrong answer. The refusal alone misses any spelling not listed.
		- A host named by `--hostname`, `-h`, `-R`, a URL or `user@host:path` argument, a repo command's `host/group/name`, or the caller's `GITLAB_API_HOST`. glab takes a dotted first part as a host only when its config knows it, which gitsby can't read, so a dotted first part always counts. Too many means no token, never a token sent astray.
		- An argument counts as a URL only from its first byte, so a label such as `priority:high` or an api field such as `url=https://...` doesn't.
	- Progress log:
		- 2026-11-10: Checked against glab 1.53.0 through a logging proxy: `GITLAB_API_HOST` wins over `--hostname`, `-R` and a URL, and with `GITLAB_HOST` set glab skips remotes on other hosts, so a second remote in the clone isn't a way out.
		- 2026-11-10: test.bash `[ddk65]` assert updated: `raw glab` now also prints `api=git.example.test`, from the pin. Old `^host=https://git\.example\.test token=tok_ghonly$`, new `^host=https://git\.example\.test token=tok_ghonly api=git\.example\.test$`.
	- Test case: Go `[df4w4]` `[df4w5]`, test.bash `[df4w6]` `[df4w7]` `[df4w8]`.
	- Verified: test.bash `[df4w6]` `[df4w7]` `[df4w8]` fail on the unfixed build (1937/4, with `[ddk65]`) and pass after. Quick gate passed, all areas, test.bash 1941/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 30/0. Real glab 1.53.0 through the built gitsby: `api user` and `mr list` go to gitlab.gnome.org as the account, `api --hostname gitlab.com user` and `mr list -R gitlab.com/someone/else` say they aren't acting as the account.
	- Swept: `hostTokenEnv`'s 3 callers. `raw glab` and `pr` now go through `glabTokenEnv`. `raw tea` keeps its env login on `GITEA_INSTANCE_URL`, and `--login` picks a stored login with its own token, so tea isn't affected, by reading only, since this box has tea 0.9.2. gh's `GH_TOKEN` is for github.com only, and Enterprise is item 20. lazygit and tig go through git's host-scoped credential helper.
	- Acceptance signoff: Closed on tests.
	- Closed: 20261110-185317

- Code Review 20261110b item 2: After account apply, a nested account's folder uses the outer account's token file and name
	- ID: 2026111016332429
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261110-163324
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Account a has a token file, a name and folder P. Account b has a GitHub login and email, folder P/nested, and no token file. Run `account apply`, then `git credential fill` and `gitsby whoami` in a repo under P/nested.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: Plain git and `gitsby raw git` both answer with b's username and a's token. `whoami` says b and shows `Author: <a's name> <b's email>`. Before apply, gitsby said b used no token.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A folder gets only its own account's keys. A key the account doesn't set is unset there, not taken from an outer account.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23, hermetic fixture with a fake gh.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: Both fragments are included in the nested folder. writeAccountFragment skips empty values, so a key only the outer fragment sets wins: `gitsby.ghTokenFile`, `user.name` and the credential username. tokenFor's fallback to `gitsby.ghTokenFile` then reads it too.
	- Origin: The fallback from d92a157, 2026-08-19. The ghTokenFile key from 0ad1374, 2026-09-16. The plain-git half from 08e7452, 2026-11-08. The 20260812 fix for apply's rule order covered only keys both accounts set. Confirmed.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: git includes every fragment whose rule matches, and a later include can't unset a key. The inner fragment left out what its account doesn't set, so the outer one's token file, name, ssh key and ghAccount held there.
	- Actual effort: Avg
	- Decisions:
		- Where an outer account's fragment can come first in a folder, the inner one writes each key its account leaves unset that the outer one sets. The value is what the global or system git config gives it outside the fragments, read at apply time. Departs from "unset", which git has no way to do from an include.
		- Where that config gives none, the key is written empty. gitsby reads an empty `gitsby.ghAccount` or `gitsby.ghTokenFile` as none, and so does the helper. An empty `user.name` makes git refuse a commit and ask who you are, rather than use the outer name. `core.sshCommand` gets plain `ssh`, since git runs an empty one as a command.
		- Only for accounts whose fragments can stack: a folder-name rule, or a path at or above the inner path, case aside. Elsewhere nothing changes, so the copied value can only go stale where accounts nest. accounts.md says to run `apply` again after changing one of those keys.
		- The credential helper isn't put back. It's a list, and the outer one reads only the keys that are.
		- Changelog under Fixed.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: `account apply` gathers every account's keys first, and `withOuterKeys` adds the outer accounts' keys to the inner fragment, with `valueOutsideFragments` for the value.
	- Branch: round-20261111
	- Commit: 6770e4f
	- Test case: test.bash `[df4ws]` to `[df4wx]` (token through plain git and `raw git`, the whoami name, the ssh key, and the outer folder still gets its token). Go `[df4x3]` for which accounts stack.
		- Verified: `[df4ws]` to `[df4ww]` fail on the unfixed build (1942/4) and pass after, with `[df4wx]` passing both ways. `[df4x3]` fails with the folder-name case broken. Quick gate passed, all areas: test.bash 1946/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 30/0.
		- Swept: every key the fragment writes, the token lookup in gitsby's own runs (`accountToken`'s fallback reads the put-back value), and `resolveAccount`'s `gitsby.ghAccount` pin. `writeAccountFragment` has no other caller.
		- Not run on Windows. The origin compare goes through `canonPath`, as `accountManagedIncludes` does.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests passed. The value choice has a Check: entry in questions.md.
	- Closed: 20261110-192044

- The pipeline prunes every project's docker build cache
	- ID: 2026110311291903
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority|Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261103-112919
	- Opened by: JC
	- Related IDs: common 2026110311291900
	- Incorrect behavior: The pipeline runs `docker builder prune` after a run, in `cicd/cicd.bash` and `cicd/test.bash`. That prunes docker's default builder, which every project shares, so a run here drops any other project's cache once it's a week unused. common's `Cleanup after a run` rule said to do it.
	- Expected behavior: The pipeline doesn't prune docker's build cache at all. Docker trims the cache itself on b23, through `builder.gc` in `/etc/docker/daemon.json`. Cache unused for a week goes first, then the rest is cut to 120 GB, or further when the disk is under 10% free, but never below 20 GB. The label cleanup of this project's containers, dangling images and old tags stays.
		- Do it once b23's `/etc/docker/daemon.json` has the `builder.gc` block. `grep -q '"gc"' /etc/docker/daemon.json` checks. Until then the prune stays.
	- Decisions:
		- Don't move to a buildx builder of the project's own instead. shcl tried that on 2026-11-02. A cold build of a 2 GB image took 299 s against 266 s on the default builder, and the builder kept a second 3 GB copy of the layers for a week. shcl is going back to the default builder. (JC, me)
		- The run no longer reports build cache in its end line, since it removes none.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The end of a run no longer runs `docker builder prune`. b23's `daemon.json` has the `builder.gc` block, so the condition to do it was met. contributing.md says the cache is left to docker.
	- Branch: round-20261106
	- Test case: test.bash [dee5k] changed: a run in the image calls no `docker builder` command, passed or stopped.
		- 2026-11-06: [dee5k] asserted `docker builder prune -f --filter until=168h` was called, and now asserts no `docker builder` call at all. Its title says the build cache is left to docker.
	- Verified: [dee5k] fails against the previous cicd.bash and passes after. `--backlog-run-quick` passed with every area, test.bash 1775/0, fuzz 313/0, parity 29/0.
	- Swept: every `docker builder`, `buildx`, `system prune` and `image prune` in the tree. Only cicd.bash had one.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its test passed.
	- Closed: 20261106-105627

- The quick run fails staticcheck in the hook's gate worktree
	- ID: 2026102518002917
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261025-180029
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026102507133273, 2026102506452488
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]:
		- `git -C .git/gitsby-gate checkout --detach --force 422b8aa`
		- `(cd .git/gitsby-gate && cicd/cicd.bash --backlog-run-quick lint)`
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: Stage 1 fails with "error obtaining VCS status: exit status 128 ... Use -buildvcs=false to disable VCS stamping", then "FAILED: staticcheck findings". The same commit passes in the live checkout.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The run passes in the gate worktree as it does in the checkout, so the pre-push hook can gate a push to main.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-10-25, at the round tip 6a752d7 in the gate worktree, in the image.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The gate worktree's `.git` is a file pointing at `repo/.git/worktrees/gitsby-gate`, which isn't mounted in the container, so git can't read the repo there. Since 461657d the quick run, `--gate` included, runs in the image, so every gated push to main fails this way.
	- Actual cause [Bug]:
		- The repo's git dir is mounted, and git works there. Go takes only a `.git` folder for a repo, not a worktree's `.git` file. So from the gate worktree under `repo/.git/` it walks up and takes the main checkout for the repo.
		- In the image the main checkout's folder is a mount point owned by root, so git refuses it as dubious ownership and exits 128. On the box it passes, and stamps the main checkout's revision into the lint builds.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: cicd.bash exports `GOFLAGS` with `-buildvcs=false`, after any flags the caller set, so nothing go builds there stamps a revision. The `-o` builds already passed it.
	- Progress log:
		- 2026-10-25: Found when the round's early full run started in the gate worktree. gover 422b8aa fails the same way, so it predates the round.
	- Branch: round-20261025b
	- Test case: test.bash [dee90].
	- Verified: [dee90] fails against the old cicd.bash, with the other 1740 passing. `--backlog-run-quick` passed with every area: test.bash 1740 -> 1748, 0 failed, fuzz 313/0, parity 29/0. The issue's steps, and `--backlog-run-quick unit`, passed in the gate worktree with the fix, in the image.
	- Swept: `GO_BUILD_FLAGS` already has the flag. `fImageGo` mounts only the tree, so go finds no repo there. release.bash runs its checks through cicd.bash. test.bash, fuzz.bash and parity.bash get it from the run.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its test failed before and passes after, and so did the issue's own steps.
	- Closed: 20261025-181343

- `repo clone` hands git a folder name taken from the URL, and git can read it as an option
	- ID: 2026100607545802
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority|Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261006-074900
	- Closed: 20261006-104608
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: With no folder given, `repo clone` names it after the URL's last part. A URL ending in `--upload-pack=<cmd>.git` put that text in git's argument list as an option. On a local or `file://` clone git runs it as a command.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The URL and the folder always reach git as plain arguments.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: Yes. A bare repo named `--upload-pack=touch CANARY;git-upload-pack.git`, then `gitsby -q repo clone file://...` made the canary file.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: `cmdClone` ran `git clone <url> <dir>` with no `--` in front.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: `git clone -- <url> <dir>`, and the plan line shows the same.
	- Swept: every `a.step` call for git, gh and tea. gitsby's own parser refuses an argument that starts with a dash, `--` included, checked for `br create`, `repo connect`, `repo url` and `repo create`. So only a value gitsby builds from other input can start with one, and the clone folder was the only such value. Built URLs start with a scheme.
	- Branch: fuzzwork
	- Commit: c1b10fc
	- Test case: fuzz.bash [ddjyb]. Red on `gover`'s code, green here.
	- Verified: fuzz.bash 311/0, test.bash 1491/0, parity.bash 29/0 on the branch.

- test.bash removes the folder it was started from when mktemp fails
	- ID: 2026100415391365
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority|Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261004-153913
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]:
		- Run `cicd/test.bash` with `TMPDIR` set to something that isn't a folder, such as a file.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: `mktemp -d` fails, and `work` ends up as the current folder. The exit trap then runs `rm -rf` on it. Started from the repo root, that is the whole checkout, `.git` included.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The suite stops before it sets the trap, and removes nothing.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: Yes, 2026-10-04 on b23, against a scratch folder, which was removed. The same day it removed the gitsby checkout, which came back whole from the 15:30 ZFS snapshot.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: test.bash line 32 is `work="$(cd "$(mktemp -d ...)" && pwd -P)"`. The mktemp failure is lost, and `cd ""` succeeds without moving.
	- Note: a probable fix checks the mktemp result before resolving it, and refuses a `work` that isn't a `gitsby-test.*` folder before arming the trap. A grep of `cicd` and the installers finds no other `cd "$(mktemp` site.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The mktemp call sat inside the `cd` that resolves it, so its failure was lost. `cd ""` succeeds without moving, so `work` became the current folder, and the exit trap removed it.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: mktemp runs on its own line and stops the suite when it fails. Before the trap is set, the resolved folder has to be the one mktemp made, named `gitsby-test.*`, and empty. A marker file goes in it, and the trap removes the folder only while the name and the marker are both there.
	- Swept: install.bash and every script in cicd/, cicd/utility/ and cicd/utility/demo/. Only test.bash wrapped mktemp in a `cd`. The rest assign mktemp straight to a variable under `set -e`, so a failure stops them or leaves an empty value that `${x:?}` refuses before any `rm`. demo-repo.bash and remote-tests.bash already check a marker before removing. The shared files in cicd/utility/include/ have no mktemp and no recursive removal.
	- Verified: with TMPDIR a file, the suite before the fix removed the folder it was started from, canary included, and the fixed one stopped at mktemp and left it alone. `[ddgkk]` fails against the old test.bash and passes against the new one, and so does `[ddgkm]`'s pattern on test.bash. With mktemp working, the scratch folder is still removed and the exit code kept, for a plain TMPDIR, one ending in a slash, and one reached through a link.
	- Verified: shellcheck, `test-id.bash --check`, and `cicd.bash --gate`.
	- Not run: the full test.bash. No run reaches the trap's refusal of a folder without the marker.
	- Test case: test.bash `[ddgkk]`, a real run with mktemp failing, and `[ddgkm]`, no script changes into a mktemp result unchecked.
	- Verified: the 2026-10-04 test batch. test.bash on b23 passed 1452 and failed 1, which is 1412 plus this round's 41 new checks. The one failure is `[db712]`, from enhancement 8.
	- Verified: stage 7 on 2026-10-04. vm925w passed its Go tests. vmFreeBSD and vmDebARM64 passed their Go tests, and their test.bash failed only `[db712]`, from enhancement 8. b26 was skipped, since another session held it.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed. Reproduced, its test failed before the fix and passes after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261004-182117
	- Branch: tmpguard
	- Commit: 609ccb9

- The README install line fails while v2.1.0 is the newest full release
	- ID: 2026100315501800
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority|Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 2026-10-03
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026100313491873
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]:
		- Run gover's install.bash with no version, against the releases as they are today.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It picks v2.1.0 and stops with "publishes no gitsby binary for linux/amd64". v2.1.0 has only the `gitsby` and `gitsby.ps1` scripts.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The install line works on the day the Go build reaches `main`.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: Yes, 2026-10-03, against the live release list.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The installer takes a pre-release only when no full release exists, and the first Go release is v3.0.0-beta.1, which must not reach the install line. So the line resolves to a release the new installer can't install. This was true before item 2026100313491873.
	- Notes:
		- Blocks the release that merges gover to `main`.
		- What the install line should give during the beta is a call for signoff, not a worker.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: With no tag, both installers took the newest full release from the `releases/latest` redirect and never asked whether it had a Go binary. The release list was read only when there was no full release at all.
	- Decisions:
		- 2026-10-03: The install line takes the beta while no full release publishes a gitsby binary. This reverses the earlier rule that the beta must not reach the install line. A full release with a binary always wins over any pre-release, so once 3.0.0 is out, later betas stay off the line.
		- A binary means any asset named `gitsby-<os>-<arch>`, not one for this platform. Every machine is pointed at the same release, and one it leaves out is told "publishes no gitsby binary for linux/386. It publishes: ..." rather than quietly getting an older beta that covers it.
		- Newest is the highest version. Full releases are compared only with each other, and pre-releases only with each other, so the `sort -V` trap can't arise. Two pre-releases of one version go by list order, which is publish order.
		- `releases/latest` is still asked first, since it has no API limit, and settles it when its SHA256SUMS lists a binary. The release list is read only otherwise, in one request, from the asset URLs it carries.
		- The README's `--tag v3.0.0-beta.1` line is dropped, since the plain line takes that beta. The paragraph says a later pre-release needs `--tag`.
		- Against: design.md "The proof is the contract, not the installer". Phase 3 now also runs the tag's install.bash, only to read which release it takes. The contract proof is unchanged, and design.md has a bullet for the new step.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: Both installers, with no tag, keep the redirect's release only when its SHA256SUMS lists a gitsby binary. Otherwise they read the list and take the highest full release with one, else the highest pre-release with one, and say so. When none has one they stop and say so, and when the list can't be read they name the full release that had none. An explicit tag works as before, and `--tag v2.1.0` still stops with "publishes no gitsby binary". release.bash phase 3 runs the tag's install.bash into a throwaway home, says which release the line takes, and warns when a full release isn't taken or a pre-release loses to an older one.
	- Swept: `releases/latest`, `pre-release`, `full release`, `beta.1` and `one-liner` across install.bash, install.ps1, release.bash, README.md, design.md and test.bash. README, design.md "Release policy" and "Automating a release", and release.bash's header and pre-release comment are updated. `legacy/` is frozen and left alone.
	- Verified: 14 of the 21 new checks fail against gover's installers and release.bash and pass here. The other 7 pin what must not change (an explicit tag, a full release over a newer beta, no list request when the redirect's release has a binary) and pass on both. test.bash 1365/0, and `cicd.bash --gate` passes. Both installers run against the live release list stop with "No release of yottacore/gitsby publishes a gitsby binary yet", which is today's state.
	- Note: the checks run under pwsh 7 and bash 5.2 here. Windows PowerShell 5.1 and macOS bash 3.2 were not run, as with the other installer checks.
	- Branch: betainst
	- Commit: 4ccd133
	- Test case: [ddf98] through [ddf9g] (install.bash), [ddf9h] through [ddf9s] (install.ps1) and [ddf9t], [ddf9v], [ddf9w] (release.bash phase 3) in test.bash.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the rule was set by hand on 2026-10-03, and the checks fail before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261003-171623

- `account apply` writes no credential helper per account, so plain `git push` over https fails in the folder of an account gh isn't active as
	- ID: 2026110810100400
	- Type: Feature
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Needs external testing: No. The same checks ran on vm925w, below. Stage 7 runs only the Go tests on a Windows box, not test.bash.
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261108-101004
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Target OS: All
	- Requirements [Feature]:
		- Port dev's 13dbf98 (2026-09-30, bash build only) to Go. Each account's fragment gets a credential helper for its host.
		- The helper text is the same for every account. It reads `gitsby.ghAccount` and `gitsby.ghTokenFile` from git config when it runs, so no login or path is pasted into a string a shell runs.
		- On GitHub it asks `gh auth token --user <login>`, then the `tokenFile`. On other hosts only the `tokenFile`, since tea has no `auth token`.
		- No token written to disk. A credential manager already set up still gets asked first.
		- Tested through real `git credential fill`, with gh active as a different account.
		- Doc it in accounts.md and the changelog.
	- Progress log:
		- 2026-11-08: Found while merging dev into gover for v3.0.0-beta.1. dev's bash and doc changes were dropped in that merge, since the Go build has none of it yet. Not in any release, so nothing regresses.
		- 2026-11-08: Ported. `account apply` writes `credential.https://<host>.helper` into each account's fragment, one fixed text per kind of host, built by `fragmentHelper` in accountcmd.go. Doc in accounts.md and the changelog.
	- Decisions:
		- No helper for an account with no way to a token on its own host: no `tokenFile`, and no `ghAccount` on GitHub, such as an ssh-only account. Departs from "each account's fragment". A helper that can never answer only adds processes to every https request.
		- The token file is read from the global config only, with `--includes`, the scope the fragment is included from. Same rule as `configOwnScope`: a repo's own config doesn't get to name a token file. A relative path is no file, as in `readTokenFile`. `gitsby.ghAccount` is read from any scope, as gitsby's own runs read it.
		- A username git already holds is left alone, and `x` stands in where there is none, as `accountLogin` does. A username that differs from the login isn't refused the way gh's helper refuses one, since `user` and `ghAccount` may differ on purpose.
		- `gh auth token --user` with no `--hostname`, the same call `probeGhToken` makes, so `GH_HOST` picks an Enterprise host for both.
		- `gh auth setup-git` run after `apply` clears the helpers ahead of its own, which takes out ours too. Checked with git 2.51. Documented: run `apply` again, which moves the includes back to the end.
		- Changelog under Added, since no release has had this.
	- Branch: round-20261108
	- Test case: [df1s0] to [df1s8] and [df1sa] in test.bash, all through real `git credential fill` with the fake gh active as another account.
		- Verified: with no helper written, [df1s0] to [df1s3] and [df1s5] fail. With gh asked on every host, a helper for every account, and the token file read from any scope, [df1s3], [df1s4], [df1s7] and [df1sa] fail. All pass on the change: test.bash 1884/0, quick gate passed (lint, go test, fuzz 313/0, parity 30/0).
		- Not watched red: [df1s6], since the order is git's own, and [df1s8], since the helper has no interpolated text to break.
		- Swept: the other place that writes a helper, `selectAccount`, resets the list for gitsby's own runs, so the two don't stack. [db5wk] still passes.
		- Verified on vm925w, Git for Windows 2.55.0, with the windows/amd64 build of 08e7452: [df1s0] to [df1s8], [df1sa] and [dd80d], run the same way as in test.bash, all pass, with every token file named by a `C:/` path. So does a `~/` token file under a backslash HOME, which the helper's sh reads as `C:\...\tildehome/tilde.tok`. With the 53fcc0b build, [df1s0] to [df1s3], [df1s5] and that `~/` check fail.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: 08e7452 passed on b23 (test.bash 1884/0) and on vm925w (12/0).
	- Closed: 20261108-142139

- CICD reset: CPU and priority on the Windows box
	- ID: 2026102508333054
	- Type: Enhancement
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
		- 2026-10-26: Back from testing. The class and the count hold on Windows, but the exit code doesn't come back. The template has no Re-opened, so Queued.
		- 2026-10-26: The exit code comes back now, so closed.
	- Needs external testing: Done. On vm925w, 2026-10-26, as below.
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: High
	- Opened: 20261025-083330
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Parent ID: 2026102416313103
	- Requirements [Feature]:
		- Stage 7's Go tests on the Windows box run in the `BelowNormal` priority class, with `GOMAXPROCS` at half that box's cores, rounded down and at least 1, per `Machine use`.
		- Windows has no load average. Say on the item what stands in for the busy rule there, or that none does.
	- Progress log:
		- ssh lands in cmd there. `set /a` can work the count out before the marker line. `start /belownormal /wait` may not hand back the test binary's exit code. Neither can be run from here.
		- 2026-10-25: The Windows command sets `GOMAXPROCS` to `%NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS%/2`, or 1 under 2 cores, ahead of the marker, and runs the tests with `start "" /belownormal /b /wait`.
		- 2026-10-25: A `--- FAIL` line in the output fails the box even when the exit code comes back 0, with a warning that says so.
		- Under Wine's cmd, the same command line gave `GOMAXPROCS` 16 on 32 cores, and the test binary's exit code 3 came back through `start /wait`. Wine ignores the priority class, so BelowNormal is unchecked. Wine's `set /a` doesn't read a variable by name, so the line expands `%NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS%`.
		- Verified: test.bash 1737/0 on the box, and `--backlog-run-quick` in the image, with test.bash 1737/0, fuzz 313/0 and parity 29/0. Against the harness before the change, `[dee74]` and `[dee75]` fail.
		- 2026-10-26: Verified on vm925w, from round-20261026 at 20bdeb6: `gitsby-test.exe` ran as `BelowNormal`, base priority 6, in four polls while it ran. vm925w has no `wmic`, so `Get-Process` stood in.
		- 2026-10-26: Verified on b29w: the command's first part gives `GOMAXPROCS=8` with `NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS=16`.
		- 2026-10-26: With one test failing on purpose, vm925w failed the box only through the guard: `WARNING: vm925w's go test failed a test and still exited 0`, then `FAIL: vm925w go test (exit 1)`. So `start "" /belownormal /b /wait` hands back 0 on real Windows, unlike Wine. The `--- FAIL` guard is what fails the box now. A crash with no `--- FAIL` line would pass.
		- 2026-10-26: On vm925w, `start /wait` leaves the test's code in ERRORLEVEL, but cmd still exits 0. The command now ends with `& call exit %^ERRORLEVEL%`, which handed back 1, 3, 0 and a crash code there, and 1 for a failed `cd` ahead of it.
		- 2026-10-26: `[dee74]` wants `& call exit %^ERRORLEVEL%` at the end of the line, where it wanted `-test.v` last.
		- Verified: with one test failing on purpose, vm925w failed the box on the exit code, `FAIL: vm925w go test (exit 1)`, with no `WARNING` line. From round-20261026 at 65e4b54. The VM was put back to off.
		- Verified: `--backlog-run-quick lint suite` passed, with test.bash 1770/0. Against remote-tests.bash before the fix, `[dee74]` and `[defv6]` fail, 1768/2.
		- Not run: under Wine, and on b29w.
	- Decisions:
		- Nothing stands in for the busy rule. The box always gets half its cores, and BelowNormal yields to its other work. A one-shot CPU sample was passed over, since it's not an average. Filed as a Check in questions.md.
		- `call exit %^ERRORLEVEL%` rather than `if errorlevel 1 exit 1`, since it keeps the code, and a crash code is negative there. The `--- FAIL` guard stays, in case the code is lost some other way.
	- Branch: round-20261025b, round-20261026
	- Test case: test.bash `[dee74]` (the count, the class and the exit code on the command line), `[dee75]` (a failing test that exits 0), `[defv6]` (a crash with no `--- FAIL` line fails on the exit code, against a stub that drops it the way Windows does).
	- Swept: every remote command in remote-tests.bash's `fRunWindows`. The copy and cleanup steps run no tests, so they keep normal priority.
		- 2026-10-26: `git grep` for `/wait`, `belownormal` and `ERRORLEVEL`. The test run is the only `start` in the repo. The copy and cleanup steps don't go through `start`, so cmd's own code comes back.
	- Prereq IDs: 2026102519554107
	- 2026-10-25: The round's full run reached stage 7, where vmDebARM64 failed 22 harness checks (2026102519554107). Waits on that.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed. Its new check fails before the fix and passes after, and the box check ran on vm925w.
