		- Sweeping override, 2026-10-24: this supersedes any earlier decision on this project that conflicts with it.
		- Per the ID and per-test line bullets in `Testing` in the shared CICD rules. Every test already has an ID and prints one line.
		- An ID is whole minutes since 2000-01-01 00:00 UTC, in lowercase Crockford base 32, such as `decp8`. Today they're milliseconds in base 62.
		- Every existing ID is converted once, from the time it already holds. When 2 come out the same, the newer one takes the next free minute.
		- `test-id.bash`, the duplicate check in test.bash, the backlog check and the IDs named in this backlog move together.
		- Each test prints `PASS <id> <name>`, `FAIL <id> <name>` or `SKIP <id> <why>`, in place of `ok: [<id>] <name>` and the rest, on this box and on the remote boxes.
		- Earlier decisions this overrides: the private test ID rule, milliseconds in base 62.
	- Progress log:
		- 2026-10-26: Split. The ID conversion is done here, and the per-test line is 2026102618140158.
		- 2026-10-26: All 1860 IDs converted from the times they held, the 3 commented-out checks included, in the suites, the Go tests and this backlog. 1650 of them took a later free minute, since most were minted in bursts a few ms apart. The furthest moved 145 minutes.
		- 2026-10-26: `test-id.bash` mints the new form, moves past a minute a test already has, and takes `-n` for several. `--check` fails an ID that isn't five Crockford base 32 characters. The test fixtures' IDs are in the new form too.
		- 2026-10-26: Asserts given new values for this change. `[ErTFcXs]`, "an ID minted for now is seven characters of base 62", is now `[ddc2j]`, "five characters of lowercase Crockford base 32". `[Er2NSAB]`, "a minted ID is milliseconds since 2000 in base 62", is now `[dd5kt]`, "whole minutes since 2000", minting for 00:32:59 rather than 00:00:00.062, still `10`. `[dd5ez]` and `[dd5p5]` match the ID in spawn-count's output as `[0-9a-z]{5}`, not `[0-9A-Za-z]{7}`.
		- 2026-10-26: Checks relabeled on the round branches before this, now under their new IDs, so against gover they read as removed: `[Er1LxTh]` -> `[dd5g1]`, `[Et6FC4K]` -> `[de4by]`, `[Et9PJrE]` -> `[de548]`, `[Etj1UKH]` -> `[dedpc]`.
	- Decisions:
		- Ties go in age order: each ID, oldest first, takes its own minute or the next one no older test has. So a burst keeps its order.
		- `--check` takes exactly five characters, which lasts until 2063, rather than any length. A leftover old ID then can't pass.

		- The `ok: [<id>] <name>` lines keep their shape until 2026102618140158.

- `--staged`: commit only what is staged, and leave the rest of the tree alone
	- ID: 2026100512025340
	- Type: Enhancement
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority [Feature]: High
	- Opened: 2026-10-05
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Requirements  [Feature]:
		- A `--staged` flag on `pullcom`, `sync`, and the branch commands that commit the tree before they move: `br create` off a feature branch, `br switch` and `br merge`.
		- With it, the commit takes the index only. Nothing is staged, and unstaged or untracked edits stay where they are.
			- Nothing staged means nothing is committed. The command goes on with the rest.
			- On a checkout, the leftover edits come along, the way plain git does it.
			- Where git would refuse that checkout, the plan says so before anything runs.
		- The plan shows which files get committed and which stay behind.
		- Without the flag, nothing changes.
	- Notes:
		- Each of those commands runs `git add --all` first today. In a tree with hand edits that aren't part of the change, that sweeps them in.
		- `br create` from `main` or `dev` already carries edits over, and stays that way.
	- Decisions:
		- A flag, not a new command (2026-10-05). It keeps the count of commands down.
		- Opt-in, not switched on by finding something staged (2026-10-05). A file staged long ago would quietly make the commit smaller, and under `-q` nobody reads the plan. Most users never think about the index, and shouldn't have to.
		- It doesn't go against design.md's line that partial staging belongs to raw git. Gitsby still stages nothing itself. It only stops undoing a `git add` that was already made. design.md gets a line saying so.
		- Before the first Go release, since flags and aliases are permanent after it.
	- Estimated effort: Avg
	- Progress log:
		- Verified: git's autostash brings staged work back unstaged, on git 2.51. A file staged and then edited again lost its staged copy. Git's current source still reapplies it that way. A plain fast-forward with no stash kept the index, and where incoming commits touched a file with edits here, git refused and changed nothing.
		- So with `--staged` no pull uses `--autostash`. Committing the staged part before the pull was the other way, but a remote that moved ahead would then be diverged.
		- Done: `--staged` on `pullcom`, `sync`, `br create`, `br hotfix`, `br switch` and `br merge`. The commit takes the index only, and the plan lists what is committed and what stays. Nothing staged commits nothing, and the run goes on.
		- Done: a pull or checkout that git would refuse over the edits left in the tree is refused before the plan, with nothing done. That is the reading taken of "the plan says so before anything runs": a plan that can't finish isn't shown. A pull from a remote other than origin can't be read ahead; git refuses that one at the time.
		- Note: `br hotfix` takes the flag too, since it is the same recipe as `br create`. `pr create` and `release` also commit the whole tree, and refuse the flag for now. Adding it there later breaks nobody.
		- Done: help, README, workflows.md, the changelog, and design.md, with the line the Decisions ask for and the autostash finding.
		- Verified: `go test ./...` and the gate pass. The 18 new suite checks pass on their own. With `--autostash` put back on every pull, 6 of them fail. With the read-ahead turned off, 4 fail.
		- Verified: the full test.bash on the merged tree, 1471/0 (2026-10-05).
		- For signoff: `br hotfix` taking the flag, `pr create` and `release` refusing it, and the plan's two list labels, "staged, so committed:" and "not staged, so left as is:".
		- Answered 2026-10-05: `br hotfix` taking the flag is OK.
		- Answered 2026-10-05: `pr create` and `release` take the flag too, with the same rules as the other commands.
		- Still open: the plan's two list labels. They are being looked at in context, and stay as they are until then.
		- Done: `--staged` on `pr create` and `release`. Their commit takes the index only, no pull uses `--autostash`, and the plan lists what is committed and what stays. Nothing staged commits nothing, and the run goes on.
		- Done: `release` reads ahead every pull and checkout up to the default branch, and refuses before the plan where git would stop. A file that passes is the same on every branch read, so the merge, the move back to `dev` and the last checkout can't touch it. Only the index counts as work to release, so a level repo with only unstaged edits says there is nothing new, as it would with a clean tree.
		- Done: `pr create` parks the way `sync` does. Both `gh` and `tea` are handed the branch with `--head`, and with that neither looks at the working tree. Read in their source, not run against a real host.
		- Done: `pr ok` still refuses the flag, since it commits nothing. The old test.bash check that release refuses the flag, `[ddhth]`, is commented out with the reason, and `[ddhvb]` asks the same of `repo connect`. Go test `[ddht9]` now expects `pr create` and `release` to take it.
		- Done: README, the changelog and design.md list the 2 commands. Help and workflows.md name no commands for the flag, so they needed nothing.
		- Verified: `go test ./...` and the gate pass. The 12 new suite checks and the 25 around them pass on their own. Against the build before this, 10 of the 12 fail; the other 2, a plan with no `git add` and `pr ok` refusing, pass either way and guard against a regression. With the release read-ahead turned off, 2 fail. With the nothing-new rule back on the whole tree, 3 fail.
		- Verified: the full test.bash on the branch, 1482/0 (2026-10-05).
		- For signoff: the plan's two list labels only.
		- Answered 2026-10-05: the labels read "Changes to commit:" and "Changes to leave alone:". The plan prints before anything runs, so past tense read wrong.
	- Branch: staged, stagedpr
	- Commit: 9f53a91, 7c3281d
	- Test case: Go tests `[ddht8]`, `[ddht9]`, `[ddhta]`. test.bash `[ddhtb]` through `[ddhtw]`, 18 checks, with `[ddhth]` off since 2026-10-05. For `pr create` and `release`: `[ddhvb]` through `[ddhvk]` and `[ddhvm]` through `[ddhvp]`, 12 checks.
	- Swept: every `--autostash` and `git add --all` in `src-go`. The commit and the pull in mutate.go, br create from `main` or `dev` in branchcmd.go, and both plan lines in preview.go. The file list in repo.go is for `repo create` and `repo connect`, which refuse the flag. The pulls in pr.go and release.go run on a clean tree, and those commands refuse the flag.
	- Swept (2026-10-05, `pr create` and `release`): every step after their commit. In release.go the pulls of `dev` and the default branch, both checkouts, the merge and its back-out, the tag, both pushes, and the fast-forward of `dev`. Its nothing-new check read the whole tree as work to release, and now reads the index under the flag. In pr.go the push and the `gh` or `tea` call. `pr ok` reads the whole tree to refuse, and refuses the flag. The line above about pr.go and release.go held only while they refused the flag.
	- Acceptance signoff: 2026-10-05, all 3 choices answered.
	- Closed: 2026-10-05

- Code Review 20261120 item 14: Every command that stages the tree runs a dry-run add before the plan, in every repo
	- ID: 2026112017135689
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261120-171356
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: In a repo with 100,000 files and one edit, time `gitsby -q --no-fetch pullcom m` on 5af785f and on 576d891.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The dry run takes about 230 ms, as long as a git status, and git's time for the run goes from 982 to 1294 ms. pullcom, br switch, sync, br merge, br create off a feature branch, pr create and release each spawn 2 more processes. A clean `br switch dev` pays it too.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Only a sparse checkout pays for it. 2026111920000538's decision says no other repo does.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, with strace and timed calls on both builds. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: refuseSparseAdd runs the dry run before it reads core.sparseCheckout.
	- Origin: be87857 (2026111910222973) and 397c85f (2026111920000538). No round saw it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: refuseSparseAdd ran git add --all --dry-run, and read core.sparseCheckout, before it knew the repo was a sparse checkout. git refuses or skips a path only where it has sparse patterns, so outside one both answers were always empty.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The rev-parse every run starts with also gives where git keeps this worktree's sparse patterns. Without that file, refuseSparseAdd returns with no spawn. With it, core.sparseCheckout decides, and only then does the dry run go.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfksq], for each of the 10 commands stagesTree names.
	- Verified: [dfksq] fails for all 10 commands with 576d891's mutate.go and passes with the fix. The gate's spawn counts are back at their expected values, such as pullcom 21 and br switch 28, 2 fewer each. Quick gate: unit, suite (test.bash 2319/0), fuzz 310/0 with spawn counts, and parity 31/0 passed. Lint: bash -n and shellcheck passed, then markdownlint stopped on a bare URL at backlog.md line 112, which dev has too; gofmt, go vet, staticcheck and golangci-lint run by hand are clean. gosec 37, as before.
	- Swept: refuseSparseAdd is the only place gitsby asks git about a sparse checkout, by grep for sparse in src-go. Both of its spawns before the plan, the config read and the dry run, now wait on the patterns file.
	- Decisions: The patterns file gates the config read too, so a repo that never had a sparse checkout pays no spawn. The run's first rev-parse locates it with one more --git-path. git reads no patterns without the file, so add refuses and skips nothing then, checked on git 2.51 with core.sparseCheckout on and no file. A disabled checkout keeps the file and pays only the config read. Skip-worktree bits set by hand with the setting off make add refuse nothing, and git diff doesn't list those files either (checked), so they don't need the dry run.
	- Branch: nov21-2026112017135689
	- Commit: 77d0101
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its test failed before the fix and passes after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261121-095627

- Go test [dfk1m] hangs on Windows, so stage 7's Go test run doesn't end
	- ID: 2026112021204523
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261120-212045
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026112017135720, 2026112017135704
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Build the Windows Go test binary from nov20c and run TestRemoteReachesGiveUpOnAStalledSSHRemote on vm925w, which has Windows OpenSSH on PATH.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The test was still running when the run was stopped at 300 s. Its own limit is 30 s per reach. No subtest line showed, so which reach waits isn't known yet.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Each reach gives up within its limit on Windows too, or the test skips there with the reason.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on vm925w, once, from e0ef618. With it skipped, the rest of the binary passed there: 294 ok, 32 skipped, none failed. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: Not known. Windows OpenSSH may not act on ServerAliveInterval against a server that sent its banner, which would mean the fetch itself still hangs on Windows. Or the listener's held connections keep something open there.
	- Origin: adcef33, nov20c (2026112017135720). Its tests ran on b23 only.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The login probe runs PATH's ssh, which on Windows is Windows' own OpenSSH 9.5p2. Against a server quiet after its banner, it reports the timeout and then doesn't exit, and it doesn't end when the server closes either. So [dfk1m]'s 30 s guard fired, and its wait after closing the listener had no limit, which held the binary. The fetch, ls-remote and repo probe passed there, since Git for Windows runs its own ssh (OpenSSH 10.5p1), which exits at the timeout.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The login probe runs ssh under its own limit, ssh's connect timeout plus stallSeconds plus 5 s, 38 s in a run, and stops waiting for output a second after the kill, for a child the ssh command left. [dfk1m] and its http twin [dfhez] now wait at most 10 s after closing the listener, so a client that ignores the close fails rather than holding the binary.
	- Branch: nov20c-2026112017135720-fix
	- Commit: 87bce73
	- Test case: Go [dfk3h] TestSSHLoginProbeEndsAnSSHThatIgnoresItsLimits, both login probe paths against a fake ssh that never ends and leaves a child holding its output. It skips on Windows, where the fakes are shell scripts. Go [dfk1m] on vm925w covers Windows' own ssh.
	- Verified: On vm925w, [dfk1m] from the unfixed build hung in the login probe, per its goroutine stacks at -test.timeout, and the fixed build passed it in 32 s, with [dfhez] and [dfk1n] passing too. [dfk3h] fails with the limit taken out and with the output wait taken out, and passes with both. The quick gate's lint and unit areas passed, and unit with --no-container ran [dfk1m], [dfk1n], [dfk3h] and [dfhez], all passing. gosec 37, unchanged.
	- Swept: every ssh gitsby runs over the network itself is probeSSHLogin, called from sshLogin and askSSHLoginAhead, and both pass the limit. The ssh -G reads in show.go and account.go read config only. The fetch, ls-remote and repo probe run ssh through git. With Windows' own ssh named as the ssh command, those wait too, filed as 2026112021513016. The tests that wait on a reach after closing a listener are [dfhez] and [dfk1m], and both are bounded.
	- Decisions: A limit on the probe's process rather than a Windows skip, since the product's login probe hung there too. One limit on every platform, since an ssh that keeps its own limits ends first. No limit on the whole fetch, which can run long. The probe's limit is read on the calling goroutine, per askSSHLoginAhead's rule. Stage 7's missing time limit is filed as 2026112021514129.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced on vm925w, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261120-215223
	- Closed reason: Done

- Code Review 20261120 item 5: release from a feature branch with unpushed work or a dirty tree tags the commit already released
	- ID: 2026112017135822
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261120-171358
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: After `release v1.0.0`, create feat and push it. Make a commit on it, or leave a file edited. Run `gitsby -q release`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It tags v1.0.1 on the v1.0.0 commit, pushes the tag and exits 0. A clean feat says "Nothing new to release". When the dev push failed after main and the tag went out, a bare release from dev also cuts v1.0.1 on the same commit.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: "Nothing new" for the feature branch runs, and the failed dev push finished as a resume.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, with local bare origins. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The `parks || isAhead()` shortcut at release.go:152-156 counts parked work that never reaches the release. unpushedRelease checks main only.
	- Origin: 20260727b item 12, ported in 4918b5b and changed in 7c3281d and 8dfe5ff. No round saw it. It undoes item 12's aim, which was to stop a second tag on one commit.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The nothing-new check counted any edit, staged change or unpushed commit on the current branch as work to release. Only dev's and the default branch's reach it, since the release merges dev alone. And after a release whose dev push was refused, dev's lead over origin's counted as new, while the resume check read only the default branch.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The current branch's work counts only on dev or the default branch, through parksIntoRelease. The check reads both copies of dev, so a local dev commit still counts from a feature branch. unpushedRelease also takes a level default branch whose tip is tagged, with dev on that tip and origin's dev behind it, and finishes that release by pushing dev.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfjy3] to [dfjyd].
	- Verified: [dfjy3] to [dfjy7], [dfjy9], [dfjya] and [dfjyc] fail on the build before the fix, and all 11 pass with it. With the branch check dropped, [dfjy3] to [dfjy7] fail. With the local dev check dropped, [dfjy7] fails. With the dev resume off, [dfjy9], [dfjya] and [dfjyc] fail. With the resume taking a dev that moved on, [dfjyd] fails. The quick gate passed in 3 calls, since all of it ran past 4 minutes at load 10: lint and unit, suite 2265/0, fuzz 310/0 and parity 31/0. gosec 37, as before, none in release.go.
	- Swept: every work check in src-go, by grep for isAhead(), treeDirty() and indexDiffers(). Only releasePreflight decides whether there is something to release. pushIfOnline, refuseParkPush, pr ok's refusal and repo connect ask about the current branch's own push, which is right for them.
	- Branch: nov20c-2026112017135822
	- Commit: c8ab774
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261120-185827
	- Decisions:
		- Only the current branch's own work is read, when it is dev or the default branch. A branch whose park push lands on origin's dev, as under push.default=upstream, isn't counted. There the worst case is a "Nothing new" that changes nothing, and reading the push remote and dev's upstream for it is more code than that case is worth.
		- On a feature branch, "Nothing new" leaves its commits and edits as they are, with nothing parked or pushed, the same as on a clean one.
		- The dev resume needs a release tag on the default branch's tip, dev on that tip, and origin's dev behind it. A dev that moved on since cuts the next release, as before. A typed version that differs still cuts its own.
		- The dev resume says "Release vX is out, but 'dev' never reached origin; finishing it.", since its tag did reach origin. The default branch's case keeps its line.
		- 1 more git call on every release (a rev-parse in the resume check), and 1 more on the nothing-new path (the local dev check). release isn't in the spawn counts.

- Code Review 20261120 item 7: After account set changes ghaccount, gitsby goes on acting as the old login until account apply
	- ID: 2026112017135793
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261120-171357
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Run apply with `ghaccount: oldlogin`, then `account set work ghaccount newlogin` and `account set work email new@example.test`. Run `whoami` and `raw git credential fill`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: whoami says oldlogin, from the gitsby.ghAccount key in the global git config, with the old email and the old token. account set doesn't mention apply.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: gitsby goes by the accounts file. design.md lets the git config key win only for a single repo that answers for itself, and apply's fragments aren't that.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: account.go:49-58 reads the key from any global config file, the fragments included.
	- Origin: 4918b5b and 1ae9d85 (2026-08-19). Not a regression, and no round saw it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: account apply writes the account's ghaccount and tokenfile into its fragment as gitsby.ghAccount and gitsby.ghTokenFile, and gitsby read both from git config with the fragments included. The fragment's key outranked the folder rule, so after account set the old login won, and the account block was dropped for naming another login, with its email and token.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: gitsby leaves out what the fragments set when it reads gitsby.ghAccount, gitsby.ghTokenFile and gitsby.host, through one reader, gitConfigOutsideFragments. A key set by hand, in a repo, a global file or an include of your own, still counts. account set and unset say plain git keeps the old values until account apply runs again, when the global config includes any fragment. design.md, accounts.md and the changelog say so.
	- Decisions: Leave the fragment's entries out and take the last one left, rather than drop the key whenever the fragment's is the one git settles on, so an apply changes nothing gitsby resolves, which [dfjyt] checks. The token file fallback and its host key go the same way, since the fragment's copy names the old token file after account unset. Fragments are told by being under the accounts file's own fragment folder, as apply's cleanup tells them. A note on account set rather than running apply for it, since apply writes your global git config.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfjyr], [dfjys], [dfjyt], [dfjyv], [dfjyw], [dfjyx], [dfjyy], [dfjyz]. Go [dfjz0].
	- Verified: test.bash [dfjyr] and [dfjyt] to [dfjyz] fail on the unfixed build (test.bash 2264/8; the eighth, [dd5ft], is the Go test file not compiling against the old code) and pass after. [dfjys] passes both ways, as it pins kept behavior. With only the token file reader put back, [dfjyx]'s case gets the old token file. [dfjz0] fails with the fragment check taken out. Quick gate passed, all areas: test.bash 2272/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec on src-go: 37, as before. Not run on Windows.
	- Swept: every gitsby.* key read from git config in src-go: gitsby.ghAccount in resolveAccount, gitsby.ghTokenFile and gitsby.host through configOwnScope. The fragment helper's own reads are plain git's, and valueOutsideFragments already left the fragments out.
	- Branch: nov20c-2026112017135793
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261120-190927
	- Progress log: 20261120: [dd80c] (status names the global git config for the key apply's fragment sets) is commented out. It pinned gitsby reading that key, which this item ends. Its display rule is kept by [dfjys], for a key from an include written by hand.
	- Commit: db581a9

- Code Review 20261120 item 9: Stage 0 passes with conflict markers in the tree when its autostash restore conflicts
	- ID: 2026112017135764
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261120-171357
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Diverge from origin, and leave an edit in a file that origin's commit also changes. Run `cicd.bash -y --no-container` with every later stage turned off.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: git makes the merge, prints "Applying autostash resulted in conflicts" and exits 0. Stage 0 says PASS, the run exits 0, and the tree has the file as `UU` with markers. The edit is only in the stash. The fast-forward path does the same.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The run stops before building, with the merge backed out and the edit back in the tree, per 2026112013542571.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, the real stage 0 in a clone with a local bare origin. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: cicd.bash:1134 and :1142 trust git's exit status after `--autostash`.
	- Origin: 0633cc1 (2026112013542571) for the merge path, and b463d2b (2026-08-12) for the fast-forward path. Missed twin of 2026111910223074. No round saw it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: git exits 0 when --autostash can't put the edits back after a merge or fast-forward. It only warns, leaves markers in the tree and keeps the edits in a new stash entry, and stage 0 trusted the exit status.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: Both stage 0 merges go through one function, fSyncMerge in cicd.bash. A new stash entry after the merge means the restore failed. It then resets to the commit it started from, pops that entry with --index, and stops the run naming the clashing files.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfk07] to [dfk0a].
	- Verified: [dfk07] to [dfk0a] fail on the unfixed cicd.bash (suite 2282/4) and pass with the fix. [dfk08] fails with --index dropped from the pop. The quick gate with every area passed: test.bash 2286/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0.
	- Swept: every --autostash in the repo's scripts, by grep: only the two stage 0 merges, both fixed. The publisher pops its own stash and checks the pop's status. Its index loss is item 27. The Go pulls already check after --autostash (2026111910223074).
	- Decisions: The new stash entry is the signal, since that is where git leaves the edits. The unmerged paths only name the files in the message. The reset goes to the commit stage 0 started from, where the stash applies clean, and --index keeps staged edits staged. A stash entry the user already had is left alone, pinned by [dfk0a].
	- Branch: nov20c-2026112017135764
	- Commit: 6d96733
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261120-200611

- Code Review 20261120 item 11: A branch another worktree is rebasing or bisecting isn't refused, so the run pushes and then fails
	- ID: 2026112017135735
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261120-171357
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Run `git worktree add ../wt dev`, then in wt stop a `git rebase -i` at an edit, or start a bisect. In the main worktree on feat with an edit, run `gitsby -q br switch dev`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It commits and pushes feat, then fails at the checkout with "'dev' is already used by worktree", exit 1.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Refused before the plan, as for a worktree that has the branch checked out.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, with a rebase and with a bisect. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: `%(worktreepath)` names only a worktree whose HEAD is the branch. git also refuses a branch that another worktree is rebasing or bisecting.
	- Origin: 6f277d3, nov19b, Code Review 20261119 item 13. Missed twin.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: refuseHeldBranch read only %(worktreepath), which names a worktree whose HEAD is the branch. A worktree stopped in a rebase of the branch, or bisecting from it, has a detached HEAD, and git still won't check the branch out anywhere else.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: refuseHeldBranch also reads each other worktree's rebase-merge, rebase-apply and BISECT_START, as git does, and refuses before the plan, naming the folder and the rebase's --continue and --abort, or git bisect reset. The worktrees folder comes from one more --git-path in enterRepo's rev-parse, so no spawn was added. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Branch: nov20c-2026112017135778
	- Commit: 486c987
	- Test case: Go [dfjzf] TestRefuseBusyBranch. test.bash [dfjzp] to [dfjzt].
	- Swept: every command that checks a branch out lists it in checkoutsAhead and goes through refuseHeldBranch: br create, br hotfix, br switch, br merge, pr ok and release. br merge deletes only the branch it stands on. br prune's branch -D is left to git, which refuses a busy branch by its source (not run), and its non-fatal handling names that branch and keeps the remote copy. No other call writes an existing branch ref, by grep for update-ref, branch -f, checkout -B and fetch refspecs.
	- Decisions: The files are read as git's is_worktree_being_rebased and is_worktree_being_bisected read them, rather than through git worktree list, which doesn't name a detached worktree's branch and costs a spawn. An am in another worktree holds no branch, as in git. The reads go through os.DirFS, which keeps them inside each git dir.
	- Note: No test fails without the rebase-apply/applying check, since git am writes no head-name. It stays, to match git.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261120-194643
	- Verified: [dfjzp] to [dfjzs] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it, and [dfjzt] passes on both. [dfjzf] fails 5 of its cases with the file check turned off. The quick gate with every area passed before a last change to the file reads in worktreeBusyWith and worktreeFolder. After it, lint, go test, test.bash 2282/0, fuzz 310/0 and spawn counts passed in one gate call that hit its time limit as parity closed, and parity passed 31/0 rerun alone. gosec 37, as before.

- Code Review 20261120 item 12: An ssh origin that stalls after its banner hangs the fetch with no time limit
	- ID: 2026112017135720
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261120-171357
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Run a 127.0.0.1 listener that sends an SSH banner and then nothing. Point origin at it with an ssh:// URL and run `gitsby -q pullcom`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It waits at `git fetch` until it's killed. A server that sends nothing at all ends at the 3 second connect timeout.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The fetch gives up after a few seconds, as an http stall does since Code Review 20261119 item 11.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, OpenSSH 10.3p1. Confirmed. The identity probe at remote.go:279 has the same arguments, by reading.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The ssh arguments at remote.go:207 set ConnectTimeout only. ServerAliveInterval and ServerAliveCountMax would end the stall.
	- Origin: 3d22222 (Go port). Missed twin of Code Review 20261119 item 11, whose sweep covered http only.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: ssh's ConnectTimeout bounds only the connect and the server's banner. gitsby set nothing for what comes after, and ssh sets no limit of its own, so the fetch and the login probe waited on a quiet server until killed.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The fetch, origin/HEAD healing, br prune's ls-remote, the repo probe and the login probe add ServerAliveInterval=10 and ServerAliveCountMax=3 after ConnectTimeout=3. A server quiet for 30 s, the key exchange included, ends the wait, the same limit an http fetch has. pullcom on such an origin warns that the fetch failed after 30 s and goes on.
	- Branch: nov20c-2026112017135720
	- Commit: adcef33
	- Test case: Go test [dfk1m] TestRemoteReachesGiveUpOnAStalledSSHRemote, the fetch, ls-remote, repo probe and both login probe paths against a listener that sends a banner and then nothing. Go test [dfk1n] TestSSHStallOptionsAsSSHReadsThem, remoteEnv's command read back through ssh -G, with a command's own values kept.
		- 2026-11-20: [dbfvz], [dcnp4], [deyth] and [dfg26] asserted the ssh command with ' -o ConnectTimeout=3' added. They now assert ' -o ConnectTimeout=3 -o ServerAliveInterval=10 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3', spelled out once in the test file. Nothing else they check changed.
	- Verified: [dfk1m] fails with the ServerAlive options taken out, the fetch still waiting at 30 s, and fails with either login probe caller passing ConnectTimeout alone. [dfk1n] fails with the options taken out, and with them put ahead of the command's own. Both pass with the fix. The built binary's pullcom on a banner-only ssh origin ended at 30 s with the offline warning. The quick gate passed with every area. [dfk1m] and [dfk1n] skip in the container, which has no ssh, and passed in the unit area with --no-container. gosec 37, unchanged.
	- Swept: every spawn that reaches a remote over ssh outside a step. fetch and set-head in fetchRemote, ls-remote --heads in askOriginHeads and ls-remote in probeRemote all read remoteEnv. probeSSHLogin is called from sshLogin and askSSHLoginAhead, and both pass the limits. The ssh -G reads in show.go and account.go read config only. Push, pull and clone run as steps.
	- Decisions: One stallSeconds, 30, for http and ssh, so both transports give up alike. ServerAliveInterval is a third of it. The options go after the command's own words, since ssh keeps the first value it reads, so a value the ssh command sets itself wins. One in ssh_config is outranked, as ConnectTimeout already was. Push, pull and clone stay as git runs them, per 2026111910223148. The look-ahead probe reads its limits on the calling goroutine, per askSSHLoginAhead's rule.
	- Note: Found while working it, filed as 2026112020462137 (the probe drops an ssh:// port) and 2026112020462150 (no ssh in the cicd image).
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261120-205352

- Code Review 20261119 item 11: A stalled https remote hangs every command
	- ID: 2026111910223148
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261119-102231
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Point origin at a local http listener that accepts and never answers, then run gitsby status.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It sits at git fetch until stopped. pullcom, sync and the push of sync --no-fetch do the same. Nothing is left half done after Ctrl-C.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The fetch and probes give up after a while, as the comment at remote.go line 274 says.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: remoteEnv sets no http speed limit, only the ssh connect timeout.
	- Origin: 88ff4ab, 2026-08-19. The comment came in 8c7a856. No round reached it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: git sets no time limit on http, and remoteEnv gave it none. Only ssh had a connect timeout.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The fetch, origin/HEAD healing, br prune's ls-remote and the repo probe run with GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT=1 and GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_TIME=30, unless the caller set either one. gitsby status on a stalled http origin now warns that the fetch failed after 30 s and goes on.
	- Branch: nov19c-2026111910223148
	- Commit: 9561f20
	- Test case: Go test [dfhez] TestRemoteReachesGiveUpOnAStalledHTTPRemote, the fetch, ls-remote and probe against a listener that never answers. Go test [dfhf0] TestRemoteEnvHTTPStallLimit, every return path of remoteEnv, and a caller's own limit kept.
	- Verified: [dfhez] and [dfhf0] fail with the limit taken out, the fetch still waiting at 30 s, and pass with it. The built binary's status on a stalled http origin ended at 30 s with the offline warning. The quick gate passed with every area.
	- Verified: git 2.51 and curl 8.14 on b23. The env variables outrank http.lowSpeedLimit and -c. A stalled TLS handshake isn't covered by the low-speed check, and ended at curl's 300 s connect limit.
	- Swept: every git call that reaches origin outside a step: fetch and set-head in fetchRemote, ls-remote --heads in askOriginHeads, ls-remote in probeRemote. All read remoteEnv. The ssh probe in probeSSHLogin talks only ssh. Push, pull and clone run as steps.
	- Decisions: Push, pull and clone are left as git runs them. They are steps the plan shows as typed, and the item's expected behavior names only the fetch and probes.
	- Decisions: 30 s at under 1 byte a second. A server packing sends a keepalive every 5 s by default, so a busy one doesn't trip it, and a false trip only reads as offline.
	- Decisions: A caller's GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT or GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_TIME leaves both alone, like a caller's GIT_SSH_COMMAND. An http.lowSpeedLimit in git config is outranked, like ConnectTimeout in ssh_config, since reading it would cost a spawn per run.
	- Decisions: A TLS handshake that never finishes is left at curl's 5 minutes. git has no connect timeout setting, and a watchdog on git's process can't tell a stall from a slow fetch.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261119-174233

The way off is 'git branch --unset-upstream', as for the other push refusals, so the next push is a first publish to origin. Check: entry filed. Answered 2026-11-19: the call stands.

- Code Review 20261119 item 12: In a single-branch clone, br merge merges into main and passes over origin's dev
	- ID: 2026111910223133
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261119-102231
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Clone with --depth 1 from an origin with main and dev, then gitsby -q br create feat, commit, and gitsby -q br merge.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: feat is branched from main and merged into main, pushed, exit 0. br switch dev says there is no dev on origin.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: gitsby finds origin's dev, or refuses and says the fetch is narrowed.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: mergeTarget and branchExistsRemote read only refs/remotes/origin, which a narrowed fetch never fills.
	- Origin: f9716e4, 2026-10-04. No round saw it.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: gitsby read origin's branches only from refs/remotes/origin, which a clone that fetches only some of them never fills. With no dev in sight the merge target was main. A clone of dev alone has no origin/HEAD, so dev read as the default branch too.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: br create, br hotfix, br switch, br merge, br prune, pr create, pr ok and release refuse before the plan when there's no dev here and origin's fetch refspecs don't bring one in, naming 'git remote set-branches origin *' and a fetch. Without origin/HEAD, a default branch not named main, master or trunk refuses the same way. br create, br hotfix and br switch refuse a branch the fetch doesn't cover. pullcom and sync run as before. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Branch: nov19b-2026111910223133
	- Test case: test.bash [dfh8c] to [dfh8h]; Go [dfh89] TestFetchSees, [dfh8a] TestRefuseNarrowFetch.
	- Swept: every branchExistsRemote caller: mergeTarget, isProtectedBranch, checkoutArgs, settleBranchNames, br switch's and br create's name checks, release's 3, backMergeRef, br prune, and pr ok's head check. All sit behind the refusal on the commands that read them. sync and pullcom ask only about the current branch's push. pr ok's 'here but not on origin' refusal for a head the fetch doesn't cover was left alone, since it refuses.
	- Decisions:
		- Refuse, not fetch every branch anyway. That overrides a narrowing that was likely meant, and the next plain git fetch leaves those refs stale. Check: entry filed. Answered 2026-11-19: the call stands.
		- One rule for the listed commands: each refuses while dev can't be seen, br switch to a branch that can be seen included, since isProtectedBranch and the merge target both read dev.
		- pullcom and sync aren't refused. They push only the branch they're on and read no merge target.
		- The default-branch check runs only without origin/HEAD and with a default not named main, master or trunk, so a clone of an empty repo pays no extra spawn. Spawn counts are unchanged.
		- br create and br hotfix read the fetch refspecs on every run, 1 local git config call, since a new name is never on origin yet. No spawn-count measure runs br create.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Commit: d757dc3
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261119-143654
	- Verified: [dfh8c] to [dfh8h] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it, run as a block against each build. [dfh89] and [dfh8a] fail with fetchSees always true. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2155/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0, spawn counts unchanged. gosec reports nothing in the changed files.

- Code Review 20261110b item 8: account apply removes every rule before adding any, so a failure partway leaves too few, and the error says nothing changed
	- ID: 2026111016332355
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261110-163323
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Make the 3rd `git config --global` call of `account apply` fail, as a held `~/.gitconfig.lock` does. Or run 2 applies at once.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The global config is left with no includeIf rules, and a repo under the account's folder has no email. The message names only the rule that failed. Failing the 2nd call says nothing further was applied, though the first rule is already gone. 2 applies at once failed 14 of 40 times and left a duplicate `path` entry.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Each step leaves a working set of rules, and the error says which rules changed.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23, with a git wrapper that fails a chosen call.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: accountcmd.go:449-462 unsets each old rule, then adds the new ones. `account set` also takes a path with a newline, which git refuses as a key, so nothing is added back.
	- Origin: 4918b5b and 353f5c9, 2026-08-19, messages from 47bcda3. Same end state as Code Review 20260819a item 1, which was fixed for one cause only. Confirmed.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: As guessed. Each old rule came out of the global config in its own git call, then each new one went in. One failed call left only some rules. 2 applies at once collided on git's lock and mixed their edits. A newline in a folder rule is a key git refuses, so that add always failed.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The global config is copied beside itself, every removal and add goes into the copy through git, and the copy is renamed over the file, all under git's own lock beside it, which apply waits on for up to 3 seconds. A failure leaves the file as it was, and the error says so and names the rule or the file. The rename follows a link, as git does, and keeps the file's mode.
	- Decisions: A rule git won't take still fails the whole apply, with nothing changed and the rule named. Skipping it would bind the other folders and leave that one quietly unbound. account set still takes a path with a newline. The lock code is the accounts file's, shared, with its messages unchanged. Reapplying still rewrites the file and puts the rules at its end, as before.
		- 2026-11-18: [dd5eg] read "Couldn't add 'includeIf.gitdir". It now reads "Couldn't make the lock beside your global git config.", since a global config under a plain file fails at its lock now, ahead of any rule. The rule-named refusal is [dffzk].

	- Verified: [dffzj], [dffzm], [dffzp], [dffzq] and [dffzr] fail on the unfixed build and pass after. [dffzx] fails with the mode restore taken out, and with the rename over the link rather than its target. [dffzz] fails with the same-file test taken out. Quick gate, all areas: test.bash 2008/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0.
	- Swept: accountManagedIncludes and cmdAccountApply held the only git config --global calls in src-go. Fragments already go through a new file and a rename (b59aab1). The accounts file save takes the same lock code.
	- Branch: nov18-2026111016332355
	- Commit: 9f1bf48
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests passed.
	- Closed: 20261118-164347

	- ID: 2026111016332342
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed

	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg

	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Run `account apply` with no `~/.gitconfig`, so the rule goes into `~/.config/git/config`. Create `~/.gitconfig`, move the folder from account a to b, and apply again.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: Apply shows no unset, adds b's rule to `~/.gitconfig`, and exits 0. a's rule stays in the other file, so the repo still gets a's email. `account list`'s stale-rule warning misses it too.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Apply finds and replaces its rules in every global file git reads.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23, git 2.51.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: `git config --global --get-regexp` reads only `~/.gitconfig` when it exists, while git reads both.
	- Origin: dfa5d05 and 4918b5b, 2026-08-19. No round saw it. Confirmed.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Note: On git 2.51 the repo took b's email, since git reads ~/.gitconfig last. The keys b leaves unset, such as name, still came from a's fragment through the old rule.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: As guessed. git config --global reads only ~/.gitconfig once it exists, while git reads ~/.config/git/config first and then ~/.gitconfig.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: apply asks git var GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL for every global file, or follows git's rule for a git before 2.42. A file under 2 names, such as ~/.config/git/config linked to ~/.gitconfig, is handled once.
	- Decisions: The other file gets only removals, after the write, so a failure there leaves the new rules in force, and they outrank it where they overlap. The error says that file was left as it was. The fallback for a git before 2.42 ran on no box here (unverified).

- Code Review 20261110b item 15: With GIT_SSH set, the fetch says offline and the pull is skipped
	- ID: 2026111016332268
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261110-163322
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Set `GIT_SSH` to a working ssh program, as PuTTY and TortoiseGit users do, with an ssh origin. Run `gitsby status`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It warns that git fetch failed, maybe offline. The fetch ran PATH's ssh with gitsby's options, since gitsby sets `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, which outranks `GIT_SSH`. The push in the same run uses `GIT_SSH` and works.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: gitsby uses the user's ssh program for fetches and probes.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23, with a logging stand-in for the ssh program.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: remoteEnv in remote.go always sets `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`. A `core.sshCommand` of plink also gets `-o ConnectTimeout=3`, which plink doesn't take. That part is Plausible.
	- Origin: 88ff4ab, 2026-08-19, from v2.1.0. No round saw it. Confirmed.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: remoteEnv exported `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` whenever the caller hadn't, to add the connect timeout. git runs `GIT_SSH` only when no ssh command is set, so the fetch ran PATH's ssh. The identity probe ignored `GIT_SSH` too. A plink `core.sshCommand` got `-o ConnectTimeout=3`, which plink refuses.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: With `GIT_SSH` set and no ssh command, the fetch leaves the environment to git, and the identity probe runs that program. A command git reads as PuTTY's, by name or by `GIT_SSH_VARIANT`, gets no timeout, and the probe leaves its account unknown rather than asking plain ssh. design.md says so under the ssh identity notes.
	- Branch: nov18-2026111016332280
	- Test case: test.bash [dfg2d], [dfg2e], [dfg2j], [dfg2k] and [dfg2m]; TestRemoteEnvLeavesGITSSHToGit [dfg26], TestSSHArgvRunsGITSSH [dfg27], TestRemoteEnvLeavesPuTTYToGit [dfg28].
	- Verified: [dfg2d], [dfg2e], [dfg2j] and [dfg2m] fail on the nov18 build and pass with the fix. [dfg2k] passes on both, and fails with the probe's PuTTY check taken out. [dfg26] to [dfg28] fail against the old remote.go. The plink part is pinned by [dfg28], not run against a real plink, which this box doesn't have. The quick gate passed with every area.
	- Swept: every place gitsby exports or runs an ssh command. remoteEnv covers the fetch, the origin check and the repo probe. The login probe, its look-ahead and the SSH line's key read sshArgv. account.go's sshkey export is left alone: it sets one command that the fetch and the push both use, so they can't disagree. The -G read stays on PATH's ssh, since it reads OpenSSH's config.
	- Decisions: GIT_SSH gets no connect timeout, since adding one takes a GIT_SSH_COMMAND, which outranks it. git config's ssh.variant isn't read, since that costs a process on every run. The test.bash block is skipped on Windows, where a bash script can't be GIT_SSH for the native build. The Go tests cover the logic there, a backslash path included. test.bash now unsets GIT_SSH, GIT_SSH_COMMAND and GIT_SSH_VARIANT, so an inherited one can't steer its checks.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261118-175751
	- Commit: fe582c7

- Code Review 20261110b item 3: A second release after a failed push of main cuts a new tag on the same commit
	- ID: 2026111016332417
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261110-163324
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Make the push of main fail during `gitsby release`, as a hook or branch protection does. Fix that and run `gitsby -q release` again.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The first run leaves tag v1.0.1 local and main ahead. The second sees main ahead, skips the nothing-to-release check, and tags v1.0.2 on the commit named Release v1.0.1. v1.0.2 is pushed, v1.0.1 never is, and it exits 0.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The second run finishes the first: it pushes main and v1.0.1, or says what's left to do.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23, local bare origin with a pre-receive hook.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: release.go:142 treats main being ahead as new work. The tag is made before main is pushed, at release.go:223-237.
	- Origin: 089776d, 2026-08-18, the Go port of a bash fix. Code Review 20260727b item 12 fixed this case, and its tests [dafrk] to [dafrq] cover only a run whose push worked. Regression. Confirmed.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: As the possible cause says. The run that failed also leaves you on main, ahead, so the second run's park push sends main, and then only v1.0.2 goes with it.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: When the default branch's tip holds a release tag and origin's copy is behind it or missing, a bare `release` finishes that release instead of cutting one: it pushes the branch and that tag, fast-forwards dev and pushes it. The plan shows only those steps, and a line says which release it is finishing. Typing that same version does the same. changelog.md has a line under vNEXT.
	- Decisions:
		- Finish rather than refuse, the first of the two outcomes the item allows, since re-running a command is meant to be safe and to get you there.
		- A different version typed out still cuts its own tag, as [dafrq] keeps for a typed version.
		- Any run with no version typed finishes, a candidate's promotion included, since that would also tag the same commit again and leave the candidate behind.
		- A default branch that went its own way from origin's isn't taken as a stuck release, since its push would be refused anyway.
		- A run whose branch push worked and tag push failed is unchanged: main is level, so the nothing-new check stands down and names the tag to push.
	- Swept: the plan (previewRelease) and the `--staged` walk (stagedReleaseCheck), which both now skip dev's pull and the merge on a finish. release.bash refuses an existing tag in phase 1, so it can't cut a second one. Its phase 2 message for a failed `gitsby release` said no tag was cut, which a refused push makes untrue, so it now names `gitsby release <version>` and then `--publish` as the way to finish.
	- Branch: round-20261111
	- Test case: test.bash [df519] [df51a] [df51b] [df51c] [df51d] [df51e] [df51f] [df51g]
	- Verified: [df51a] [df51b] [df51e] fail against the old release.go and pass after. [df519] and [df51d], the refused first runs, and [df51c], dev after the second run, pass on both. [df51g], a candidate left behind, failed on a first version of the fix that keyed on a bump, and passes after. Quick gate passed, every area: test.bash 1975/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261110-213630

- Code Review 20261110b item 5: sync and the park pushes follow push.default, so they push branches the plan never names
	- ID: 2026111016332392
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261110-163323
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Set `push.default=matching`. On a feature branch, with an unpushed commit on local main, run `gitsby -q sync`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The plan says it pushes the feature branch. git pushes the feature branch and main, and it exits 0. That gets past `--direct`. A mirror refspec in `remote.origin.push` could delete branches on origin.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: gitsby pushes only the branch its plan names.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23, local bare origin.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: pushArgs in mutate.go returns a bare `git push` once the branch has an upstream.
	- Origin: 38cc756, 2026-10-04. The bare push is older. No round saw it. Confirmed.
	- Sweep: Every caller of pushArgs: sync, each park, release's 2 pushes, br merge's fallback push, repo connect.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: pushArgs returned a bare `git push`, which follows push.default and remote.origin.push. release's push of dev was a second bare push.
	- Decisions:
		- The push goes where a bare push would send that branch alone. pushRemote and remote.pushDefault still pick the remote, and a push refspec that renames the branch is followed. Fork users keep pushing to their fork.
		- Where git has no one answer, as under push.default=nothing, it goes to the upstream, since the command asks to push.
		- On a mirror remote git refuses a named branch, so the push fails and nothing moves. A `+` in a push refspec no longer forces.
		- A remote name that starts with a dash gets `--` before it, since git takes a remote named `--all`.
		- 1 more git call per push, a for-each-ref that also names the current branch. spawn-count `[df37w]` 37 -> 38 and `[df052]` 42 -> 43. Check: entry filed.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: pushArgs names the remote and `HEAD:<ref>`, read from 1 for-each-ref. release's dev push uses it too. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Swept: every `"push"` in src-go. publishBranch, repo connect's add, the tag push, br merge's atomic push and the deletes already name their refs. pr create and the branch commands park through cmdPush.
	- Test case: Go [df52f], test.bash [df52c] to [df52e]. [df52f] fails 9 of its 10 cases on the old pushArgs, and [df52c] to [df52e] fail against the build before the fix: main went to origin, and the mirror remote lost a branch.
	- Acceptance signoff: Quick gate passed, all areas. gosec has no finding in the changed lines.
	- Closed: 20261110-221524

	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed

	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg

	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: Both pass, exit 0. [dab6x] counts as named since its ID is on the Test case row from when it was added. 1077 of the 1725 IDs it can see are already in the backlog. The fuzz.bash line isn't seen at all, since the check only knows `fAssert*`, `fSame*` and `fOk`.

A removed check has to be named, by its ID as a word or by its label, on a backlog line the merge base's backlog doesn't have.

- Code Review 20261110b item 17: release.bash tests one commit and releases another
	- ID: 2026111016332243
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261110-163322
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: With local dev behind origin's dev, run `cicd/release.bash <version>`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: Phase 1 runs the full pipeline on the local tree. Phase 2's `br create` and `gitsby release` pull dev first, so the tag and the published binaries are origin's commit plus the changelog edit, which nothing tested. Run from a feature branch, it tests that branch. The Notes say it refuses unless you're on the merge target, and nothing checks that.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: It fetches first, refuses unless HEAD is dev and level with origin, and checks after phase 2's pull that dev is still the tested commit.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: No. Read only, since release.bash can't run for real here.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: release.bash:339-343 checks for unpushed commits but never fetches or checks the branch.
	- Origin: 8d108fd, 2026-08-12. The pre-push gate on main still runs on the real commit where it's installed. No round saw it. Plausible.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: As the possible cause says. The pipeline's sync, `br create`, `pr ok` and `gitsby release` each pull, so origin's dev could also move between the run and the tag. The release merge also took in anything main had that dev didn't.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: release.bash fetches, and refuses unless HEAD is the branch `gitsby release` cuts from, level with origin's, and unless origin's main has nothing that branch lacks. After the pipeline it fetches again and refuses a branch origin moved. Phase 2 checks that the version branch starts at the tested commit, and that dev after the merge and the tag each hold the tested tree plus the bump. A stop at the tag publishes nothing.
	- Decisions:
		- The branch is found the way gitsby finds it: dev where the repo has one, else the default branch.
		- After the merge and the tag, trees are compared, not commits, so a merge commit and a squash both pass.
		- `--publish` skips the branch checks, since it builds from the tag, so it no longer needs an upstream.
		- A dry run fetches too, so it refuses what a real run would.
		- The check on main goes past the wording. The release merge would put a commit there that dev lacks into the tag untested.
	- Swept: every pull in phase 2 (`br create`, `pr create`, `pr ok`, `gitsby release`), the header Notes, the phase 3 comment that said nothing checked the tag, and design.md "Automating a release".
	- Branch: round-20261111
	- Test case: test.bash [df4xt] [df4xv] [df4y1] [df4y2] [df4xx] [df4xy] [df4xz] [df4y0]
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261110-195237
	- Verified: [df4xt] [df4xv] [df4y2] [df4xx] [df4xy] [df4xz] [df4y0] fail against the old release.bash and pass after. [df4y1], the control that dev is taken where there is one, passes on both. Quick gate passed, every area: test.bash 1959/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 30/0.

- Code Review 20261109 item 1: A failed `account apply` empties a working account fragment that the global config still includes
	- ID: 2026110912215201
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261109-122152
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]:
		- Run `gitsby account apply` once, so the global config includes an account's fragment.
		- Leave git's lock file beside that fragment, such as `github.com_work.gitconfig.lock`, then run `account apply` again.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It exits 1 with "Couldn't write user.name into '...'; it is incomplete". The fragment is now 0 bytes, and the global includeIf still points at it. Plain git in that folder has no name, email, sshCommand or credential helper until an apply succeeds. A full disk or a permissions error does the same.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A failed apply leaves every fragment the global config includes as it was. The comment above the write says nothing goes into the global config until every fragment is written.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-09 on b23, built binary with a temp HOME, XDG dirs and global git config.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: `writeAccountFragment` (accountcmd.go:534) truncates the fragment first, then writes 1 key per `git config --file` call into it. The config file itself is written to a new file and renamed, but fragments aren't.
	- Origin: accountcmd.go:534 from 353f5c9, 2026-08-19. Code Review 20260818 item 5 added a check on each write, not a safe replace. No earlier round saw this. Confirmed.
	- Notes:
		- Writing the keys into a temp file beside it and renaming that over the fragment keeps the per-key writes the 20261003 round decided to keep.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The fragment was cut to nothing first, then written a key at a time in place. Any failed key left it empty or part written, while the global config still included it.
	- Actual effort: Low
	- Decisions:
		- The keys go into a new file beside the fragment, made 0600 by `os.CreateTemp`, and it is renamed over the fragment once every key is in. On a failure it is removed. Its name ends in `.tmp`, so a crash's leftover is never listed as an unused fragment.
		- A fragment that can't be opened for writing, such as a read-only file or a folder in its place, is still refused before anything is written. A rename would replace it without a word. This keeps the "is a directory" reason `[ddf43]` and `[ddf46]` check.
		- The separate chmod is gone. The new file is always 0600, and `[dbfvv]` still passes.
		- A lock file left beside the fragment no longer stops the run, since git now locks the new file instead.
		- A fragment that is a symlink is replaced by a plain file. gitsby writes these files itself, so a link there isn't expected.
		- Changelog under Fixed.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: `writeAccountFragment` writes to a new file and renames it over the fragment. The refusals say the fragment was left as it was.
	- Branch: round-20261109
	- Commit: b59aab1
	- Test case: `TestAccountApplyFailureKeepsTheFragment` `[df35e]`: a key git won't write, a stale lock beside the fragment, and a folder that takes no new file.
		- Verified: all 3 cases fail on the old code and pass on the fix. The quick gate with every area passed (test.bash 1901/0, fuzz 314/0, parity 30/0).
		- Swept: every other file write in src-go. This was the only in-place write and the only `git config --file`.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests passed.
	- Closed: 20261109-133919

- Code Review 20261109 item 2: Ctrl+C on a cicd.bash run skips its cleanup
	- ID: 2026110912215202
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261109-122152
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: After Ctrl+C the run prints no FAIL step line and no `Cleanup:` line. Its run folder stays, and the container tidy-up doesn't run. `fSweepRuns` removes the folder 2 days later.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The comment at cicd.bash:411 says a stop still runs the exit trap, the container's tidy-up included.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-09. The trap and tee layout was copied into a probe script and SIGINT sent to its process group. The cleanup marker was never written. With the tee started as `>(trap '' INT TERM; exec tee ...)` it was, and the probe exited 130.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: A run with `LINT_LOG_DIR` set tees its output (cicd.bash:1112), and Ctrl+C kills tee too. The exit trap's first line of output then kills bash with SIGPIPE. The bash traps notes list this trap and its fix.
	- Origin: the tee from bbce553, 2026-07-22. The INT trap and its comment from 637c182, 2026-10-25. No earlier round saw this. Confirmed.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual cause [Bug]: As given. Ctrl+C reaches the whole foreground group, so tee died with bash, and the exit trap's first line took SIGPIPE. A TERM to the group does the same.
	- Actual effort: Low
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The run log's tee is started as `>(trap '' INT TERM; exec tee ...)`, so it lives until the exit trap closes its pipe and waits for it.
	- Decisions:
		- The test gives the run a process group of its own with `set -m`, since a background job in a script starts with INT ignored, and bash can't trap it then.
	- Branch: round-20261109
	- Test case: test.bash [df33r]
	- Verified: [df33r] fails on the unfixed cicd.bash, with no FAIL line, no `Cleanup:` line and the run folder left, and passes after, exit 130. `--backlog-run-quick` passed: test.bash 1889/0, fuzz 313/0, parity 30/0.
		- Swept: the only `tee` in the cicd scripts and installers.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its test runs passed.
	- Closed: 20261109-124440

- Code Review 20261109 item 3: Two pipeline steps can pass having checked nothing
	- ID: 2026110912215203
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261109-122152
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]:
		- A full run with `--no-test` never builds, so fuzz.bash, the spawn counts and parity test whatever `src-go/gitsby` is on disk. On a clone with no build, parity prints "nothing to compare, skipping." and the step passes.
		- The native fuzz step gets its targets from `go test -list ... 2>/dev/null | grep '^Fuzz' || true` (cicd.bash:1200). When that fails, the loop runs 0 times and prints "OK: native fuzz targets". fuzz_test.go has 9 targets.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A step with nothing to check fails, or says it was skipped. parity.bash:112 and fuzz.bash:13 both say they test the build stage 2 made. The quick run already builds for this reason (`gateBuilt`, cicd.bash:905-910).
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-09. The fuzz loop, run against a stub `go` that prints a build error, printed OK and exited 0. The `--no-test` path by grep: `fNativeBuild` runs only at cicd.bash:909 and :1174, and the second is inside `if ((doTest))`.
	- Origin: parity's skip from 1928f35, 2026-08-18. The fuzz list from c943c5a, 2026-08-21. No earlier round saw them. Confirmed for the fuzz list, Plausible for the `--no-test` run end to end.
	- Sweep: every cicd.bash step that takes its input from a list or a build that may be missing.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Only the test step and the quick run built, so a full run with `--no-test` left fuzz.bash, the spawn counts and parity on whatever build was on disk. parity.bash passed with no build at all. The native fuzz loop threw away `go test -list`'s exit code and errors, so a failed or empty list ran no target and printed OK.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The fuzz and parity steps build first when no earlier step in the run did, and a run with all three builds once. parity.bash fails with no build, as fuzz.bash and spawn-count.bash already did. The native fuzzing fails, with what go said, when `go test -list` fails, and fails when it lists no target. The plan's "Go build" line shows whenever a step that runs the build is on.
	- Decisions:
		- No build fails parity rather than printing SKIP. A missing build means the run went wrong, and the other two suites already fail on it. A missing frozen build still skips, since the header names that as the end state.
		- An empty fuzz list fails rather than skips. The module has 9 targets, and `[dd5ft]` already wants at least 5.
		- The quick run's `gateBuilt` became the same `nativeBuilt` flag, set by `fNativeBuild`.
	- Swept: every cicd.bash step that reads a list or a build. test.bash, fuzz.bash and spawn-count.bash exit 1 with no build. Lint dies on an empty shell file list, and `[dd5f4]` and `[dd5f6]` pin the markdown and PowerShell globs to the tracked files. CodeQL dies on an empty file list. Dogfood, the demo and the remote tests make their own builds. The leak checks alone, under `--no-fuzz`, need no build.
	- Verified: `--backlog-run-quick`, every area, test.bash 1895/0, fuzz 313/0, parity 30/0. Against the old cicd.bash and parity.bash, `[df340]`, `[df341]`, `[df343]`, `[df344]` and `[df345]` fail and pass after. `[df342]` passes both ways, since it guards against a second build.
	- Verified: a real `--quick --no-test` run with only the fuzz step built first, then fuzzed all 9 targets.
	- Test case: test.bash `[df340]` `[df341]` (the fuzz and parity steps build under `--no-test`), `[df342]` (one build for all three), `[df343]` `[df344]` (a failed or empty fuzz list fails), `[df345]` (parity.bash with no build fails).
	- Branch: round-20261109
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed. Its new checks fail before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261109-125809

- Code Review 20261107 item 1: Two small crypto imports made the binary 25% bigger and slower to start
	- ID: 2026110708000101
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261107-080001
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026100416430451, 2026101916533300
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: `crypto/sha256` in `rawHash` and `crypto/rand` for the accounts lock token pull in Go's whole FIPS crypto module. BSS went from 0.2 MB to 33.8 MB. Max RSS is about 9.3 MB, start time about 2.1 ms.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Size and speed are the top 2 priorities for the binary. Neither value needs crypto strength.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-07 on b23, go1.26.2 linux/amd64. With `hash/fnv` and `math/rand/v2` in their place, the binary is 163,840 bytes smaller, RSS about 7.2 MB, and `--version` starts about 19% faster. Removing only one of the two saves almost nothing.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: Both imports came in with fixes, the lock token and the raw nesting chain.
	- Origin: accountcmd.go:969 from 0738416, 2026-10-04, the fix for 2026100416430451. exec.go:277 from 8e403d5, 2026-10-21, for 2026101916533300. Both after the 20261003 round. A regression in size and speed from 2 correct fixes. Confirmed.
	- Notes:
		- A new hash changes the `GITSBY_RAW_ACTIVE` entries, so a chain that mixes old and new builds won't match. That's acceptable before the first Go release.
		- Needs a numeric gate, such as a cap on binary size and BSS, watched to fail with the imports put back.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual fix [Bug]: `rawHash` uses `hash/fnv` (64a, same 12 hex characters) and the lock token is 2 words from `math/rand/v2`. No `crypto/` package is left in the build. Unstripped data and BSS went from 33.8 MB to 254 KB, the plain build from 6,063,994 to 5,839,550 bytes.
	- Branch: round-20261107b
	- Test case: test.bash `[df024]`, the data and BSS of the unstripped probe build under 2 MB by `go tool nm`, and `[df025]`, no `crypto/` package in `go list -deps`.
	- Verified: both fail on gover's source and pass after. Go tests, test.bash 1826 -> 1833, 0 failed.
	- Closed: 20261107-084700

- The Pillow lock check fails on FreeBSD
	- ID: 2026110610343700
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261106-103437
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]:
		- `--backlog-run-full` at 4e39d4a, to stage 7.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: vmFreeBSD's test.bash fails `[de5av]`, so the remote tests fail, while every other box passes it.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: `[de5av]` passes on every box.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: `grep ... | grep -q "^pillow=="` under pipefail. Pillow is the first of 2 lines the left grep prints, and BSD grep writes a line at a time, so `grep -q` quits before the second write and the left grep exits 141. 9 runs in 10 on vmFreeBSD. GNU grep writes once at exit, so Linux never saw it. PyYAML is the last line, so `[deavy]` passed.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The 2 pipes in `fSysPyFromLock` grep a capture instead. The other pipes into `head` or `grep -q` that run under pipefail read with `sed -n` or a capture too, 9 more in test.bash and 1 in remote-tests.bash. None of those failed yet.
	- Swept: every tracked bash file outside legacy/. A pipe inside a `bash -c` string runs without pipefail, and one ending in `|| true` drops the code, so those stay.
	- Branch: pipe-drain
	- Test case: test.bash `[deyrt]` lists any pipe into `head`, `grep -q` or an awk `exit` that pipefail would see, and fails on one. It flagged all 11 lines before the fix, and a line added to parity.bash after it.
	- Verified: test.bash 1774/0 on b23 and 1380/0 on vmFreeBSD, where it was 1378/1.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed. The new check fails before the fix, and vmFreeBSD passes `[de5av]` after it.
	- Closed: 20261106-104500
