- A `gh` wrapper that calls `gitsby raw gh` still fails, and gitsby's own `gh` calls fail behind it
	- ID: 2026102306584122
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Needs local test suite run?: No. test.bash ran 1667/0.
	- Needs external testing: No. Stage 7 on vmDebARM64 ran them 2026-10-23.
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261023-065841
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026101916533300
	- Target OS: All
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]:
		- Put the wrapper tukzedo used on b28l first on PATH, a `gh` that runs `exec gitsby raw gh "$@"`, with the real `gh` later on PATH.
		- Run `gitsby raw gh --version`, a bare `gh --version`, a script that calls bare `gh`, `gitsby whoami` and `gitsby pr`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]:
		- No loop since 2026101916533300, but every one fails. `raw` refuses with "Looping: ... Unset GITSBY_RAW_ACTIVE to run anyway." `whoami` says gh is not logged in, and `pr` says "'gh pr list' failed".
		- The hint is wrong for a wrapper. Unsetting the variable brings the endless loop back.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]:
		- The wrapper does what it was written for. Every one of those reaches the real `gh`, as the account, after one extra start.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-10-23 on b23, with `private/claude_simple/tools/rawloop-rig.bash`. 2 or 3 wrapper starts each, then the refusal. 6 for `whoami` and `pr`, from their probes.
	- Possible cause [Bug]:
		- `rawNest` refuses when its own entry is already on the chain. That entry means the file it found is what started it, so the file is a wrapper. Passing over that entry and going on down PATH would find the real tool.
	- Requirements [Bug fix]:
		- A `raw` whose entry for a PATH entry is already on the chain passes over that entry and tries the next one. It refuses only when none is left, or past the depth limit.
		- A `raw` started under the probe mark does the same, and hands over with no account work or probes of its own, so probes can't multiply.
		- The refusal drops the advice to unset `GITSBY_RAW_ACTIVE`, or gives it only where it can't loop.
		- Hooks and aliases that call `raw` keep working as the 2026-10-22 decision says.
		- Test case: the wrapper above, with each of those commands reaching the real `gh` and a counted cap on starts. Watch it fail on the current build first.
	- Actual cause [Bug]:
		- As guessed. `rawNest` refused a repeat instead of passing over the file that started it, and a `raw` under the probe mark refused outright, so every probe behind the wrapper failed too.
	- Estimated effort: Avg
	- Actual effort: Avg
	- Progress log:
		- 2026-10-23: The item it follows set out to refuse. The 2026-10-22 answer, "What any sane human git user would expect", points at making a wrapper like this work instead. tukzedo's memory now says never to put such a wrapper on PATH.
		- 2026-10-23: Fixed. `raw` walks PATH per candidate and passes over a tool file whose run, same folder and arguments, is already on the chain, then takes the next one. It refuses only when none is left, or past 16 deep, and no longer says to unset `GITSBY_RAW_ACTIVE`. A `raw` that passed one over, or runs under the probe mark, hands over with no account work or probes.
		- Cost behind the wrapper, in wrapper starts: `raw gh` 2, its probe and the handover. A bare `gh` or a script 3. Each `gh` call gitsby makes 3, so `whoami` and `pr` take 6, as before, but now reach the real `gh`. A wrapper adding an argument each time takes 2 per level and stops at 16 deep, 32 starts, the same as before.
		- Departs from the wording: not "one extra start". Getting there would mean gitsby's own `gh` calls not starting a full `raw` behind the wrapper, for one by having every gitsby mark what it runs the way the probes are marked. That changes hooks under non-raw commands, so it isn't done here.
	- Decisions:
		- Under the probe mark, a tool file on the chain is passed over whatever its arguments. A probe's arguments are gitsby's own, so nothing under it has a reason to run that file again. Matching on the arguments too cost 2 starts a probe, and a drifting wrapper's probes each ran to the depth limit.
		- A chain entry now holds a hash of the tool's path on its own as well as the one over path, folder and arguments.
		- The entry handed over is for the arguments handed over, which `glab auth status` changes.
	- Actual fix [Bug]:
		- `walkTool` in exec.go is `lookTool` with a filter, and `cmdPassthrough` uses it with `rawOnChain`. `rawNest` only adds the entry and keeps the probe mark last.
	- Branch: round-20261023b
	- Test case: test.bash `[de899]`, `[de89a]` and `[de89c]`, reworded to reach the tool, and new `[deatd]` (bare gh), `[deate]` and `[deatf]` (refusal with nothing after it), `[deatg]` (whoami) and `[death]` (pr). Each wrapper quits past 8 starts now, since a gitsby `gh` call takes 3. Go `[de89e]`, `[de8pk]` and `[de8pm]`, reworded.
	- Verified: 2026-10-23, test.bash 1662 -> 1667, 0 failed. On the build before, the 8 reworded and new checks fail. The Go tests fail with the pass-over, the probe file match and the kept probe mark each taken out. The rig shows every one of the five commands reaching the real `gh`, where before each was refused. The hook and alias rig still passes. `GOOS=windows go vet` and the Windows test build, and darwin and freebsd builds, pass.
	- Verified: 2026-10-23, the round's full run. The 8 reworded and new test.bash checks passed in the container, on b26 and on vmFreeBSD, and `[de89e]`, `[de8pk]` and `[de8pm]` in the Go tests on b26, vmFreeBSD and vm925w. test.bash was 1438 of 1439 on b26 and 1341 of 1342 on vmFreeBSD, each 6 more than on 10-22. The one failure on each is `[de5av]`, from 2026102220133673. Go tests: b26 211 ok and 6 skipped, vmFreeBSD 213 ok and 4 skipped, vm925w 195 ok and 23 skipped. The macOS workflow, run 39970887647, passed the same checks on both runners, test.bash 1417 of 1418 with the same one failure. b29w was not reachable. Logs: `/mnt/ext/wip2/wip/tmp/test_gitsby_20261023-07353000/run.log` for the container, `run2.log` beside it for stage 7.
	- Verified: 2026-10-23 on b28l with tukzedo's wrapper and the real `gh`, on the synced build `c917c95`, together with 2026101916533300. Every command in the steps above reached the real `gh` and exited 0. `whoami` took 9 wrapper starts and `pr` 6, the rest 2 or 3.
	- Verified: 2026-10-23, stage 7 on vmDebARM64 alone, on round-20261023d `e2f93e9`. The 8 reworded and new test.bash checks passed, and `[de89e]`, `[de8pk]` and `[de8pm]` in the Go tests for linux/arm64 and for windows/arm64 under Wine. Go tests 218 ok and 2 skipped, and 190 ok and 30 skipped under Wine. test.bash failed 23 checks of the remote harness and stopped there, all from the narrowed host lists, filed as 2026102321011743. Log: `/mnt/ext/wip2/wip/tmp/gitsby/20261023-200002/001/run.log`.
	- Swept: `rawActive` and `rawNest` have one caller, `cmdPassthrough`, which every `raw` tool shares. `findTool` and its cache are unchanged for every other spawn. README names no refusal text. design.md's `raw` bullet updated.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed 2026-10-24. The behavior changed from the expected "one extra start" to 2 or 3 per `gh` call. Each is a short Go start, and getting to one would change hooks under every command, against the 2026-10-22 decision.
	- Closed: 20261024-133500

- test.bash's goleak check `[de54n]` fails on macOS, since BSD find has no `-printf`
	- ID: 2026102220274491
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Needs external testing: No
	- Priority|Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261022-202744
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026102218410000
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]:
		- Run `cicd/test.bash` on a Mac whose `find` is the system one.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: `[de54n]` fails. The first macOS workflow run, 39893939993 on `macos-latest` (arm64), passed 1411 and failed only that one.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: It passes whenever every folder with Go tests calls `goleak.VerifyTestMain(m)`, on any OS.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: Yes, 2026-10-22 on b23, with a stand-in `find` on PATH that refuses `-printf` the way BSD find does. The check failed.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The check listed test folders with `find ... -printf '%h\n'`. BSD find has no `-printf`, so it printed nothing. The loop then counted 0 folders and failed.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The folder is cut off the file path with `sed`, then `sort -u`. Same folders as before on b23, and the check still fails when one package lacks goleak. New check `[dea6f]` fails if a `find` with `-printf` or `-fprintf` comes back into test.bash or install.bash.
	- Swept: `find -printf`, `sed -i` without a suffix, `grep -P`, `readlink -f`, `date -d`, `date +%N`, `stat -c`, `sort -V`, `xargs -r`, `realpath -m`, `tar --transform`, `wc -l` compared as text, `\?` and `\t` in sed, in cicd/*.bash, cicd/utility/*.bash, cicd/utility/include/*.bash and install.bash. In test.bash, only `[de54n]` used one where a Mac runs it. The bare `sed -i` and `date +%N` sit in the Linux-only release and pre-push blocks, and so do the `wc -l` compares and the remote-tests checks that run `tar --transform`. `date -d` runs behind a probe for GNU date. `stat` falls back to BSD's. The rest are in Linux-only cicd.bash, in keep-build.bash's `--keep` path, which test.bash doesn't run, and in the `--help` text of backlog-check, test-id and lint-report, where BSD sed would leave the tab in the printed help.
	- Verified: 2026-10-22, with BSD-like find, `[de54n]` fails on the old test.bash and passes on the new one. It passes on a stand-in tree and fails once one package there drops goleak. `[dea6f]` fails on the old test.bash and passes on the new one. `cicd.bash --gate` and `backlog-check.bash` passed.
	- Verified: 2026-10-22, test.bash on b23 1662/0, 1661 -> 1662.
	- Not checked: why `[de54n]` passed in stage 7 on b26 and vmFreeBSD. Likely a GNU find first on b26's PATH, and a FreeBSD find that has `-printf`.
	- Test case: test.bash `[de54n]` itself on the Mac runners, and `[dea6f]`, which needs no Mac.
	- Branch: fix-macos-find
	- Commit: 0d01f82
	- Verified: 2026-10-22, run 39895628537: `[de54n]` and `[dea6f]` passed on `macos-15-intel` and `macos-latest`. Both had failed `[de54n]` in run 39893939993.
	- Acceptance signoff: Passed its own test on both runners, no open choice.
	- Closed: 20261022-203900

	- Note: 2 ways out. Reword workflows.md to say gitsby steers work onto branches and still allows a deliberate commit on `main` or `dev`. Or warn above the prompt when the push goes to `main` or `dev`. Refusing is out, since the tool's own advice and every repo with no `dev` lean on it.
	- Note: The reword is the smaller change. A warning would show on every push in a GitHub Flow repo that commits to `main`.
	- Progress log:
		- 2026-10-05: The fix chosen is a warning on stderr before going ahead, with a flag to turn it off.
		- 2026-10-05: The flag is `--direct`. `-q` without it refuses, per the UI style guide's rule for warnings, since the question about `-q` went unanswered.
		- 2026-10-05: Warning reworded as given in review. The `-q` refusal starts with the same sentences.
	- Decisions:

	- Actual fix [Bug]: `sync` on `main`, `dev` or the default branch warns on stderr above the prompt when it would push commits made on that branch, or commit a dirty tree there. Under `-q` it refuses and names `--direct`. A merge left for `sync` to publish doesn't count, so `br merge` offline and the hotfix back-merge still publish without it. workflows.md, the README, design.md and the UI style guide say so.

- test.bash's binary checks fail on macOS
	- ID: 2026100409453279
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority|Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261004-094532
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026100312332924
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: On b26 `tr -d '\000'` stops with "Illegal byte sequence" on a binary file. So `[dd5fe]` and `[dbftv]` fail, and `[dd5ff]` and `[dbftx]`, which expect no match, pass without reading anything.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The four checks read the file on macOS as they do on Linux.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: Yes, 2026-10-04, in stage 7's run on b26, where ssh gets `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`, and again by hand on the `.syso` files.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: macOS `tr` and `grep` both check bytes against the locale. With `LC_ALL=C` on both, the copyright check found its string on b26. On the `tr` alone it still failed.
	- Origin: the `tr` lines, from 5eadb03 (2026-10-01, the macOS pass, which swapped out `grep -P`) and 7846d29 (2026-09-26). Not seen by an earlier round. Confirmed.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual cause [Bug]: macOS `tr` and `grep` check bytes against the locale, and ssh there gets a UTF-8 one. `tr` stopped at the first byte that wasn't text. The two checks expecting no match passed because nothing was read.
	- Actual effort: Low
	- Progress log:
		- Verified: on b26 the old checks fail two and pass two without reading. The new ones pass all four.
		- Verified: the new `[ddg8y]` fails against the old way of reading and passes with the helper.
		- Verified: test.bash on Linux, 1399 -> 1400, all passing.
		- Verified: stage 7 run alone passes on b26 and vm925w. test.bash on b26 is 1216/0.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The four checks go through one helper in test.bash that runs `tr` and `grep` in the C locale. It tells a string not found apart from a file not read, so the two no-match checks fail when the read fails.
	- Note: the two no-match checks moved from `fAssertFail` to `fAssert`. They keep their IDs and labels.
	- Swept: every `tr` and `grep` in `cicd/` that reads a binary file. Only these four did. The icon check `[dbftw]` already had `LC_ALL=C`, and the `od` reads of Mach-O headers don't depend on the locale.
	- Branch: remfix
	- Commit: 6842035
	- Test case: test.bash `[dbftv]`, `[dbftx]`, `[dd5fe]` and `[dd5ff]`, plus the new `[ddg8y]`.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, and the checks fail before and pass after on b26.
	- Closed: 20261004-103900

- Code Review 20261003 item 2: A pipeline reader that quits early can fail its writer
	- ID: 2026100313123865
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority|Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 2026-10-03
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]:
		- release.bash's proof step pipes `--version` into `grep -q`. Now and then grep quits first and the check fails. That costs two retries and can end in a false warning that the release didn't verify.
		- `tag --sort ... | head -n 1` in release.bash and gen-winres.bash fails the same way once there are enough tags.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Capture the output first, then match it, the way cicd.bash already does.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: The proof step failed 1 run in 300. The tag lookup failed every time with 3000 tags, never with today's 6.
	- Origin: release.bash:132 and :333 from 1928f35 (2026-08-18), gen-winres.bash:100 from cf5922e (2026-08-19). Same class as the Bash trap on early-exit readers. Confirmed for the proof step, Plausible at today's tag count.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: `head -n 1` and `grep -q` stop reading at the first match. A writer with more to say than a pipe holds then fails writing the rest, and `pipefail` fails the pipeline.
	- Sweep: also `spawn-report.bash:53` and `install.bash:196`.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The tag lists and the proof's `--version` are captured whole and then matched, the way cicd.bash reads the tags. The installer and spawn-report.bash take their first lines with `sed -n`, which reads to the end.
	- Swept: release.bash:132 and :333, gen-winres.bash:100, spawn-report.bash:53 and install.bash:196, all fixed. Left alone, since `|| true` keeps the right value there: install.bash's wget redirect read, cicd.bash's tool version read and parity.bash's diff excerpts. Found by a grep for `| head`, `| grep -q` and `| awk ... exit` over every `.bash` outside `legacy/`. test.bash's `| grep -q` runs inside `bash -c`, which has no pipefail.
	- Verified: all five checks fail on `gover` and pass here. test.bash passes 1280 of 1280 with both fixes in.
	- Branch: relpipe
	- Commit: 76675b3
	- Test case: in test.bash, [ddf3s] for a published binary whose `--version` outruns a pipe, [ddf3t] and [ddf3v] for 3000 tags, [ddf3w] for a long SHA256SUMS, and [ddf3x] for 1000 spawn recordings.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, the checks fail before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261003-141543

- Two account blocks with one name merge without a word
	- ID: 2026093013034093
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority|Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 2026-09-30
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]:
		- Write `account: t00mietum` twice, one block with `host: gitea.com` and one with `host: github.com`.
		- Run `gitsby account list --config` on that file.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: One account is listed, with a mix of both blocks' values. Nothing says a block was merged.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The clash is reported, the same way an unread key is.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: Yes, 2026-09-30.
	- Actual cause [Bug]:
		- SHCL merges two blocks with the same name on purpose. It is how a key gets added further down.
		- gitsby read each repeated key last-wins and said nothing. Names differing only in case, and a dotted line beside a block, merged the same way.
		- `account set` edited the first block even when a later one held the key.
		- The 2.x flat reader had the same silent last-wins.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual effort: Avg
	- Decisions:
		- Merging stays, since the format allows it. What gets reported is a key given two different values.
		- The last line is still read, as before. Each earlier one is listed as ignored, with its line.
		- A repeated top-level `protocol` is listed the same way.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: Repeated keys are checked per account after the whole file is read, in both layouts. `account set` edits the block holding the key, and refuses when more than one does.
	- Branch: dup-acct
	- Test case: TestRepeatedAccountKeys, TestAccountSetFindsTheKeyInAnyPiece, and one account list check in test.bash.
	- Closed: 2026-09-30

- Convert config files from every earlier version
	- ID: 2026110707345874
	- Type: Task
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261107-073458
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Milestone: Pre-next-cut.
	- Related IDs: 2026100312145843, 2026100313483664
	- Requirements [Feature]:
		- Make sure this executable version can import their config files to the new shcl version format, from all previous versions, even the old scripts.
		- Rename the old one or ones and leave them in place.
	- Notes:
		- 2026100312145843 converts SHCL 2.x files and renames the old one. A 1.x file is read as 2.x, which wasn't run.
		- The v2.1.0 bash and pwsh scripts hand-parse flat `key = value` lines from a file with the same name. It has no `Format` line and no 2.x footer, so the Go build reads it as current and doesn't convert it. Not tried yet.
		- v2.1.0 looked in `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, then `~/.config`, then `%APPDATA%`, on every OS. The Go build looks only in `%APPDATA%` on Windows and `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS, so an old file in `~/.config` there isn't found. details.md calls that an accepted cost. This item reverses it.
		- A file from the old shcl 3 pseudo-version pin also says Format 3, so it can't be told apart. Check whether anything it wrote reads differently now.
	- Actual fix [Task]: `load` in config.go converts a flat file whose every line v2.1.0 could read, through `flatToSHCL` and `replaceOldFormat`, the path a 2.x file takes. The old file is kept as `config_backup_<date>-<time>_format-flat.shcl`, and `reportMigration` names both on File and From lines. `configCandidatesFor` adds `~/.config/gitsby/config.shcl` last on Windows and macOS. accounts.md, design.md, README.md and the vNEXT changelog say so. parity.bash runs the frozen build first in `fSameLead` and writes its flat fixtures again per check.
	- Decisions:
		- A v2.1.0 file has no `Format` line and no 2.x footer, and every line is blank, a comment, or `key = value` with `protocol` or an `account.<name>.<key>` key v2.1.0 took. That is `wholeFlat` in config.go. A key it refused, such as `account.../x.path`, or a line with no `=`, keeps the file as it is. The ignored list names that line, and the first `account set` rewrites the file, as before.
		- The backup is named `_format-flat`, since the layout had no SHCL format number.
		- Where the file can't be replaced, the run reads it the v2.1.0 way and `account set` refuses, as for a 2.x file.
		- On Windows and macOS, `~/.config` is read after the platform's own place, so a new file still goes in the platform's place. A file found in `~/.config` is converted where it is and stays there. This reverses the accepted cost in details.md and in design.md's "lives where the platform in hand keeps one". Both now say so. `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` stays Linux and BSD only, per design.md.
		- A file from the old shcl 3 pin reads differently in 1 case. Built at 958fac2^, on shcl b10c200, `account set work name "O'Brien \ x"` wrote `name: "O'Brien \\ x"`, since a value with an apostrophe goes in double quotes with each backslash doubled. v3.0.0-beta1 reads both backslashes as text. Plain, single-quoted, `#` and space values read the same. Both say Format 3, so it isn't converted here. Filed as 2026110710480989.
		- The flat fixtures of other checks now convert on first read. test.bash `[db00e]` and `[dcmey]` named keys the flat way, and `[db010]` and `[dbfh2]` dropped an account by its flat lines. All 4 are commented out, with replacements below. The fixtures `[db62z]` and `[db01q]` add to are written in the SHCL spelling. In the Go tests, 4 cases of `[dbjjn]`, a case each of `[dcmfa]` and `[ddav1]`, and the plan's `converts` check in `[dd83m]` and `[dbss1]` are commented out, with the new expectations beside them.

- Code Review 20261107 enhancement 2: Every non-GitHub ssh remote costs an extra `ssh -G`
	- ID: 2026110708000113
	- Type: Enhancement
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261107-080001
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Requirements [Feature]:
		- `remoteTarget` at remote.go:338 calls `parseRemote`, which resolves the ssh alias, when it only needs owner and name. It runs from the status and whoami Account line through `convertibleToHTTPS`.
		- Parsing the text alone takes 1 spawn off each of status 18, whoami 14, pr create 34, repo url 9 and sync 29, with status output byte for byte the same.
		- `resolveSSHHost` and `readSSHConfig` also ask `ssh -G` separately about the same host. One cached read could answer both.
	- Origin: remote.go:338 from 3d22222, 2026-08-17. The 20261003 round measured no non-GitHub remote. Confirmed for the first, Plausible for the second.
	- Notes:
		- A fix lowers the spawn-count limits for these commands in the same commit, adding rows for a Gitea ssh folder if there are none.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual fix [Enhancement]: `remoteTarget` reads owner and name from the text alone, through the new `parseRemoteText`, and asks ssh nothing. `parseRemote` resolves the alias by asking about the connect target, `git@gh-acme` in place of `gh-acme`, the same target the SSH line reads. `sshConfigText` keeps each `ssh -G` answer for the run, keyed by target and PATH and locked like `toolCache`, so `resolveSSHHost` and `readSSHConfig` share one read.
		- Spawn counts, before and after, in a new Gitea ssh folder with an account, a fake tea and a push URL on the local origin: status 18 -> 16, whoami 14 -> 12, repo url 9 -> 8, pullcom 29 -> 27, pr create 39 -> 37. Every GitHub row is the same as before: status 11, whoami 7, repo url 6, pullcom 21, status in an account folder 19, whoami there 15, the https folder 15.
	- Decisions:
		- The alias lookup asks about `user@host`, as git connects. `ssh -G` gives the same hostname for both unless a `Match user` block applies, and then the connect target is the right answer.
		- The cache is package level, like `toolCache`, since both callers are plain functions and nothing in a run writes ssh_config. HOME is left out of the key: ssh reads its config from the passwd home, and `[dbfvy]` allows one HOME read.
		- test.bash `[dd5cb]` is commented out. It pinned the bare alias in the lookup, `-G -- gh-acme`, which this change drops on purpose. `[df054]` checks the one read and its `--`.
		- The new spawn-count rows have the after counts as their limits. A rise of 2 is inside the headroom, so the Go test and `[df054]` are what fail on the old code.
	- Branch: round-20261107b
	- Test case:
		- Go `[df053]` TestSSHConfigAskedOnce: with a logging fake ssh, `remoteTarget` asks ssh nothing, and `parseRemote` twice plus `readSSHConfig` ask `ssh -G` once.
		- test.bash `[df054]`: status on an aliased remote asks `ssh -G` once, as `-G -- git@gh-acme`.
		- spawn-count.bash `[df04s]`, `[df04t]`, `[df04v]`, `[df051]`, `[df052]`: status, whoami, repo url, pullcom and pr create in the tea ssh folder.
	- Verified: `[df053]` fails on HEAD's githost.go, remote.go, account.go and show.go, with 1 call from `remoteTarget` and 4 in all, and passes after. The old build asks `ssh -G` 3 times for status on the aliased remote, the new one once, so `[df054]` fails then passes. Status output is byte for byte the same between the 2 builds for `git@github.com` and for the alias. Go tests pass, test.bash 1850/0, fuzz 313/0, parity 30/0, lint passed, spawn-count passed.
	- Swept: every `ssh -G` and every `parseRemote` caller. `remoteOwner`, `authHost` and the tea login match need the resolved host, and keep it. `sshLineAsks` and `sshTarget` start no process.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests passed.

- Code Review 20261107 enhancement 1: `encoding/json` costs 344 KB for 2 glab reads
	- ID: 2026110708000112
	- Type: Enhancement
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261107-080001
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Requirements [Feature]:
		- pr.go:285 and :314 decode `glab mr list` and `glab mr view` with `encoding/json`. Stubbing those 2 calls takes 344,064 bytes off linux/amd64, 8.2% of the binary, and about the same on Windows and macOS. Start time doesn't change.
		- Read the 3 fields some other way, or ask glab for an output format that needs no JSON parser.
	- Origin: pr.go:13 from 197677f, 2026-10-22, the glab path. After the 20261003 round. Confirmed, measured on top of item 1's change.
	- Notes:
		- With item 1, this accounts for 507,904 of the 847,872 bytes the binary grew since 2026-10-03. Most of the rest is the shcl v3 module.
	- Estimated effort: Avg
	- Actual fix [Enhancement]: A small reader in pr.go takes `iid`, `state` and `source_branch` from glab's JSON, at the top level only, in any key order, with spacing and escapes decoded. Nested values are stepped over, so the author's `state` never counts. Invalid JSON reads as no answer, as before. linux/amd64 with the pipeline's flags went from 4,022,398 to 3,686,526 bytes, 335,872 or 8.4% less. windows/amd64 4,226,560 to 3,890,176, darwin/amd64 4,013,216 to 3,671,440.
	- Decisions:
		- The hand reader, over glab's text output. glab 1.53 takes only `text` or `json` for `mr list` and `mr view`. `mr view`'s text form has had `source_branch` only in recent releases, and `mr list`'s is a table for people. The JSON is the GitLab API's own object, the stable choice.
		- An `iid` that is missing or not a whole number now reads as no PR. encoding/json gave 0 for a missing one, so `pr create` could have said PR #0 was open.
	- Branch: round-20261107b
	- Test case:
		- Go `[df04m]` TestReadGlabMR: key order, spacing, a nested state, escaped quotes and commas, `\u` escapes and a surrogate pair, the first of a list, an empty list, and 15 kinds of bad input, deep nesting among them.
		- Go `[df04n]` FuzzReadGlabMR: encoding/json is the reference in the test, and both agree on whether an object reads and on the 3 fields.
		- test.bash `[df04p]` pr ok reads glab's state past a nested author state, keys out of order. `[df04q]` a source branch with an escaped quote and a comma comes through whole. `[df04r]` no encoding/json in `go list -deps`, in the style of `[df025]`.
	- Verified: `[df04r]` fails on a copy of src-go with HEAD's pr.go and passes after. The fuzz target ran 60 s with no difference found. Every existing glab check passes. Go tests pass, test.bash 1847 -> 1850 with 0 failed, fuzz 313/0, parity 30/0, lint passed.
	- Swept: `go list -deps` for other encoding packages and reflect-heavy ones. Only encoding/hex is left, and reflect comes in through fmt. No other non-test Go file imported encoding/json.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests passed.
	- Closed: 20261107-101500

	- Requirements [Feature]:
		- The parent's second requirement: Go's module cache in the `gitsby-cicd-cache` volume pruned of what the current `go.sum` doesn't name.
	- Notes:
		- The volume is shared by every worktree's runs, and another branch's `go.sum` may name other versions. A prune could take a module from under a run in progress. Prune only when no other gitsby run's container is up, which only the run out here can see.
		- Keep the `golang.org/toolchain` modules for the `toolchain` line in go.mod, which `go.sum` doesn't name, and the `/go.mod`-only entries it does.
		- test.bash builds the SHCL 2.x build offline from the cache ([ddg6f]), so check that every module it needs is in `go.sum`.
		- Module paths in the cache spell capitals as `!` plus the lower case letter, and go makes the files read-only.
	- Progress log:
		- 2026-11-06: At the end of a run in the image that passed, with no gitsby run's container up, a container of its own with no network takes every module version `src-go/go.sum` doesn't name out of the volume's module cache, downloads and extracted trees both. It keeps the toolchain for go.mod's `toolchain` line, or its `go` line where there's none. The end line counts the versions that went. The first run took out the old `yottacore/shcl/source/go/v2` pseudo-version.

- Leak, memory, and correctness checks in CICD
	- ID: 2026101816064794
	- Type: Enhancement
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Needs external testing: Done 2026-10-19. A full run passed stage 7 on b26, vmFreeBSD, vmDebARM64 and vm925w.
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Avg
	- Opened: 20261018-160647
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Milestone: Pre-next-cut.
	- Related IDs: 2026101816064793, 2026101009380628
	- Requirements [Feature]:
		- For all code:
			- The checks cover first-party and third-party code. Vendored code is included.
				- On third-party code, run the leak, memory, and correctness checks named here, not style lints. Style findings in someone else's module aren't ours to fix.
				- CodeQL reports only on source inside the database's root. For its run, vendor the dependencies into the tree first (`go mod vendor`, unpacked sdists for Python).
			- Any report fails the test that made it.
			- Any leak is fixed. If the fix has to wait, it gets a backlog item, and the test that shows it turns the check off with that item's ID beside it.
			- A `--leakcheck` flag adds the slow checks:
				- CodeQL, from a pinned CLI run locally. No hosted service.
				- A soak test. It loops through the program's main actions headless, and fails if the heap at round 2N is larger than at round N by more than a set margin. The heap report is kept as a pipeline artifact.
			- Every tool is pinned and runs in the build container or lint image, never installed on the host.
			- Each new gate is watched to fail before it's trusted, by planting the leak it's meant to catch and seeing it go red.
			- Known-advisory scans run on every full run: `govulncheck` and `pip-audit`. They cover third-party code only, which is the point.
		- For Go:
			- Go leaks are goroutines that never exit, and references held too long: a map or slice that only grows, or a small slice keeping a big backing array alive.
			- Every package's tests run `goleak.VerifyTestMain(m)` from `go.uber.org/goleak`, pinned in go.mod. A goroutine still running after the tests fails the run, whether our code or a dependency started it.
			- Every full run runs the whole test suite with `-race`.
			- If the code uses cgo, every full run also runs the tests with `-asan`, in a build dir of its own.
			- Every full run runs `go vet` and `staticcheck`. `go vet`'s `lostcancel` and `copylocks` checks are the leak-related ones.
			- The soak test reads `runtime.MemStats.HeapInuse` and `runtime.NumGoroutine()` at round N and 2N, after `runtime.GC()`. Its heap profile (`pprof`) is kept as the artifact, and `go tool pprof -base` shows what grew.
			- Traps:
				- `goleak.VerifyNone` per test doesn't work with `t.Parallel()`. Use `VerifyTestMain`.
				- goleak ignores by function name. That's the only form of suppression allowed.
				- `go test` caches a pass. Run with `-count=1`.
				- One `runtime.GC()` can leave garbage behind. Call it twice before reading the stats, or the margin has to be wide enough to hide a real leak.
				- `-race` needs cgo on some platforms. A job with `CGO_ENABLED=0` fails to build it or skips it, so check the job's env.
				- `-race` is 2 to 20 times slower and uses 5 to 10 times the memory. Size the job's timeout for it.
		- For Python:
			- Python leaks are references held too long: module-level caches, `functools.lru_cache` on a method, closures kept in a global list, and C extensions that drop a reference count.
			- Every full run runs the tests with `-X dev` and `-W error::ResourceWarning`, so an unclosed file or socket fails the test.
			- Every full run runs the tests under `pytest-memray`. Each test that loops gets `@pytest.mark.limit_leaks(...)` with a margin. memray sees native allocations, so leaks in C extensions show up, third-party ones included.
			- After the tests, `gc.collect()` runs, and `gc.garbage` must be empty.
			- The soak test takes `tracemalloc` snapshots at round N and 2N and fails on growth past the margin. The top lines of `snapshot.compare_to()` are kept as the artifact.
			- ruff runs `B019` (`lru_cache` on a method), `SIM115` (`open` with no context manager), and `B006` (mutable default argument).
			- `--leakcheck` also runs the tests on a CPython built with `--with-address-sanitizer`, under `PYTHONMALLOC=malloc`, for C extensions.
				- The interpreter's own reports are suppressed by library name, `libpython` only.
			- Traps:
				- Start `tracemalloc` before importing the code under test, or allocations made at import aren't traced.
				- The first rounds fill caches: the regex cache, interned strings, freelists, and lazy imports. That's why it's round N against 2N, never 0 against N.
				- `tracemalloc` sees only allocations made through Python's allocator. A C extension calling `malloc` directly is invisible to it. memray covers that.
				- memray runs on Linux and macOS only. On Windows, the test exits as skipped, not passed.
				- pytest keeps the traceback of a failed test, which keeps its frames alive. A leak count from a run with failures means nothing.
				- `ResourceWarning` shows only in dev mode or with `-W`. A plain run hides it.
				- Without `PYTHONMALLOC=malloc`, ASan can't see inside pymalloc's pools.
	- Note: The Rust, C, and C++ parts of the list were left out, since there's no code in those here. The only Python is the demo gif script, which uses Pillow, cairo, Pango, and fontTools, and it has no tests yet. The Go code starts one goroutine (`startAhead` in app.go), and builds use `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
	- Progress log:
		- 2026-10-19: Everything but CodeQL is in, on `leakchk`. CodeQL is the part left. `fLeakCheck` in cicd.bash marks where it joins.
		- 2026-10-19: Already there, so not added again: every full run had `go test -race`, `go vet` with its default analyzers, `lostcancel` and `copylocks` among them, and `staticcheck`. Only the builds set `CGO_ENABLED=0`. The image has gcc, so the race detector works there, and a planted data race failed it.
		- 2026-10-19: Not applicable: `-asan`, since nothing imports "C". The test-time Python checks (`-X dev`, pytest-memray, `gc.garbage`, the tracemalloc soak, and an ASan CPython) wait until the demo script has tests to run them on.
		- 2026-10-19: CodeQL is in, on `codeql`. `--leakcheck` runs it in the image over a scratch copy of the module, with `go mod vendor` done there. The Go extractor leaves out tests and vendor/ by default, so both are turned on. It runs once for each OS a release is built for, since the extractor sees one OS's files at a time.
		- 2026-10-19: CodeQL found 2 problems in shcl 2.0.0, the old writer the tests use. Both are set aside until 2026101906343987.
		- 2026-10-19: Split out: CodeQL over the demo script and its Python libraries, as 2026101907065426.
		- 2026-10-19: A source check now stops any tracked script or Go file from running tmux, pkill or killall.
	- Decisions:
		- The soak test is a Go test, `TestSoak`, run in one process. It loops pullcom, br create, sync, br merge, status, br, whoami and br prune against a bare origin and a clone, 30 rounds and then 30 more. It skips unless `GITSBY_SOAK_ROUNDS` is set, so a plain `go test` doesn't run it. The heap margin is 256 KB; 2 reads differ by under 100 KB, on a heap under 2 MB.
		- pip-audit checks the demo's libraries at the versions installed, given as pins, since they come from Debian's archive and not pip. Debian patches them without moving the upstream version, so the 18 advisories reported today are set aside in config.bash until 2026101905585018 checks them. A new one fails the run.
		- ruff and pip-audit go into the image from a lock that pins every wheel by hash.
		- CodeQL goes in the default image, not one of its own. The Go-only bundle adds about 400 MB on disk to a 2.6 GB image, and a second image would need its own tag, build and cleanup.
		- On vendor/, only findings from queries tagged security, correctness or reliability count. The rest of the suite is style, such as a value assigned and never read.
		- A finding is set aside by rule and file in `CODEQL_IGNORE`, with its backlog item beside it. An entry no report has any more fails the run.
		- `--leakcheck --no-container` stops on a box without CodeQL rather than skipping it, since it was asked for by name.
	- Branch: leakchk, codeql
	- Test case: `TestMain` [de545] runs goleak, and `TestSoak` is [de546]. test.bash [de547], [de548], [de549], [de54a], [de54h], [de54j], [de54b] and [de54c] for `--leakcheck`. [de54d] and the ruff pass of [dcmap] for ruff. [de54e], [de54g] and [de54k] for pip-audit and `govulncheck -test`. [de54m] for `-count=1`, [de54n] for goleak in every Go package, and [de54f] for the image tag. [de55e], [de55f], [de55g], [de55h], [de55j] and [de55k] for the CodeQL step, and [de55x] for its install. [de55m], [de55n], [de55p], [de55q], [de55r], [de55s], [de562], [de55t], [de563] and [de55v] for how its reports are read. [de55w] for tmux, pkill and killall.
	- Verified:
		- A goroutine left running in `startAhead` failed the unit tests through goleak. In the soak test, a goroutine left per run failed it on the count, and a 4 KB slice kept per run failed it on the heap, where `go tool pprof -base` named `run`. Each was restored by copy, and both pass after.
		- ruff failed on a planted B019, SIM115 and B006, and `--gate` stopped on it. pip-audit failed in the image with one advisory taken off the list.
		- test.bash 1524 -> 1540, 0 failed. The 16 new checks all failed against gover's cicd.bash and config.bash. A full container run with `--leakcheck` passed, with sync, dogfood, the demo, the remote tests and publish off.
		- A planted `n == n` in app.go failed `--leakcheck` in the image, on CodeQL's comparison-of-identical-expressions query. Turning off the extractor's test option failed it too. Both were restored by copy, and the run passes after.
		- test.bash 1540 -> 1560, 0 failed. The new checks all failed against gover's cicd.bash, config.bash and Dockerfile, or against a broken copy of codeql-findings.py. The kill check failed on `pkill` and `tmux` lines planted in a script, a `tmux` line in a Go file, and a `killall` line in legacy/bin/gitsby.
		- A full container run with `--leakcheck` passed, with sync, dogfood, the demo, the remote tests and publish off: test.bash 1560/0, fuzz.bash 313/0, parity 29/0, the spawn counts, the soak test and CodeQL on all 4 OSes.
	- Swept: The comments in cicd.bash and test.bash that said there were no third-party dependencies, the 2 "pure stdlib" lines in config.bash, the style guide's goroutine rule, the help header, both history footers, README and contributing.md. install.bash's "pure Go with no dependencies" is about what a build needs installed first, and goleak is test-only, so it stays. remote-tests.bash runs compiled test binaries, which never cache, so it needs no `-count=1`.

		- Verified: after the reboot the kernel line has it, the kernel no longer reports branch protection, and the CPU flags no longer list it.
		- Verified: that was the cause. Wine's first-run setup finished in about 90 seconds, and `gitsby.exe --version` printed the version in 1 second.

- Pipeline test for converting old SHCL settings files
	- ID: 2026100313483664
	- Type: Enhancement
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority [Feature]: Avg
	- Opened: 2026-10-03
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026100312145843
	- Requirements  [Feature]:
		- As part of CICD, create settings files in the older SHCL format versions.
		- Test the automatic conversion on them, the one gitsby does on first run with no help from shcl.
	- Notes:
		- Today's checks feed in hand-typed 2.x text.
	- Progress log:
		- Done: test.bash compiles the last gitsby build on SHCL 2.x from its commit (53a6231), and has it write an accounts file with `account set`. The current build has to convert that file, list every account the way the old build did, and keep the old file byte for byte. A fuzz target writes values through the 2.x module itself and checks each reads the same after the conversion.
		- Note: nothing is downloaded at test time. The 2.x module is a test-only require in go.mod, so the lint and unit test stages put it in the module cache, and the old build compiles from there with the proxy off. - The ssh identity probe and the ssh -G read cut a bracketed IPv6 host in an ssh:// origin at its first colon
	- ID: 2026112111542213
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261121-115422
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026112020462137
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Point origin at ssh://git@[::1]:2222/o/r.git. Run gitsby status.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: sshTarget gives '[' as the host, so the probe asks ssh about git@[ and the SSH line reads no config. sshPort gives no port either.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The probe and the ssh -G read ask about ::1 on port 2222, as git's fetch does.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: sshTarget, sshConnectTarget and sshPort in remote.go split the authority at its first colon, with no case for brackets.
	- Origin: Plausible, read only. Found while working 2026112020462137.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-21, [dfkyf] fails on the unfixed remote.go: sshTarget gave '[' and sshDest gave '--', 'git@['. Confirmed.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: sshTarget and sshPort cut the authority at its first colon, so a bracketed IPv6 host ended at '[' and its port was lost.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: A new sshURLHostPort reads the authority once for both. A bracketed host keeps its colons and loses the brackets, and only a ':' after the ']' starts the port. sshConnectTarget and sshDest take it through those two.
	- Branch: nov21-2026112111542213
	- Test case: Go [dfkyf], the bracketed rows of TestSSHTarget and TestSSHDestCarriesThePort.
	- Verified: [dfkyf] fails on the unfixed code and passes after. The quick gate passed for lint and unit.

	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261121-115917

- Stage 0 brings staged edits back unstaged after a merge that goes in clean
	- ID: 2026112110520434
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261121-105204
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026112017135488, 2026112017135764
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Stage an edit and edit the file again, on a tree behind or diverged from origin, where the merge goes in clean. Run stage 0.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The edits come back, but the index no longer holds the staged copy.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Staged edits stay staged, as they do when fSyncMerge backs a merge out, and as the publisher keeps them since 2026112017135488.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-21 on b23, the real stage 0 against a local bare origin: [dfkwk] and [dfkwm] fail on the unfixed cicd.bash. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: git applies its autostash without --index. fSyncMerge keeps --autostash, and the new stash entry it leaves is the signal item 9 chose for a failed restore.
	- Origin: b463d2b (2026-08-12) for the fast-forward, 0633cc1 for the merge. Found in the sweep for 2026112017135488. Confirmed for git, Plausible for stage 0.
	- Note: A fix that stashes by hand and pops with --index changes the signal in 2026112017135764's Decisions, so it needs an Against: line.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: git puts an autostash back without --index, so after a fast-forward or merge that went in clean, staged edits came back unstaged and a file staged and then edited again lost its staged copy.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: fSyncMerge in cicd.bash stashes the edits itself, merges without --autostash, and puts them back with stash pop --index. A pop that fails, whether on a clash in the tree or in the index, backs the merge out to the commit it started from, pops there with --index, and stops naming the files. A merge that fails is aborted and the edits put back the same way.
	- Against: 2026112017135764's Decisions, where the new stash entry is the signal. The signal is now the pop's exit status, since a hand pop reports a failed restore and --autostash didn't. The rest of that decision holds: the reset goes to the starting commit, --index keeps staged edits staged, and a stash entry the user already had is left alone.
	- Decisions: Stash by hand and pop with --index, as the publisher's fStashPop does, rather than keep --autostash and rebuild the index afterward, since git keeps no copy of the index once an autostash applies clean. A new stash entry after the push is how stage 0 knows it stashed anything, so with nothing to stash the user's own entry is never popped. A clash in the index leaves no unmerged file, so the message names the files both the stash and the merge changed. git stash refuses an intent-to-add file, as --autostash does (git 2.51 probe), so that case now stops with its own message rather than the diverged one; not run through stage 0. A Ctrl+C between the stash and the pop leaves the edits in stash@{0}.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfkwk], [dfkwm], [dfkwn] and [dfkwp], with [dfk07] to [dfk0a] still passing.
	- Verified: [dfkwk] and [dfkwm] fail on the unfixed cicd.bash (suite 2335/4) and pass with the fix. [dfkwn] fails when the pop runs with nothing stashed, and [dfkwp] fails with the file-naming fallback taken out, and both pass with the fix. The quick gate with every area passed: test.bash 2339/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0.
	- Swept: every --autostash and stash pop in cicd/, by grep. Only fSyncMerge's two callers had --autostash, and both go through the hand stash now. The publisher already pops with --index (2026112017135488). parity.bash's --autostash is a plan-text pattern for gitsby's own pulls. Left alone: the frozen v2.1.0 scripts under legacy/, and the Go pulls, which 2026112017135488 swept.
	- Branch: nov21-2026112110520434
	- Commit: d37b6ce
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261121-111634

- With Windows' own OpenSSH as the ssh command, a fetch from an ssh origin that stalls after its banner waits until killed
	- ID: 2026112021513016
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261120-215130
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026112021204523, 2026112017135720
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: On vm925w, point a GIT_SSH_COMMAND of C:/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe with gitsby's three ssh options at a 127.0.0.1 listener that sends an SSH banner and then nothing, and run git ls-remote on it, as gitsby's fetch does with a core.sshCommand naming that ssh.exe. People set that to use Windows' ssh-agent.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: ssh prints that the connection timed out after about 3 s, but neither it nor git exits. git ls-remote was still running when killed at 28 s.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The fetch gives up within its 30 s limit, as it does with Git for Windows' own ssh, which exits at the timeout.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on vm925w, OpenSSH_for_Windows_9.5p2, git 2.55.0.windows.5, with GIT_SSH_COMMAND naming that ssh.exe. Confirmed. The same ssh run alone, with stdin NUL, a pipe held open, a closed pipe or -n, was still running at 25 s, and kept running 20 s after the server closed the connection.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: Windows' OpenSSH doesn't exit after it reports the timeout, so git waits on it. The fix is upstream. gitsby can't put a time limit on a whole fetch, since a large one can run long. Killing git on Windows also leaves its ssh running.
	- Origin: Win32-OpenSSH. gitsby's limits from adcef33 (2026112017135720) reach that ssh; it ignores them by not exiting.
	- Note: Upstream issue text drafted in private/claude_simple/upstream/2026112021513016/.
	- Upstream: PowerShell/Win32-OpenSSH#1427, commented 20261121 (<https://github.com/PowerShell/Win32-OpenSSH/issues/1427#issuecomment-7066202716>)
	- 20261121: the hang is Win32-OpenSSH#1427, an async write to stderr that never completes when stderr is a pipe. Checked on vm925w: with stderr to a file, ssh.exe exits 255 at 3 seconds; with stderr to a pipe it was killed at 20 seconds, whatever stdout is. Commented there rather than filing a new issue.
	- 20261121: a possible workaround on gitsby's side is to give that ssh a file for stderr, read back afterwards. Not tried.
	- Note: the 3 seconds above was with ServerAliveInterval=1, as in the upstream draft. With gitsby's options, ssh.exe with stderr to a file or NUL ends at 30 s on a stalled server.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Windows' own OpenSSH 9.5p2 never exits once it has written a line to a stderr that is a pipe, whatever the server does next: a stall, a close, or a refused login. To NUL or a file it exits on its limits. gitsby's fetch gives git NUL, so it ended at 30 s all along. The repo probe gave git a pipe, so it waited until killed. The login probe gave ssh a pipe, so it waited for its own 38 s limit on any server that made ssh write a line.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: On Windows, the repo probe and the login probe read what git and ssh said back from a temp file rather than a pipe (errSink in remote.go). design.md says so under the ssh identity notes.
	- Branch: nov21-2026112021513016
	- Commit: b205e4a
	- Test case: Go [dfkxx] TestRemoteReachesEndWithWindowsOwnSSH, on Windows with Windows' own ssh as core.sshCommand: the fetch, the repo probe and both login probe paths, against a server that closes at once and one quiet after its banner, each ending inside the login probe's own limit. It skips elsewhere. Go [dfkxw] TestErrSinkFileReadsLikeThePipe, the file path forced on: the same answers as the pipe, and no file left.
	- Verified: On vm925w (OpenSSH_for_Windows 9.5p2, git 2.55.0.windows.5), [dfkxx] fails on a build with the file path turned off, with the repo probe and both login probes still waiting at 9 s against both servers. It passes with the file path, in 13 s. [dfk1m] passes there in 16 s, down from 32 s.
	- Verified: In a rig run on vm925w, ssh.exe alone and under git ls-remote, with stderr to NUL or a file, ended at 30 s on a stalled server, and at once on a closed one or a refused login. With stderr to a pipe, every case was still running at 10 to 12 s.
	- Verified: [dfkxw] fails with the file read taken out, with the removal taken out, and with the file never made. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2339/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec 37, unchanged.
	- Swept: every command that reaches a remote and whose output gitsby reads, by grep for Stderr, Output and CombinedOutput beside remoteEnv and probeSSHLogin. probeRemote and probeSSHLogin use errSink. The fetch and set-head in fetchRemote run with NUL. askOriginHeads and the steps pass gitsby's own stderr through. gh and tea calls go over https, not ssh.
	- Decisions: A workaround rather than Won't fix. The pipe that triggers the hang was gitsby's own, a temp file costs little, and the hang came from any line ssh wrote, not only a stall.
	- Decisions: Windows only, behind errToFile, so other platforms keep the pipe. [dfkxw] runs the file path on every platform. If the temp file can't be made, the pipe is used.
	- Decisions: A command that writes to gitsby's own stderr is left alone, since it gets what git run by hand would. Fixing that case for git run by hand is the upstream issue's job.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced on vm925w, its test failed before the fix and passes after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261121-115347

- The ssh identity probe asks port 22 for an ssh:// origin on another port
	- ID: 2026112020462137
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261120-204621
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Point origin at ssh://git@host:2222/o/r.git, where only port 2222 serves git, with no ssh_config entry for the host. Run gitsby status.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The SSH line's account probe runs ssh -T git@host with no -p, so it asks port 22. The SSH line's ssh -G read has no port either, so a Match on the port isn't seen.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The probe and the ssh -G read connect to the port the URL names, as git's fetch does.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: sshConnectTarget in remote.go drops the port, and neither caller passes -p. TestSSHConnectTarget pins the target without it.
	- Origin: Plausible, read only. Found while working 2026112017135720.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-21 on b23, with a logging stand-in for ssh: [dfkxv] fails with the port left out, which gives the old arguments. Confirmed.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: sshConnectTarget gives only '[user@]host', and neither the login probe nor the ssh -G read added the URL's port.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: sshDest in remote.go gives the URL's port as -p, then '--' and the target. The login probe, the SSH line's ssh -G read and the alias lookup all end their ssh call with it, so the last two still share one read. The port goes after the ssh command's own words, where git puts it.
	- Branch: nov21-2026112021513016
	- Commit: b205e4a
	- Test case: Go [dfkxt] TestSSHDestCarriesThePort. Go [dfkxv] TestSSHCallsGoToTheURLsPort, the login probe and the ssh -G read through a logging stand-in for ssh, with one -G read for the alias lookup and the SSH line.
	- Verified: [dfkxt] and [dfkxv] fail with the port left out of sshDest and pass with it. [df053] still counts one -G read. [dfkxx] on vm925w reaches its listener through the URL's port. The quick gate passed with every area.
	- Swept: every ssh gitsby runs about a remote. probeSSHLogin, from sshLogin and askSSHLoginAhead, and sshConfigText, from readSSHConfig (the SSH line) and resolveSSHHost (parseRemote), all take sshDest. sshConnectTarget is now called only by sshDest and its own test.
	- Decisions: Digits only for the port, since git can't connect with anything else. An scp-like URL has no port to give, as in git. [dbfrr] TestSSHConnectTarget still pins the target without the port, since the port now goes apart from it.
	- Note: Examined and left alone: an ssh:// URL with a bracketed IPv6 host, which sshTarget cuts at its first colon. Filed as 2026112111542213.

- Code Review 20261120 item 46: A submodule whose remote is gone makes pullcom skip the pull as if origin were unreachable
	- ID: 2026112017151559
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261120-171515
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Clone a repo with a submodule. Move the submodule's remote away, have origin's dev bump the gitlink, and run `gitsby -q pullcom` on dev.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The fetch of origin works, but the submodule fetch fails, so gitsby warns that the remote is unreachable, skips the pull, and prints Done at exit 0. dev stays behind 1.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The pull runs, since origin answered. A failed submodule fetch is named for what it is.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, git 2.51, local bare repos. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The fetch at remote.go:310 follows fetch.recurseSubmodules, which defaults to on-demand, and any failure sets offline.
	- Origin: 3d22222 (Go port). No round saw it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The pre-command fetch follows fetch.recurseSubmodules, on-demand by default, so once origin's branch moves a submodule it fetches that submodule too, and exits 1 when its remote is gone. Any failure set offline, though origin's refs were already in.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: fetchRemote reads the fetch's stderr under LC_ALL=C, through a temp file. git's 'Errors during submodule fetch:' heading means origin's fetch worked, since git fetches submodules only after it does. Then the run warns that a submodule's fetch failed, names 'git submodule update', and isn't offline. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfkym] and [dfkyn].
	- Verified: [dfkym] and [dfkyn] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it. Quick gate with every area: lint and unit passed, test.bash 2348/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0.
	- Swept: fetchRemote is the one git fetch in src-go, by grep, and the only place that sets offline. A pull of an upstream on another remote fetches through git pull as a step, so its failure is git's own output.
	- Decisions: The warning names no submodule, since git lists submodule names rather than paths and a path goes on a File: line. Read from git's text rather than retrying the fetch with --recurse-submodules=no, which would double the wait when truly offline. A git that words the heading another way falls back to offline, as before. Once the pull runs, it meets 2026112112175066, as the case with the submodule's remote in place does today.
	- Branch: nov21-2026112017151559
	- Commit: 867360f
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261121-123934

- Code Review 20261120 item 18: pr create takes the PR's base from the current branch's name while its head is the branch it pushes
	- ID: 2026112017135624
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261120-171356
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Under push.default=upstream, run `git checkout -b fix --track origin/hotfix/x`, commit, and run `gitsby -q pr create Fix`. Then run `pr ok` on that PR.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It opens `--base dev --head hotfix/x`. pr ok then takes the head as a hotfix, pulls main and back-merges origin/main into dev at exit 0, though the fix never reached main. Names the other way round open against main and skip the back-merge.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The base follows the head that's pushed, so pr create and pr ok agree.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, with a fake gh and a stand-in for the git host's merge. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: `base := a.branchTarget("")` at pr.go:613. refuseUnrelatedPr at pr.go:464 reads the base the same way. pr ok reads only the PR's head, never its base.
	- Origin: 4918b5b. Code Review 20261119 item 7 (5b4e930) moved the head and left the base. Missed twin.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: pr create's run, its plan line and its unrelated-history refusal read the base off the current branch's name, while the head was the branch on origin the push lands on. pr ok reads that head back and takes its target and back-merge from it, so the two disagreed whenever the names differed.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: One helper, prTarget in pr.go, reads the target off the PR's head branch on origin. pr create's gh, tea and glab calls, its plan line and its unrelated-history refusal use it, and so do pr ok's checkout, plan and held-branch check. prCreateArgs and prCreateDisp take no base, so a caller can't pass another. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Branch: nov21-2026112017135624
	- Commit: 953ac24
	- Test case: test.bash [dfm0q] to [dfm0s]; Go TestPrTarget [dfm0t].
	- Verified: [dfm0q] to [dfm0s] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it. [dfm0t] fails with prTarget reading the current branch's name, for gh, tea and glab, the plan line, pr ok and the refusal. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2361/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0, spawn counts unchanged. gosec 37, as before, none in the changed lines.
	- Swept: every branchTarget and isHotfixBranch caller. pr create's run, plan and refuseUnrelatedPr, and pr ok's cmdPrAccept, previewPr and checkoutsAhead now read prTarget. pr ok's isHotfixBranch calls and mergePushesOwn already read the PR's head. br merge, its staged check and refuseUnrelatedMerge read the current branch's name for both the merge and its target, since the merge is local, so they agree and were left alone. goneBranchLeave leaves pr create out, which has no gone-branch warning.
	- Decisions: pr ok still reads only the PR's head, not its base. A PR opened elsewhere against another base is filed as 2026112113223086. isHotfixBranch(a.pr.headBranch) stays at its 4 sites rather than getting a helper of its own, since each already reads the head.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261121-132243

- Code Review 20261120 item 25: repo connect from a shallow clone commits and adds origin, then the push is refused
	- ID: 2026112017135517
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261120-171355
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Run `git clone --depth 1`, remove origin, add a file, and run `gitsby -q repo connect <empty bare repo>`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It commits and adds the remote, then the push fails with "shallow update not allowed", exit 1. A rerun fails the same way. A local target that isn't bare fails the same way.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Refused up front, as repo.go's header promises for a target that can't work.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, both cases. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: settleRepoConnect at repo.go:287 doesn't check for a shallow repo or a local target that isn't bare.
	- Origin: 115bb7d and aa044ac (Go port). No round saw it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: settleRepoConnect checked only whether the target existed and was empty. git refuses a shallow clone's push to a repo with none of its history, and a push into the branch a non-bare repo has checked out, and both were found at the push, after the commit and the remote add.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: refuseShallowPublish refuses repo connect and repo create in a shallow clone, naming 'git fetch --unshallow', when the target is new or origin has no branches. refuseCheckedOutTarget refuses a local target with a working tree whose checked-out branch is the one the push goes to, unless its receive.denyCurrentBranch allows the push. Both run before the plan. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfkys] to [dfkyx], [dfkz9] and [dfkza].
	- Verified: [dfkys], [dfkyt], [dfkyw], [dfkz9] and [dfkza] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it. [dfkyv] and [dfkyx] pass on both. Quick gate as on 2026112017151559, then lint, unit, fuzz and parity again after [dfkz9] and [dfkza], and test.bash 2350/0.
	- Swept: all 3 connect modes: add and create refuse a shallow clone before the probe or gh, and push mode does when origin has no branches. A local target is checked in add mode and in push mode with an origin with no branches, such as one a refused push left set.
	- Decisions: A shallow clone is refused even where a local target sets receive.shallowUpdate, which git hosts don't offer. A target given as a file:// URL isn't checked for a working tree. The refusals sit in the sentence with the target, as the other repo connect refusals do.
	- Branch: nov21-2026112017151559
	- Commit: 4342a52
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261121-123934

- Code Review 20261120 item 27: The publisher brings other staged edits back unstaged
	- ID: 2026112017135488
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261120-171354
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Stage b.txt, edit it again, and run the publisher with `GIT_BACKUP_AND_PUBLISH_PATHS=a.txt -q -m pub`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It commits only a.txt, which is right, but b.txt's index entry goes back to HEAD. The staged copy is left only in a dropped stash.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Other staged edits stay staged, as n8git_backup-and-publish:371 says.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, the real publisher with a stub gitsby. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: A plain `git stash pop` at n8git_backup-and-publish:341 and :357. Stage 0's autostash merge does the same, by a git probe.
	- Origin: bbb90b5 (2026-07-25), and the claim in 0633cc1 (2026112013542584). No round saw it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Related IDs: 2026112110520434
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Both of the publisher's pops were a plain git stash pop, which brings staged edits back unstaged and drops an edit that is only staged.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: Both pops go through fStashPop, which pops with --index. When the pull changed a staged file in the same place, --index puts nothing back, and the publisher stops with the edits all still in the stash. Nothing is committed or pushed.
	- Decisions: An index clash stops the run rather than falling back to a plain pop, since a plain pop drops an edit that is only staged (git 2.51 probe). It is told from an untracked file in the way by the stash having a staged part, so that case keeps fStashPopFailed's message.

The Go pulls take no --autostash under --staged (staged.go), and commit the whole tree otherwise. Stage 0's --autostash on a merge that goes in clean brings staged edits back unstaged too, filed as 2026112110520434.
	- Branch: nov21-2026112017135640
