- pr create from a branch that shares no history with dev pushes it, then the git host refuses the pull request
	- ID: 2026112007483630
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261120-074836
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026111919473452
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: In a clone of a GitHub repo with main and dev, git checkout --orphan feat, commit a file, then run gitsby -q pr create T.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The plan and park push run and publish feat, then gh fails, since GitHub won't open a pull request between unrelated histories. By reading; not run.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Refuse before the plan, as br merge does for the same branch, if every git host refuses it. GitLab and Gitea may not, which needs checking first.
	- Origin: Go port. Found while sweeping 2026111919473452. Plausible.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on b23, with a fake gh and a fake tea: an orphan branch passed every check before the plan, so the park push would publish it. GitHub refuses a pull request between unrelated histories, and Gitea does since 1.26.2 (go-gitea/gitea PR 37472), by their docs and source; no real git host was run. Confirmed.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Nothing before the plan asked whether the branch shares a commit with the base the pull request goes into. The git host answered that only after the park push.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: pr create refuses before the plan through gh and tea when the branch shares no commit with its base, origin's or else the local one. The refusal names git merge --allow-unrelated-histories as raw-git territory. glab and a shallow clone go on as before. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfjg8] to [dfjgc].
	- Verified: [dfjg8], [dfjg9] and [dfjgc] fail with the refusal call removed and pass with it. [dfjga] and [dfjgb] fail with the shallow and glab skips removed and pass with them. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2218/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec reports the same 37 hits, none in pr.go.
	- Swept: every place a merge happens on the git host: pr create's create call, through gh, tea and glab. pr ok merges a PR the git host already opened, so it can't meet this. br merge's local merge has its own refusal (2026111919473452).
	- Branch: nov20b-2026112007483630
	- Commit: ca1848e
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261120-113528
	- Decisions: Refused on GitHub and Gitea only. GitLab opens and merges a request between unrelated histories: Gitaly added an option to allow them after refusing them broke merge requests in production (gitlab-org/gitaly MR 5385). Refusing there would block a request the git host takes.
		- Gitea is judged by tea, so a Forgejo host reached through tea is refused too. Forgejo's behavior wasn't checked. Gitea before 1.26.2 failed its compare page on such a pair, so no release of it is known to open one.
		- A shallow clone goes on, since the shared commit can be cut off here while the git host has it. br merge refuses there, since git merges locally.
		- The base is origin's, which the git host compares against, and the local one only when origin has none. The paste line names that ref, such as origin/dev.
		- One more git spawn for a pr create through gh or tea, the merge-base. The shallow check runs only on the refusal path. spawn-count [df052] measured 46 against 43 expected, within its headroom; [df37x] for glab measured 33 against 31, which this change doesn't touch.

- A candidate suffixed after a dot sorts above its own release in every tag scan
	- ID: 2026111920273377
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261119-202733
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026111910222928
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Tag v3.0.0.rc1, then v3.0.0, then run 'gitsby release' or release.bash with no version.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: git's version sort with versionsort.suffix=- ranks v3.0.0.rc1 above v3.0.0, so the newest tag reads as the candidate, the next version comes out as v3.0.0 again, and the cut stops on a tag that exists. gen-winres.bash and the demo stamp take the candidate's version too.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A candidate sorts below its own release whether its suffix follows a dash or a dot.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23, the sort only, in a temp repo with tags v3.0.0, v3.0.0.rc1 and v3.0.0-rc.2. Adding versionsort.suffix=. puts v3.0.0 first. The cut that follows is read, not run.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The tag scans in src-go/release.go (resolveRelease and the --points-at one), cicd/release.bash, cicd/utility/gen-winres.bash and the demo stamp in cicd/cicd.bash pass only versionsort.suffix=-.
	- Origin: ed296a4, 2026-09-16, with the dotted suffix the version check admits. Found while fixing 2026111910222928. Plausible for the cut, Confirmed for the sort.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: As the possible cause says. git calls a suffix a pre-release only after the separator it's given, and every scan gave it only a dash. gitsby's newestReleaseTag took git's first v tag as it came.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: gitsby's newestReleaseTag weighs every tag by number, then a release over its own candidate, and git's order only breaks a tie. The three scripts share fReleaseTags in cicd/config.bash, which gives git a dot as well as a dash. changelog.md has a line under vNEXT.
	- Decisions: gitsby weighs the tags itself rather than giving git a dot suffix, since it runs on any repo, and a dot suffix ranks v1.2 above v1.2.1. The scripts give git the dot, since they run only here, where every tag cut is X.Y.Z. A tag with a fourth number, such as v1.2.3.4, counts as a candidate of v1.2.3 in both, as the version check and nextVersion already read it.
	- Swept: every tag scan that sorts: resolveRelease and unpushedRelease's --points-at scan in release.go, release.bash, gen-winres.bash, and the demo stamp in cicd.bash. branchcmd.go's call to newestReleaseTag only asks whether any tag exists. The installers go by GitHub's pre-release flag. legacy/bin/gitsby.ps1 has the same scan and is frozen at v2.1.0.
	- Branch: nov20-2026111920273377
	- Test case: Go [dfj8g], test.bash [dfj8h] [dfj8j] [dfj8k] [dfj8m] [dfj8n]
	- Verified: each fails against the old code and passes after. [dfj8h] runs the cut the item read only: 'gitsby release' stopped on the existing v3.0.0. Quick gate passed, every area: test.bash 2204/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec 37, as before.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261120-072915

- br merge from a branch that shares no history with dev pushes it, switches to dev, then fails
	- ID: 2026111919473452
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261119-194734
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026111910222988
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: git init -b feat, add origin with main and dev, fetch, stage a file, then run gitsby -q br merge.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The park push commits and pushes feat, checks out dev, then git refuses to merge unrelated histories. It ends on dev, exit 1.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Refuse before the plan when the branch and its target share no commit, or end back on the branch.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23, local bare origin, while fixing 2026111910222988. Confirmed.
	- Origin: Go port. No round saw it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Nothing before the plan asked whether the branch shares a commit with its target. git refuses to merge unrelated histories only at the merge, after the park push and the checkout, and that failure isn't a conflict, so backOutMerge left the run on the target.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: br merge refuses before the plan when the branch has no commits yet, or shares no commit with its target, the local one or else origin's. The unborn case names git switch to the target, then br create, which takes the work along. The other names git merge --allow-unrelated-histories as raw-git territory, and a shallow clone names git fetch --unshallow. The changelog says so.
	- Test case: test.bash [dfj98] to [dfj9c]; [dcnqy] updated.
	- Verified: [dfj98] to [dfj9c] fail with the refusal stubbed out and pass with it. The repro from the item and an orphan branch both refuse with nothing pushed, still on the branch; the unborn way off was run and merged. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2209/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec reports the same 37 hits.
	- Swept: every local merge: br merge's, which this covers for hotfix branches too through branchTarget; the hotfix back-merge of main into dev and release's merges of dev and main, which join 2 branches gitsby made from each other, left alone. pr create's merge happens on the git host, filed as 2026112007483630.
	- Branch: nov20-2026111919473452
	- Commit: fb7a6d6
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261120-074856
	- Decisions:
		- Refused before the plan rather than ending back on the branch, since the push and the commit would already have happened, and git refuses the merge either way.
		- A shallow clone gets its own text, since there origin may have the shared commit but the clone not. Read only on the refusal path, so a normal run spawns 1 more git, the merge-base.
		- 20261120: test.bash [dcnqy] made its hotfix uncomparable with an orphan branch, which now refuses up front. Its pattern changed from the 'couldn't tell whether this hotfix' note to the refusal's 'shares no history with main'. That note can now only show when the target is missing.

- On Windows PowerShell 5.1, a paste line drops a double quote from a branch name
	- ID: 2026111917564808
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261119-175648
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026111910223104
	- Target OS: Windows
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Make a branch a"b, and get a line that names it, such as from br prune with origin unreachable. Paste it into Windows PowerShell 5.1.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: git gets ab, so it names another branch or none.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: git gets a"b, or gitsby gives no command for such a name.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-20 on vm925w (Windows 11 build 26200). Confirmed. In Windows PowerShell 5.1 git got ab for a"b, and an empty word for a lone double quote. pwsh 7 passed it right. pwsh set to Legacy argument passing failed the same way, on Windows and on Linux.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: Windows PowerShell 5.1 passes a double quote inside an argument to the program bare, and git reads it as a quote. pwsh 7.3 and later escape it, so no one spelling suits both.
	- Origin: df38db0, 2026-09-15, typedArg's Windows form. Plausible: the 5.1 passing is documented, not run here.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: As read. Windows PowerShell 5.1, and pwsh in Legacy argument passing, put the double quote on git's command line bare, and git's command-line parsing reads it as a quote. pwsh 7.3 and later escape it.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: On Windows typedArg gives a word with a double quote both spellings, and the line picks one when it runs: as is under pwsh's Standard or Windows passing, and with each double quote backslashed under anything else, 5.1 included.
	- Branch: nov20-2026111917564808
	- Commit: 7ab6156
	- Test case: Go [dfhfc] TestPasteLinesReadBack, with 10 words that hold a double quote and a new pwsh Legacy leg, and [dcnmn] TestTypedArg.
	- Verified: [dfhfc] fails on the code before the fix and passes after, on b23 (pwsh 7.6 Legacy leg) and on vm925w (Windows PowerShell 5.1 and the pwsh Legacy leg, 20 lines each before the fix). Quick run of every area passed: test.bash 2209/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec 37, as before.
	- Swept: every typedArg caller (branch.go, branchcmd.go, main.go, mutate.go, pr.go, release.go, and leaseDeleteLine in prune.go) goes through the one function. No other code in src-go, cicd or the docs spells a PowerShell argument.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced on vm925w, its test failed before the fix and passes after there.
	- Closed: 20261120-080834
	- Decisions:
		- Both spellings in the line, picked by $PSNativeCommandArgumentPassing when it runs, rather than no command for such a name. Every caller keeps its command, and only a name with a double quote gets the longer line. Its Check: entry was answered 2026-11-20, and the call stands.
		- With Set-StrictMode on in Windows PowerShell 5.1, the unset variable stops the line with an error and git doesn't run. Left as is, since it's an error rather than a wrong branch, for a rare name in a rare setup.
		- The pick reads Standard and Windows as escaping. Under Windows passing pwsh still passes .cmd and .bat files the Legacy way, and git and gitsby are .exe files.
		- The Legacy spelling leaves out the quotes 5.1 adds around a word with a space, since no ref name holds one.
		- [dfhfc]'s Windows PowerShell 5.1 leg exited 1 partway once on vm925w, the first run after a start from off, with no stderr kept. It passed in the 3 runs after. psRun now prints the shell's stderr when it fails.

- Code Review 20261119 item 27: release.bash finds the default branch with symbolic-ref --short
	- ID: 2026111910222914
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261119-102229
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: In a clone, make a tag named origin/main, then run the default branch lookup.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It reads remotes/origin/main, the show-ref fails, and the check for untested commits on main is skipped.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Read the full ref and strip refs/remotes/origin/, as branch.go's originHead does.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: fpDefaultBranch at release.bash line 203.
	- Origin: dc94879, round-20261111. Sibling of originHead's rule, Never --short.
	- Closed reason: Done

The current branch had the same flaw: rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD gives heads/dev beside a tag named dev, so release.bash refused to cut from dev.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: fpDefaultBranch reads the full ref and strips refs/remotes/origin/, and goes on to main, master or trunk when origin/HEAD points anywhere else, as originHead does. The current branch comes from git branch --show-current, with HEAD when detached.
	- Swept: every symbolic-ref and abbrev-ref in cicd/ and src-go/. release.bash had two more, both reading the current branch, now fpCurrentBranch. cicd.bash's rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{u} only asks whether an upstream exists. branch.go strips full refs throughout.

	- Closed: 20261120-072915

- In a sparse checkout, an edited tracked file outside it is left uncommitted at exit 0
	- ID: 2026111920000538
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261119-200005
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Set a sparse cone, write a tracked file outside it back into the tree and edit it, then run gitsby -q pullcom m.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: Status lists the file as modified, git add --all stages nothing for it, and gitsby says Nothing to commit and Done, exit 0.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The edit is committed, or the run says why it isn't.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23, git 2.51, found while fixing 2026111910222973. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: git add --all skips tracked paths outside the sparse patterns without an error, and nothing before the commit compares that with status.
	- Origin: Go port. No round reached it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: git add --all skips a tracked path outside the sparse patterns without an error, even with its skip-worktree bit cleared, and the commit decides from the index after the add. So the edit was left out and the run said Done.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: refuseSparseAdd also compares git diff with the paths its dry run of git add --all would take. In a sparse checkout, an edited tracked file the dry run leaves out is refused before the plan, in the same list as new files outside it, with the same two fixes. --staged is left alone.
	- Branch: nov19c-2026111910222973
	- Commit: 397c85f
	- Test case: test.bash [dfhkj] to [dfhkm]; Go [dfhkn] TestSkippedEdits.
	- Verified: [dfhkj] and [dfhkk] fail on be87857 and pass with the fix. [dfhkm], an edit and a delete inside the checkout, passes on both, and fails with the dry run's remove lines not read. A conflicted file in a sparse checkout still gets the conflict advice. The quick gate's lint, unit and suite areas passed: test.bash 2194/0. gosec reports nothing new in the changed files.
	- Swept: the dry run is the only place gitsby asks what git add --all takes. Submodules are compared with --ignore-submodules=dirty, as treeDirty reads them, since add stages nothing for a dirty one.
	- Decisions: Refuse, not stage with --sparse, as for 2026111910222973, since the checkout's shape is the user's choice. The comparison runs only when core.sparseCheckout is on, the one case where add skips an edit, so no other repo pays for it or can be refused by it. It is folded into the one dry run rather than a second check.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its test failed before the fix and passes after.
	- Closed: 20261119-200649

- br merge on a branch that tracks one of another name leaves that branch on origin and warns about the wrong one
	- ID: 2026111913330350
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261119-133303
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: 2026111910223203
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Have feat track origin/feature-x under push.default=upstream while origin also has an older feat, add a commit, and run gitsby -q br merge.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It pushes to feature-x, merges into dev, and asks to delete origin's feat. The lease refuses, so it warns that origin's feat has commits the merge doesn't, which is false, and feature-x stays on origin. Exit 0.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The delete names the branch the push went to, as pr create's head does, or br merge refuses before the plan.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23, local bare origin, while fixing 2026111910223203. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The atomic push, mergeDeleteRemote and the plan name the current branch, while pushDest pushes to the upstream.
	- Origin: The delete has named the current branch since the Go port, and a push to another name came with push.default=upstream. No round saw it. Confirmed.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: br merge's plan, its atomic push and its leased delete named origin's branch of the current branch's name, while the park push went where pushDest sends it: to an upstream of another name under push.default=upstream, or through a push refspec that renames it.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: br merge's plan, atomic push, delete and offline note name the branch on origin the park push lands on, read by parkHead, which pr create now shares. br merge refuses before the plan where git would refuse the push, where the push goes to another remote or to a ref that isn't a branch, and where it lands on main, dev or the default branch, whether or not anything is left to push. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Branch: nov19c-2026111913330350
	- Commit: 8f9e019
	- Test case: test.bash [dfhfw] to [dfhg1]; Go TestMergeHead [dfhg7].
	- Verified: [dfhfw] to [dfhg1] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it. [dfhg7] fails 4 of its 8 cases with mergeHead reading the current branch. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2170/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0, spawn counts unchanged. gosec has no finding in the changed lines.
	- Swept: every place br merge names origin's copy: the plan's 2 delete lines, the for-each-ref that asks whether origin has it, the atomic push, mergeDeleteRemote and the offline note. pr create's head goes through the same parkHead. br prune deletes origin's branches by local name, and only ones already merged into the target, so it was left alone. pr ok reads its head from the git host.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261119-182500
	- Decisions:
		- The delete names the branch the push went to, rather than br merge refusing every branch that tracks another name, since under push.default=upstream that push is meant.
		- Refused where pr create refuses, with the same way off, so the 2 commands that read the park push's head agree. A push to another remote is refused rather than left with no delete, since the merge goes to origin and gitsby's branch commands act on origin. Its Check: entry was answered 2026-11-20, and the call stands.
		- A head on a protected branch is refused with br merge's own text, ahead of refuseParkPush's 'sync --direct', since after that the delete would still take dev.

- Code Review 20261119 item 15: pr ok from another branch pulls that branch while its plan says the target
	- ID: 2026111910223089
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261119-102230
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Stand on a branch whose upstream moved ahead, then run gitsby pr ok <n> and answer y.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The plan says it checks out and pulls dev. The run fast-forwards the current branch instead and leaves dev stale.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The run matches the plan.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23, with a fake gh. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: cmdPrAccept in pr.go checks out the target only in some cases. The plan line in preview.go always names it.
	- Origin: 4918b5b and 353f5c9, 2026-08-19. Plan line from c4fa47c. No round saw it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The plan always named a checkout and pull of the merge target. The run checked it out only when the current branch had no upstream once the merge's branch delete was pruned, and otherwise pulled the current branch. The worktree check read a third rule, the current branch being the PR's.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: prOkMoves in pr.go is the one rule: pr ok moves to the merge target when the current branch has no upstream or tracks origin's copy of the PR's branch. It's read before the merge by the plan, the run and the worktree check. Otherwise the plan shows the pull of the current branch, and no checkout. The checkout line lost its asterisk, since it always runs when shown. The changelog says so.
	- Branch: nov19c-2026111910223089
	- Commit: 764fc97
	- Test case: test.bash [dfhgf] to [dfhgk]. Go [dfh8b] TestRefuseHeldBranch, new case 'pr ok from a branch with no upstream'.
	- Verified: [dfhgg], [dfhgh] and [dfhgj] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it. [dfhgf] and [dfhgk] pass on both, since the run itself didn't change there. The new [dfh8b] case fails before the fix. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2175/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0, spawn counts OK. gosec reports nothing in the changed files.
	- Swept: every reader of where pr ok ends: previewPr, cmdPrAccept and checkoutsAhead now share prOkMoves. mergePushesOwn and previewBackMerge read only the hotfix back-merge, which is unchanged. No other site compares the PR's branch with the current one, other than preflight's refusal wording.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261119-183738
	- Decisions:
		- The plan follows the run, not the other way round. Code Review 20260725 item 5 moved pr ok to the merge target only when the branch it stood on went away, so a run from another branch stays there. Moving it to the target every time would switch branches under work the PR has nothing to do with.
		- The local copy of the merge target stays behind origin's after a run from another branch, as any branch not checked out does. The next br switch to it pulls it. The issue named that as wrong, but its expected behavior asks only that the run match the plan.
		- The answer is settled before the merge. The run also still moves when the prune took the current branch's upstream, which can only happen when someone deleted it on origin since the first fetch, since pulling it would then fail after the merge.
		- Under --no-fetch, a run standing on the PR's branch now moves to the merge target, as its plan always said. It used to stay, since nothing was pruned. Unverified: read from the code, not run.
	- Note: [dfh8b]'s fixture now gives w an upstream, so its 'pr ok of another branch' case still checks nothing out under the new rule. Its asserts are unchanged.

On an unborn main, br switch, br merge, sync and pr create already refuse before the plan, pullcom makes the first commit, and br prune finds nothing. On an unborn feature branch beside origin's main and dev, br create, br hotfix and br switch work, since the park push makes the first commit. br merge there is 2026111919473452.

- Code Review 20261119 item 23: In a sparse checkout, a failed git add leaves the index half staged
	- ID: 2026111910222973
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261119-102229
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Set a sparse cone, add a file inside and outside it, edit one outside, then run gitsby -q sync.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: git add --all fails after the plan, with one file staged and one not, exit 1 with only git's advice.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Refuse before the plan, or say the index was left partly staged.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: cmdCommit doesn't know about sparse checkout.
	- Origin: Go port. No round reached it.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: In a sparse checkout, git add --all stages what is inside it, then exits 1 over a new file outside it. Nothing before the plan asked, so the run stopped after the pull with the index half staged.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: Every command whose commit stages the whole tree runs the same add as a dry run before the plan. When git names files outside the sparse checkout, the run refuses, lists them, and says how to take them in or use --staged.
	- Branch: nov19c-2026111910222973
	- Commit: be87857
	- Test case: test.bash [dfhk8] to [dfhkb]; Go [dfhkc] TestSparseAddPaths.
	- Verified: [dfhk8] and [dfhk9] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it. [dfhka] (--staged) and [dfhkb] (br create off dev) pass on both, as guards. The fixture turns advice.updateSparsePath off, since git still lists the files then. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2191/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec reports nothing new in the changed files.
	- Swept: git add runs only in cmdCommit, by grep for "git", "add" in src-go. Its callers are pullcom, sync, br switch, br merge, br create and br hotfix off a feature branch, pr create, release, repo create and repo connect; stagesTree names each. --staged never stages, so it isn't checked.
	- Decisions: Refuse rather than stage with --sparse, since the sparse checkout is a choice the run shouldn't undo, and the expected behavior asks for a refusal. Only git's sparse-path failure is refused; any other dry-run failure, such as a held index lock, is left to the real add. LC_ALL=C keeps git's lead in English; no git translation is installed here, so that part isn't pinned. An edited tracked file outside the checkout is a separate case, filed and fixed as 2026111920000538.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its test failed before the fix and passes after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261119-200016

- Code Review 20261119 item 26: release.bash publishes a dot-suffixed version as a full release
	- ID: 2026111910222928
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261119-102229
	- Opened by:
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Cut v3.0.0.rc1 with release.bash.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The version passes the check, but the pre-release test only looks for a dash, so no --prerelease, and installers take it as the newest full release.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Any suffix the version check admits, dot or dash, makes a pre-release, as gitsby's nextVersion reads it.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on b23, fIsReleaseVersion v3.0.0.rc1. Confirmed.

	- Actual fix [Bug]: release.bash calls a version a candidate when the shared version pattern finds anything past X.Y.Z, after a dash or a dot. That one test makes the pre-release, promotes the last tag to its plain version, and reads the install line's tag. design.md's release policy names the dot form.
	- Decisions: The pre-release message says a suffix, not a semver suffix, since a dot suffix isn't semver. A dotted suffix is still taken rather than refused, since 'gitsby release' takes it and its nextVersion reads it as a candidate. Its Check: entry was answered 2026-11-20, and the call stands.
	- Against: 2026111016332132's Decisions row, which left a dotted suffix publishing as a full release, unchanged. This item asks for the change, and the standing rule calls any suffixed tag a candidate.
	- Swept: every dash test on a version in release.bash: the bump (was line 325), the pre-release flag (349) and phase 3's install line check (619). The asset name split at 235 is a file name, not a version. Go's nextVersion already reads any suffix. Installers go by GitHub's pre-release flag, not the tag. The tag sort is the same class and is filed as 2026111920273377.
	- Branch: nov19c-2026111910222928
	- Test case: test.bash [dfhm3] [dfhm4], and [dd5es] for the dash form.

- Code Review 20261119 item 30: On Windows, a git.bat or git.cmd on PATH re-reads gitsby's arguments through cmd
	- ID: 2026111910222873
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261119-102228
	- Opened by:
	- Target OS: Windows
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Put a git.bat that calls git.exe ahead of git.exe on PATH, with a branch named x&ver, then run gitsby -q br switch x&ver --no-fetch.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: cmd runs ver, and gitsby exits 0 still on main. raw git exits 0 where git would exit 128.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: gitsby skips or refuses a batch file match, and names it.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-19 on vm925w, also with git.cmd and a name holding %PATH%. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: walkTool in exec.go accepts .bat and .cmd, and Go doesn't quote for cmd.
	- Origin: c14672e, 2026-10-21. exec.LookPath did the same before it. No round saw it.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: As guessed. Windows runs a .bat or .cmd file through cmd, which reads the command line again, so an `&` in an argument runs what follows and `%NAME%` expands. Go quotes only for the program's own parser.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: On Windows the PATH walk that every spawn and `raw` use passes over a .bat or .cmd file and takes the next program. With none left, the "Not found in path" refusal names the batch file. A program named by its path is refused when it is a batch file, PATHEXT included.
	- Decisions: Pass over rather than refuse, as with gitsby's own entry, since a batch file can't be run safely at all. The batch file is named only in the refusal when nothing else is found. A warning on each pass-over would have to be a refusal under `-q`, per the UI style guide, so skip and refuse would differ only interactively. This departs from "names it" when another program is found. The tool cache key now holds PATHEXT too, since the look reads it.
	- Test case: Go `[dfhmh]` (batch names, refusal text), and Windows-only `[dfhmj]` (the walk passes over .bat and .cmd, the refusal names them, a given path is refused) and `[dfhmk]` (a real run: an `&` and a `%NAME%` argument never reach cmd).
	- Verified: the quick gate, every area, on the fix (test.bash 2197/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0). Under wine, `[dfhmk]` fails on the build before, with cmd running the text after the `&` and expanding the name, and passes after. `[dfhmj]` fails with the path check taken out. gosec gives the same 37 findings before and after.
		- 2026-11-19 on vm925w (Windows 11 build 26200), from a Windows test build of nov19c at fca0441: [dfhmj], [dfhmk] and [dfhmh] passed.
	- Swept: every spawn goes through toolPath (`TestOneSpawnSite`): the findTool callers, `raw`'s own walkTool and its handover, and the ssh probe, whose program can be a path. install.ps1 runs no tool by bare name. The test-only `cmd /c mklink` runs cmd.exe itself.
	- Branch: nov19c-2026111910222873
	- Commit: 3058008
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: [dfhmj] and [dfhmk] passed on vm925w.
	- Closed: 20261119-210053

The [dbjjn] case "falls back to the Unix spelling" is now "falls back to dot-config".

- Code Review 20261110b item 36: install.ps1 changes PATH without telling Windows, so a new shell from the Start menu doesn't find gitsby
	- ID: 2026111016332008
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261110-163320
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Install with install.ps1, then open PowerShell from the Start menu or taskbar.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: gitsby isn't found until sign-out, though the installer says to open a new shell. Windows Terminal tabs reload the environment and work.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A new shell finds gitsby.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: No. ssh to the Windows boxes lands in a session with no Explorer.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: install.ps1:407 writes the registry with `Set-ItemProperty` and doesn't broadcast `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`. `SetEnvironmentVariable`, which it replaced, did.
	- Origin: 37b7445, 2026-08-19, which kept `%VAR%` entries unexpanded. Regression. Plausible.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: install.ps1 writes PATH with Set-ItemProperty, which doesn't broadcast WM_SETTINGCHANGE, so Explorer keeps its old environment and hands it to every shell it starts. SetEnvironmentVariable did broadcast, but it was dropped because it rewrites an expandable PATH as plain text.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: after the PATH write, install.ps1 calls Send-EnvironmentChange, which sends WM_SETTINGCHANGE with 'Environment' through SendMessageTimeout (Add-Type, SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG, 5 s). It's sent even when the registry already had the folder, for installs by the older script. If it can't be sent, the closing line says to sign out instead of opening a new shell. changelog.md has a line under vNEXT Fixed.
	- Decisions: Add-Type P/Invoke rather than setting and clearing a throwaway variable with SetEnvironmentVariable to get its broadcast, since that writes the registry twice for a side effect. A failed broadcast doesn't fail the install, since PATH is already written.
	- Branch: nov19-2026111016332008
	- Commit: c5ebe1b
	- Test case: test.bash [dfgxc] defines Send-EnvironmentChange from install.ps1 and calls it: off Windows it gets into the compiled P/Invoke stub, which proves the Add-Type text compiles and binds. [dfgxd] checks in the parsed script that the call comes after the PATH write and outside that write's try.
	- Verified: [dfgxc] and [dfgxd] fail on the old install.ps1 (no function, no call). [dfgxc] fails with a broken C# signature, and [dfgxd] fails with the call moved inside the write's try. Quick gate, every area, passed on c5ebe1b's tree: test.bash 2080/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. PSScriptAnalyzer clean on install.ps1. The Windows branch itself didn't run here.
	- Swept: every PATH or environment write in the tree. install.ps1 has the one registry write. legacy/install.ps1 still uses SetEnvironmentVariable, which broadcasts, and is frozen. No cicd or Go code writes the Windows environment.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Closed: 20261119-084520
	- Verified: on vm925w at nov19 ee2e268, as wintest in its desktop session, with only the two GitHub fetches stood in (SHA256SUMS and the binary). A whole install in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and again in pwsh 7.6.6, each from a PATH without gitsby's folder, printed 'Open a new shell to pick it up' and kept the user PATH's ExpandString kind. After each, Explorer's environment held the new folder with no sign-out. Control: a PATH registry write with no broadcast left Explorer's environment unchanged. test.bash [dfgxc]'s check printed 'REACHED (sent)' in pwsh 7, in the desktop session and over ssh. wintest's PATH and folders were put back after.
	- Note: wintest's machine PATH on vm925w has an old v2.1.0 gitsby.exe ahead of the user PATH, so 'gitsby --version' from a new shell there runs that one. The new folder is still on the shell's PATH.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: whole install passed on vm925w in 5.1 and 7, and Explorer's environment took the new PATH with no sign-out.
	- Stand-in: In place of opening PowerShell from the Start menu, the environment of wintest's running Explorer was read after each install. Explorer is what hands PATH to a shell started from the Start menu or taskbar (20261119).

- Converting an SHCL 2.x accounts file changes a value holding a byte that isn't UTF-8
	- ID: 2026111819043675
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261118-190436
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026111016332218
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: A 2.x accounts file with the byte 0x87 as a name's whole value. Run `account list`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: 2.x read the value as U+FFFD. After the conversion it reads as the byte 0x87, and the notice says nothing about it.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The converted file reads what 2.x read, or the conversion is refused.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-18 on b23, found by FuzzOld2xHandTyped `[dfg4d]`, which now skips such values.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: shcl 2.x replaced a broken byte when it read the file, and v3 keeps it as written. Not looked at further.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: shcl 2.x turned each byte of a line that isn't UTF-8 into U+FFFD as it read the line, one per byte. v3 keeps the byte, so the module's migration wrote it out as it was.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: `broken2xBytes` in cfgformat.go, called first in `convert2x`. Each such byte in a 2.x value is written as U+FFFD before the module converts the file. The notice counts the line as re-spelled.
	- Decisions: Converted rather than refused, since U+FFFD is the value 2.x read and the file as it was is kept. One U+FFFD per byte, as 2.x did, not one per run as strings.ToValidUTF8 gives. Only the value is changed. A comment keeps its bytes, since nothing reads it and the after-check compares comments with the file as it was. A quoted key with such a byte isn't changed, since gitsby reads no such key.
	- Branch: nov18-2026111819043675
	- Commit: 93bab4e
	- Test case: Go `[dfg4d]` FuzzOld2xHandTyped no longer skips such values, with 4 new seeds; `[dfg5b]` TestOld2xBrokenByte: 3 values read what the real 2.x module read, a comment keeps its bytes, the kept copy is the file as it was. test.bash `[dfg5c]` the steps' file through the binary.
	- Verified: `[dfg4d]` (its 4 new seeds) and `[dfg5b]` fail without the `broken2xBytes` call, and `[dfg5c]` fails on a binary built without it. All pass with it. 90 seconds of fuzzing found nothing more. Quick gate, every area: test.bash 2064/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0.
	- Swept: `convert2x` is the only 2.x conversion. The flat conversion keeps the byte, as v2.1.0's bash build read it, from reading only. Whether its pwsh build read U+FFFD wasn't checked. The earlier SHCL 3 module's reader has no such replacement, also from reading, and its re-spelling touches double-quoted escapes only.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, and its tests fail before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261118-193251

- The --direct refusal and warning advise br create for commits already on main, which br create leaves there
	- ID: 2026111815522440
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261118-155224
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026111016332380
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: On main in a repo with dev, commit a change with pullcom, then run gitsby -q sync or gitsby -q br switch dev. Follow the advice and run gitsby br create x.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The refusal says to move the work to a branch with br create. br create from main checks out dev first, so the commit stays on main, still unpushed, and the next sync or br switch from main refuses again. Without dev the new branch has the commit, and main still holds it too.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The advice names a way out that works for committed work, or speaks only of a dirty tree when the work is uncommitted.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-18 on b23. [dfg30] fails on the build before the fix: after br create, main still held the commit.
	- Origin: e1cc030, 2026-10-05, the sync warning. Confirmed.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The refusal and the warning named br create whatever was going out. br create takes a dirty tree along, and leaves commits on the branch they were made on.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: With commits going out, both name 'git checkout -b <branch-name>', then 'git branch -f <branch> <upstream>', which takes the commits and the tree to a new branch and puts the protected branch back at origin's tip. A dirty tree alone still gets br create. pr create's refusal on main or dev does the same. design.md and the changelog say so.
	- Branch: nov18-2026111815522440
	- Commit: c203ecd
	- Test case: test.bash [dfg2y] to [dfg32], and [dfg38] for pr create.
	- Verified: [dfg2y] to [dfg32] and [dfg38] fail on the build before the fix and pass with it. [dfg30] runs the commands as the refusal prints them. [dfg31] guards the dirty-tree advice, and fails before only since main still held [dfg30]'s commit. The quick gate passed with every area: test.bash 2055/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0. gosec reports nothing in the changed files.
	- Swept: every message that names br create. The --direct refusal and warning, and pr create's refusal on main or dev, now fit committed work. br switch's dirty-branch refusal and its no-such-branch hint are about a dirty tree or a new name, so br create fits there.
	- Decisions: The way off is plain git, since no gitsby command moves commits off a branch. Making br create take commits along would change what it does, and wasn't asked for. git checkout -b rather than git switch -c, to match the plan's own steps and older git. The upstream is named as git has it, so a fork's upstream is right too.

- Code Review 20261110b item 19: Converting a SHCL 2.x accounts file cuts off any value with a quote before a #
	- ID: 2026111016332218
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261110-163322
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: A 2.x accounts file with `name: O"Brien#2` and `pathcontains: dev/c"#/proj`. Run `gitsby account list`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The file becomes `name: 'O"Brien'#2`, which v3 reads as `O"Brien` with the rest a comment. The folder rule changes the same way. gitsby says the lines were re-spelled to keep their values, exit 0.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The converted file reads the same values the 2.x reader did, or the conversion is refused.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23. 9 of 11 such values were cut.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: shcl's migrateLine and valueEdits, reached through `MigrateUnstamped` at cfgformat.go:82. gitsby doesn't check the result against the 2.x reading.
	- Origin: 37f4843, 2026-10-03. [ddg6e] feeds only values the 2.x writer quoted itself. No round saw it. Confirmed.
	- Notes: The module half belongs upstream in shcl. Only dev and gover builds wrote 2.x files, since v2.1.0 used the flat layout.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: In 2.x a quote anywhere in a value opened a run to the same quote or the end of the line, so a `#` or `,` after it was text. shcl v3.0.0-beta1 reads a 2.x line with its own 2.x rules, which don't run a quote opened mid-value, so its migration ends the value at the `#` or splits it at the `,`. The 2.x writer always quoted such a value, so `[ddg6e]` never fed one.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: `convert2x` in cfgformat.go. Before the module converts the file, a value it would cut or split, where 2.x read one value, goes in single quotes, or double where it holds an apostrophe. Quotes with no backslash read the same in 2.x. After, each line's comment and list reading is checked against 2.x's. A line that still differs, or one no quote fits, keeps the file as it is, and the notice and `account set`'s refusal name the line, with a Fix to quote it.
	- Decisions: The 2.x module stays out of the binary, per design.md, so the check uses a copy of 2.x's quote rule. 2.x is frozen, so it can't drift, and the fuzz target holds it to the real module. A value a quote can keep is converted rather than refused. The fuzz target skips lists, since `name` takes one value, and bytes that aren't UTF-8, filed as 2026111819043675.
		- 20261118: FuzzOld2xHandTyped [dfg4d] no longer skips bytes that aren't UTF-8, since 2026111819043675 added them.
	- Branch: nov18-2026111016332218
	- Commit: 5d58999
	- Test case: Go `[dfg4d]` FuzzOld2xHandTyped: a hand-typed 2.x value reads what the real 2.x module read, or the file is left as it was; `[dfg4e]` 8 such values, the steps' folder rule and their comments; `[dfg4f]` a value no quote fits refuses, naming the line. test.bash `[dfg4g]` the steps' file through the binary.
	- Verified: `[dfg4d]` (8 of 15 seeds), `[dfg4e]` and `[dfg4f]` fail on the previous config.go, cfgformat.go and accountcmd.go, and `[dfg4g]` fails on the binary built from 5f96830. With the quoting taken out, the after-check refuses every seed instead, and with both out `[dfg4d]` fails. 2 minutes of fuzzing found nothing more. Quick gate, every area: test.bash 2059/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0.
	- Swept: the flat conversion and the earlier module's re-spelling write values through the setter, not the module's 2.x reading, so neither has this shape. `convert2x` is the only caller of `migrateText` in the load.
	- Note: The module half is upstream, in shcl's 2.x reading of a line.

The kept `_format-v3old` backup gets a new mtime, so moving it back reads its escapes as text.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Only a file written by the old pin is converted, and a restored backup reads as it did.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23.

	- Origin: The mtime rule from Bug 2026110710480989. Confirmed.

	- Actual fix [Bug]: `fromOldPin` in cfgformat.go also wants a time no earlier than 2026-09-24 19:49:10 UTC, the commit time of the first module ca0e55c pinned. Every kept copy gets the file's own time, and a copy that can't keep it is removed and the file left as it was. A lock refused for permissions says the folder can't be written, another cause is named, and a held lock says another run held it.

A file touched to a time inside the window, as in the first steps, is still converted: the time is the rule, per the Against line. Every kind of kept copy keeps the time, so a restored 2.x or flat copy also reads as it did.

- Code Review 20261110b item 33: The ssh probe passes $HOME in GIT_SSH_COMMAND to ssh unexpanded
	- ID: 2026111016332045
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261110-163320
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: `GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -i $HOME/.ssh/work_key'` with an ssh origin. Run `gitsby status`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The probe runs ssh with the literal `$HOME/.ssh/work_key`. ssh falls back to its default keys, so the identity check may name the wrong account or refuse a push. git itself runs the command through a shell and expands it.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A command with `$`, a backtick or `~user` falls back to plain ssh, as one with quotes already does.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23, the argv. The wrong account is Plausible.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: remote.go:198 and show.go:607 split the command on spaces.
	- Origin: No round saw it. Confirmed.
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Actual cause [Bug]: gitSSHCommand split the command on blanks, and sent only a quoted one to plain ssh. A `$HOME`, a backtick or `~user` reached ssh as typed, where git's shell expands it.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: A command is split only when a shell would do nothing more than split it. A quote, backslash, `$`, backtick, `~user`, `#`, newline, `;`, `&`, `|`, `<`, `>` or parenthesis sends the probe and the SSH line's key to plain ssh, and the fetch leaves the command to git. A leading `~/` is still split, since ssh expands it in a key path, and gitsby's sshkey command is spelled that way.
	- Branch: nov18-2026111016332280
	- Test case: test.bash [dfg2f] and [dfg2g]; TestSSHCommandOnlyAShellCanRead [dfg25].
	- Verified: [dfg2f], [dfg2g] and [dfg25] fail on the nov18 build and pass with the fix. The quick gate passed with every area.
	- Swept: remote.go's probe and show.go's key line, the two splits the item names, both read sshArgv now. remoteEnv uses the same test. No other site splits an ssh command.
	- Decisions: A command only a shell can read now goes without the connect timeout on the fetch, as a quoted one already did. Before, a `$HOME` command in core.sshCommand got it. Recorded in design.md.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261118-175751
	- Commit: fe582c7

- Code Review 20261110b item 25: gitsby release takes a version git can't use as a tag, and fails after the merge into main
	- ID: 2026111016332145
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261110-163321
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: `gitsby release 1.2.3.lock` or `1.2.3-a..b`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: It commits the release merge on main, then `git tag` fails. Exit 1, with main 2 ahead.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The version is refused before anything runs.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: release.go:27 and :61 check the version with a regexp only.
	- Origin: 089776d, 2026-08-18. No round saw it. Confirmed.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: releaseVerRE took `..`, a trailing `.` and a `.lock` ending, which git refuses in a tag, and nothing else checked the version before the release merge.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The pattern takes dot-separated parts, none of them empty, and releaseVersionOK also refuses a `.lock` ending, so `release` refuses before anything runs. changelog.md has a line under vNEXT.
	- Decisions:
		- A pattern plus the `.lock` rule, not `git check-ref-format`, so it costs no spawn and release.bash can use the same rule. The test asks git about every short suffix that passes.
		- An empty part, such as `1.2.3-.a`, is refused too, which git would tag. Semver has no empty part either.
		- `.lock` is refused in lower case only, as git does.
	- Swept: every releaseVerRE use (resolveRelease, newestReleaseTag, isReleaseVersion) goes through releaseVersionOK. release.bash's side is 2026111016332132.
	- Branch: round-20261111
	- Test case: release_test.go [df4yj]
	- Verified: [df4yj] fails on the old pattern, where `1.2.3.lock`, `1.2.3..a` and 7 more pass and git refuses them, and passes after. Quick gate passed, every area: test.bash 1964/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 30/0.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261110-201616

- Code Review 20261110b item 26: release.bash takes version strings gitsby release refuses
	- ID: 2026111016332132
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261110-163321
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: `cicd/release.bash v3.0.0-`, `v3.0.0.` or `v3.0.0rc1`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: release.bash's pattern takes them and Go's doesn't. With `v3.0.0-` the version PR is merged into dev before `gitsby release` refuses, which then needs a PR by hand to undo. With `v3.0.0rc1` it dies at the winres step after the whole pipeline.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Both use the same pattern, checked before the pipeline runs.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23, the 2 patterns compared and `gitsby release v3.0.0rc1` run in a temp repo.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: release.bash:304 uses `([A-Za-z0-9.-]+)?`, where releaseVerRE uses `([-.][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?`.
	- Origin: 8d108fd, 2026-08-12. No round saw it. Confirmed.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: As the possible cause says. gen-winres.bash and the demo stamp in cicd.bash had the same loose pattern, and gen-winres.bash put a suffix after a dot, as in `v3.0.0.beta`, into the patch number.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: config.bash has RELEASE_VERSION_RE, the same pattern as releaseVerRE, and fIsReleaseVersion, which also refuses a `.lock` ending. release.bash checks with it before the pipeline, gen-winres.bash takes the three numbers from it, and the demo stamp uses it.
	- Decisions:
		- In config.bash, which release.bash, gen-winres.bash and cicd.bash all source. The Go build can't read cicd/, so test.bash holds the two patterns together over the same versions.
		- release.bash still wants the `v`. The shared pattern takes it as optional, for gen-winres.bash and the demo.
		- A dotted suffix such as `v3.0.0.beta` still publishes as a full release, since release.bash calls a version a pre-release by its `-`. Unchanged.
	- Swept: every version pattern outside legacy/. release.bash's argument check, gen-winres.bash and the demo stamp, fixed. release.bash's bump wants a plain vX.Y.Z already. test.bash's changelog heading check, and the installers' `--tag` check, which checks a tag's characters rather than a version, left. legacy/ is frozen.
	- Branch: round-20261111
	- Test case: test.bash [df4ym] [df4yk] [df4yn] [df4yp]
	- Verified: all 4 fail against the old release.bash, config.bash and gen-winres.bash and pass after. [df4yk] has a dry run refuse v1.3.0-, v1.3.0., v1.3.0rc1, v1.3.0.lock and v1.3.0-a..b before the pipeline. Quick gate passed, every area: test.bash 1964/0, fuzz 310/0, parity 30/0.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests failed before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261110-201616

- Code Review 20261110b item 41: 114 test.bash checks drop out with no SKIP line where pwsh or a pty is missing
	- ID: 2026111016331944
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261110-163319
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Run test.bash on a box with no pwsh, such as vmFreeBSD, or no `script -qec`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The checks in 9 `if ((hasPty))` blocks and 2 `if command -v pwsh` blocks vanish from the count without a SKIP. That's 15 and 99 checks.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Each block a box can't run calls fSkipBlock, per the 2026-10-26 test line rule.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: Yes, 2026-11-10 on b23. `[df4zw]`'s check, run on the unfixed test.bash, names the 11 blocks, and 18 more behind other probes of the box.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The blocks at test.bash:1748, 2424, 2448, 3474, 3604, 3887, 3892, 4033, 8313, 8473 and 8496 have no else. fEveryBlockSkips checks only existing calls.
	- Origin: 2026102618140158 added fSkipBlock. These blocks weren't swept. Plausible.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: As above. Nothing checked that a block behind a probe of the box has an else, so 29 blocks never got one.
	- Actual effort: Low
	- Decisions:
		- The 18 other blocks are the same class, behind `isWindows`, `canNoTty`, `shNoTty`, a writable `/usr/local/bin`, `ln -s`, `/proc/self/mem`, GNU `date -d`, `OSTYPE` and root. They got the same else. A Linux box with pwsh now prints one SKIP, `[db5xm]`, which runs only on Windows.
		- An if/else on `isMac` or `isWindows` with tests in both arms counts as covered, since each arm is that platform's form of the check.
		- No changelog line. Only the suite's output changes.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: Each of the 29 blocks has an else that calls fSkipBlock. fUnskippedBlocks finds a block behind a probe of the box that holds tests and skips none.
	- Swept: every multi-line `if` in test.bash that holds a test and has no SKIP. Left out: a `gateTool` loop branch, a soak branch inside a quoted script, and an awk line, none of them a probe of the box.
	- Branch: round-20261111
	- Commit: 6c6baad
	- Test case: test.bash `[df4zv]` (the check finds a bare probe block in a fixture, and passes one with a SKIP or a tested else) and `[df4zw]` (no such block in test.bash).
		- Verified: `[df4zw]`'s check fails on the unfixed test.bash, naming the 29 blocks, and passes after. Quick gate passed, all areas: test.bash 1969/0 with 1 SKIP, fuzz 310/0, parity 31/0.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its tests passed, and the check was watched to fail.
	- Closed: 20261110-204858

- Code Review 20261110 item 1: An option a command doesn't read is taken and dropped
	- ID: 2026111010494811
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261110-104948
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: In any repo, run `gitsby --staged raw git commit`, `gitsby -m msg raw git commit`, `gitsby status -m hello`, `gitsby repo connect <url> --public` or `gitsby pullcom --direct`.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: Each runs with the option dropped and says nothing. `gitsby --staged status` is refused, so only `raw` lets `--staged` through, and design.md:180 says any other command refuses it, since ignoring it would sweep in the edits it was typed to keep out.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A command refuses an option it doesn't read, the way `--staged` is refused, and names the commands that take it. `-q`, `--any-identity` and `--config` stay valid wherever they mean something.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10 on b23, built binary in a temp repo.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: parseArgs and scanPassthrough each keep their own list of options, and only `--staged` is checked against the commands that read it, in staged.go:20. Nothing ties the other options to theirs.
	- Origin: `--staged` in scanPassthrough from 9f53a91, and `--direct` from e1cc030, both 2026-10-05. `--public` and `--private` from 8da8951, 2026-08-17. A 2026-08 round fixed trailing arguments that were silently ignored, not options. No round saw this. Confirmed.
	- Notes: 1 table of options and the commands that read each, used by both parsers, is where a new option can't get past the check. `-m` on `br create` and `br switch` is read by the commit that parks work, so it stays there.
	- Against: A script that passes an option to a command that ignores it starts failing.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Only `--staged` was checked against the commands that read it, and `raw`'s scan took every option and kept 3.
	- Decisions:
		- `-q`, `--no-fetch`, `--any-identity` and `--config` stay valid on every command. `--no-fetch` asks for nothing a command could fail to do where nothing fetches, and parity `[db601]` pins v2.1.0 taking `-NoFetch` ahead of `raw`.
		- So the refused set is `-m` outside the 10 commands that commit, `--direct` outside `sync`, `--public` and `--private` outside `repo create`, and `--staged` as before, now ahead of `raw` too.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: 1 table of options, `optSpecs` in args.go, which both parsers read. An option with a command list is refused on any other command, as "-m works with pullcom, ... and repo connect." `checkStagedFlag` folded into it, with the same wording.
	- Swept: every option the 2 parsers took. design.md's Execution flow and the UI style guide's Commands and options say the rule.
	- Branch: cr1110
	- Test case: Go [df4e9] and [df4ea], test.bash [df4eb] to [df4ed], [ddht9] kept. [df4e9], [df4ea] and [ddht9] fail with the check stubbed out. [df4eb] and [df4ec] fail against the build before the fix.
	- Checks changed: test.bash [db5yb] loops over `-NoFetch` and `-AnyIdentity` only. It pinned `-Public` ahead of `raw` being taken rather than blamed on `raw`, and `-Public` is now refused by its own name, which [df4eh] checks. The point it was written for still holds.
	- Acceptance signoff: Quick gate passed, all areas.
	- Closed: 20261110-1140

- Code Review 20261110 item 3: One placeholder has several names across the help, the README and the Syntax lines
	- ID: 2026111010494785
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261110-104947
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: `repo connect` takes `[url]` in the help, `[target]` in the README and `[url | owner/name]` in its Syntax line. A PR number is `n` in the help, `<#>` in the README and `<number>` in the Syntax line. `repo create` takes `<o/n>` in the help and `<owner/name>` in the README and its Syntax line.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: One name per placeholder everywhere, per the UI style guide's "One word per thing" and the output sweep's row for it in design.md.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-10, `gitsby --help`, `gitsby pr list` and `gitsby repo` against the README's Commands table.
	- Origin: help.go:65 from 2206206, 2026-10-05, help.go:78 from 197677f, 2026-10-22, and README.md:105 from d446496, 2026-07-26. No round saw it. Confirmed.
	- Notes: The help's left column is 20 wide, which is why it shortens them. Widening it, or moving the arguments into the description as `account set` already does, are the 2 ways.
	- Decided against: making the Syntax line's `e.g. 'work', 'personal'` match the `github.com_my-work-login` examples. An account name is any string, and both are valid.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Each Syntax line, the help's command list and the README's table wrote their placeholders out by hand. The Syntax lines disagreed with each other too: `br create <new branch name>` against `<branch>`, and `repo connect` as both `[url | owner/name]` and `<url | owner/name>`.
	- Decisions:
		- `[message]`, `[version]`, `[directory]` and `<number>` everywhere, the Syntax lines' names. `repo connect` takes `[<url> | <owner/name>]`, so its Syntax line names the placeholders it defines.
		- The help lists `pr`, `pr <number>`, `pr create [title]` and `pr ok <number>` on 4 lines, the way the README does, and `raw <tool> <arguments ...>` on 1. A syntax too long for the 20-wide column moves into the line's text, as `account set` already did.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: 1 table, `usages` in usage.go, with each command's placeholders, their meanings and its help line. Every Syntax refusal and the help's command list read it, and a noun's block, such as bare `repo`, is built from its verbs. The README's Commands table uses the same names.
	- Swept: every `syntaxUsage` call, the 3 inline `repo connect <url | owner/name>` fix lines, app.go's comment, and the README table. design.md's Output sweep has a row for it. The fix lines now say `repo connect <url>, or <owner/name> for a GitHub repo`, with no `|` a pasted line would hand the shell.
	- Checks changed: test.bash [dbefw] and [dbefx] pinned the help's `pullcom [msg]` and `br merge [msg]`, to show the renamed commands lead. They are off, and [df4ej] and [df4ek] check the same with `[message]`.
	- Branch: cr1110
	- Test case: Go [df4ef], [df4eg] and [df4f8], test.bash [df4ee]. [df4f8] fails with a fix line put back to the `|` form. [df4ef] and [df4eg] fail with a placeholder renamed in the table. [df4ee] fails against the README before the fix, and against the build before it.
	- Acceptance signoff: Quick gate passed, all areas.
	- Closed: 20261110-1140

- Native fuzz step fails on a fuzz deadline, not a crasher
	- ID: 2026110915475544
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261109-154755
	- Opened by:
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The native fuzz step stopped with `--- FAIL: FuzzParseTeaTable (5.42s) context deadline exceeded` and printed `fuzzing found a crasher`, with no reproducer under src-go/testdata/fuzz/. Load was about 14 on b23, in the image, during a --backlog-run-full on round-20261109 at 4e70dce.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: A fuzz run that ends on its own deadline with no reproducer passes, or retries once. Only a saved reproducer counts as a crasher.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Origin: Seen 2026-11-09 in the gate step's security run. 3 reruns alone with the same flags (-fuzztime 5s, 8 workers) passed. The round didn't change parseTeaTable.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The step read any nonzero exit from `go test -fuzz` as a crasher. Go saves a crasher's input and says "Failing input written to". A worker stopped at -fuzztime saves nothing.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: Only output naming a saved input is a crasher, and it stops the run at once. Any other failure runs the target once more, and fails as "failed twice and saved no failing input" if that one fails too.
	- Decisions:
		- A second failure still fails the step. A target that hangs looks the same as a slow worker, and it shouldn't pass.
	- Branch: fuzzretry
	- Test case: test.bash [df3gx], [df3gy], [df3gz]
	- Verified: [df3gy] and [df3gz] fail on dev's cicd.bash. [df3gx] fails with crashers retried too. `--backlog-run-quick` passed, test.bash 1922/0. The real fuzz step passed on all 9 targets.
	- Closed: 20261109-195600

- spawn-count.bash names its records in local time, and the run in the image in UTC
	- ID: 2026110914575286
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Opened: 20261109-145752
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026110912215212
	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Run cicd.bash --backlog-run-quick (in the image), then cicd/utility/spawn-count.bash on the box, west of UTC.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The box run is stamped hours before the image run, so it compares against the image's record as its baseline, and gfs-rotate drops its own record at once as the oldest of the hour.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: Every record is stamped in one zone, so the newest run is the baseline and is kept.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-09 on b23 (PST). Two box runs in a row both read the image's spawn_20261109-224726 as baseline, and neither record was left.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: stamp="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)" is local time, and the image stays in UTC. lint-report.bash may stamp the same way.
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Actual cause [Bug]: spawn-count.bash and cicd.bash took their stamps in local time, and the image runs in UTC. gfs-rotate reads a name in the zone it runs in, so it misread the other side's records too.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual fix [Bug]: Both stamp in UTC, with `date -u`, and run gfs_rotate under `TZ=UTC0`. In cicd.bash that one stamp names the run log, the temp folder, the soak and CodeQL folders and the archived demo gif.
	- Decisions:
		- UTC, not the box's zone passed into the image. The image already runs in UTC, a record run by hand in the image gets no zone from outside, and UTC has no repeated hour at the fall-back.
		- cicd.bash's stamp too, since the soak and CodeQL folders and the demo archive are written by the image and by --no-container runs alike, and are pruned by name. Its run log is written only on the box, so it was never mixed, but it shares the one stamp.
		- lint-report.bash stamps nothing. It reads cicd.bash's run log names, which only the box writes, so it needed no change.
		- Old records keep their names. West of UTC they sort before every new one. East of UTC, a local name can sort after a new one for a few hours, once.
	- Swept: every `date +%Y` in cicd/. keep-build.bash, release.bash's run name and remote-tests.bash's folder run only on the box, and nothing compares them with an image run's name.
	- Branch: round-20261109
	- Test case: test.bash [df385] (spawn-count.bash) and [df386] (cicd.bash's soak folder), both under TZ='<-08>8'.
	- Verified: [df385]'s case, by hand on the script before, left the image's record as latest and the new one stamped 8 hours earlier. [df386] fails against cicd.bash before. Both pass after. cicd.bash --backlog-run-quick passes, test.bash 1918/0.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: its test runs passed.
	- Closed: 20261109-151048

- The SSH line puts the key's path inside parentheses
	- ID: 2026110914001448
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261109-140014
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026110912215207
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: status and whoami print the key file inside the SSH line's parentheses, as `SSH ..........: <account> (git@host via alias 'x', key /home/pat/.ssh/id_work)` (show.go showSSHLine). A long path wraps the line.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: UI guide: a path goes on its own labeled line, never inside a sentence or parentheses. Found in the 2026110912215207 sweep and left, since it changes the identity block's layout, its pinned checks and the demo.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: No. By reading.
	- Origin: show.go's key on the SSH line from 2fcc6c06 (2026-08-21). The 20261107 and 20261109 sweeps didn't reach it. Confirmed.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual cause [Bug]: The 2026110912215207 sweep searched for `" (" +` joins, and the key was joined on with `", key " +`, inside parentheses opened on another line.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: The SSH line ends at the host and alias. The key goes on a `File:` note under it, in the identity block's column, through `showAccountNote`.

	- ID: 2026110912215206
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261109-122152
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]:
		- Fix notes put a path in single quotes with no escaping, so a path with an apostrophe gives a command bash can't parse: show.go:484 (`chmod 600`), accountcmd.go:957 (`chmod u+r`), :977 (`chmod u+x`) and :1070 (`rm`). `shellWord` in exec.go:131 already quotes these right.
		- The merge back-out prints its settle text as a literal line (branchcmd.go:253, passed in at branchcmd.go:119 and release.go:220), such as `git checkout dev && git merge main, then 'gitsby release'`. That's prose inside a command. branchcmd.go:330 and release.go:175 put the command after a colon on the same line. `devBranch`, `mergeRef`, `targetBranch` and the tag go in unquoted, where `returnTo` and the branch use `typedArg`.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: UI guide: a fix that can be a command is given as one, and a literal to copy is indented under its note.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-09. `bash -n` on `chmod 600 '/home/o'brien/tok'` fails with unexpected EOF. backlog.md:2782 names `C:\Users\O'Brien` as a real case. The back-out lines by reading.
	- Origin: show.go:484 from 76e1cd3, 2026-11-07, the Code Review 20261107 item 6 fix. The accountcmd.go lines from 457a31b4, ca76d60c and 81e2d472, 2026-09-14 and 09-15. The back-out from b34a25c, ef2b917 and a71263d, 2026-09-15 to 10-04. No earlier round saw this. Confirmed for the quoting, Plausible for the back-out.
	- Sweep: every Fix literal built by string concatenation.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Each Fix line pasted the path between 2 single quotes. The accountcmd.go ones already left the command out for a path with an apostrophe, so they gave no command rather than a broken one. show.go's gave the broken one. The back-out took its settle text as one string.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: `shellQuote` in exec.go, which `shellWord` and `typedArg` now share, quotes the 4 paths, so each Fix gives its command whatever the path holds. The back-out takes the settle commands and the rerun command apart, and prints each on its own line under its note. A clean back-out says "Stopped with nothing merged." with a Fix note, in place of the commands after a colon. The dev back-merge, the tag to push, and pr ok's push put the command on its own line. Every branch name and the tag go through `typedArg`.
	- Decisions:
		- Single quotes always for a path, as before, so a plain path prints as it did. An apostrophe comes out as `'\''`. Not `shellWord`'s double quotes, which would re-spell every plain path's line.
		- The release rerun line keeps the version typed, such as `gitsby release v1.0.0`. Without it a rerun picks the next patch version, which may not be what was asked for.
		- Left as they are: the commands after a colon with no value in them, such as "Connect one first: gitsby repo connect <url | owner/name>" and "Cut a patch release when you're ready: gitsby release". They paste as shown, and the placeholders make them templates rather than literals.
		- 2026-11-09: test asserts given new values for this change. [dcmjz], [dcmpq] and [dcnkc]: a path with an apostrophe got a sentence with no command, and now gets the quoted command. [dafrn]: `push it: git push origin tag v1.3.1` is now its own line. [dcnqe]: `git merge dev, then '...br merge'` is now `git merge dev` on its own line.
	- Branch: round-20261109
	- Test case: Go `TestFixLiteralsPaste` [df35x], which reads each Fix command back as sh would, for paths with an apostrophe, a space, `$`, a backtick and a backslash. test.bash [df35r], [df35s], [df35v] and [df35t] for the back-out and pr ok lines, and the updated [dafrn] and [dcnqe].

	- Swept: every Fix or literal line built by concatenation in src-go: the account set lines (account names and hosts are held to plain characters), `leaseDeleteLine`, the abort-failed back-out, the dev back-merge, release.go, and pr.go's 2 push lines. pr.go:552 and the other "first: gitsby ..." lines hold no value.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed. Its new checks fail before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261109-134949

	- ID: 2026110912215208
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Closed
	- Closed reason: Done
	- Target version: v3.0.0-rc.1
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low
	- Opened: 20261109-122152
	- Opened by: jim-collier
	- Related IDs: 2026110708000113
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: style-guide.md:75 says nothing at package level changes after startup. `toolCache` (exec.go:229) and `sshConfigCache` (show.go:575) are package maps filled during the run.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: The code and the public guide agree.
	- Origin: `toolCache` from 26c8a425, 2026-10-21. `sshConfigCache` from c31a204, 2026-11-07, Code Review 20261107 enhancement 2, which chose package level since both callers are plain functions. No earlier round saw the conflict. Confirmed by reading.
	- Against: Code Review 20261107 enhancement 2's choice of a package-level cache.
	- Notes:
		- Either the guide allows a per-process cache keyed on its inputs, or both caches move onto `app`. The first is 1 line in a public doc. The second touches every caller.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Decisions: The guide changes, the code stays. A per-process cache keyed on its inputs, filled lazily and never read as repo state, is allowed at package level. Least churn, since Code Review 20261107 enhancement 2 chose package level 2 days ago, and memoizing at package level is common Go practice. Guarded if any caller runs it from a goroutine.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: style-guide.md's package-level rule now allows a cache of a pure lookup: keyed on all its inputs, filled lazily, guarded by a sync.Mutex, never read as repo state. toolCache and sshConfigCache both fit, and both are already mutex-guarded. Code unchanged.
	- Branch: round-20261109
	- Test case: Not applicable, docs only.
	- Verified: both caches read in exec.go and show.go and found locked.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed. Docs-only edit, per the Decisions row.
	- Closed: 20261109-141557

	- Type: Bug

	- Closed reason: Done
	- Priority [Feature|Enhancement] | Severity [Bug]: Low

	- Opened by: jim-collier

	- Steps to reproduce [Bug]: Build src-go at 958fac2^, on shcl b10c200. Run `account set work name "O'Brien \ x"` with it, then `account list` with the current build.
	- Incorrect behavior [Bug]: The commits line says `O'Brien \\ x`. The file holds `name: "O'Brien \\ x"`, and v3.0.0-beta1 reads a backslash as text in any quote.
	- Expected behavior [Bug]: `O'Brien \ x`, as the old build read it.
	- Reproduced [Bug]: 2026-11-07, by hand. A Windows path with an apostrophe, such as `C:\Users\O'Brien\dev`, is the likely real case.
	- Possible cause [Bug]: The old pin's file says Format 3, like the new one, so nothing tells them apart. Only a double-quoted value holding `\\` is affected. Respelling `\\` to `\` there would fix those files and change a value that meant 2 backslashes. Needs a choice.
	- Decision: 2026-11-07, jim-collier: "I'm the only one using this utility for now. So when converting the file, go by mtime of the shcl file (before doing any writes to it), and use that as the basis for deciding how to interpret."
	- Actual fix [Bug]: A Format 3 file whose time, read before anything writes it, is from before the installed build moved to v3.0.0-beta1 (2026-11-06 19:37 PST) came from the old pin. Its double-quoted values with an escape are read by that pin's rules and written the way v3 spells them. The file as it was is kept as `config_backup_<date>-<time>_format-v3old.shcl`, and the run says so, as the 2.x and flat conversions do. A newer file, or an old one with no such value, is left as it is. The cutover is a constant in cfgformat.go.

	- Test case: Go `[df08m]` an old file is converted, backed up, reported, and left alone on the next read; `[df08n]` the same text with a current time reads as v3 text; `[df08p]` an old file with no escape is not touched, time included; `[df08q]` each escape the old pin read, and the lines it didn't. test.bash `[df08w]`, `[df08x]` and `[df08y]`: the same through the binary, with `touch -d`.
	- Verified: `[df08m]` fails on the previous config.go, and the binary built from it leaves the fixture file alone where `[df08w]` and `[df08x]` want the notice and the backup. go test, test.bash 1870/0 and the quick lint area pass.
	- Swept: the old pin wrote no arrays and quoted with double quotes only where the text had an apostrophe, so a scalar value is the whole case. `\t`, `\n`, `\"`, `\'`, `\u` and `\U` are read with it. A file from the old pin that `account set` already rewrote under v3 has a new time and is not converted; nobody but me had one.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the choice was answered, and its tests passed.
	- Closed: 20261107-122000
